cards.title: Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch
cards.summary: For a projective morphism of smooth varieties, ch(f_! α)·td(T_Y) = f_*(ch(α)·td(T_X)).
cards.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $f : X \to Y$ a projective morphism of smooth quasi-projective varieties over $k$. For every $\alpha \in K_0(X)$, in $A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$:
$$\operatorname{ch}(f_!\,\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_Y) \;=\; f_*\big(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_X)\big).$$

**How it is read in Lean.** $X$ and $Y$ are smooth, separated schemes of finite type over $k$ (every smooth quasi-projective variety is one; integrality and quasi-projectivity are not used). $f$ is projective in the sense that it factors as a closed immersion $X \to \mathbb P^n_Y$ followed by the projection $\mathbb P^n_Y \to Y$. $K_0(X)$ is the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves and $f_!\,[\mathcal F]=\sum_i(-1)^i[R^if_*\mathcal F]$. Both sides are capped with the fundamental class $[Y]$, which identifies $A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ with $CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ for smooth $Y$, and $f_*$ is proper pushforward of cycles. So the statement is
$$f_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_X))\cap[X]\big) \;=\; (\operatorname{ch}(f_!\,\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_Y))\cap[Y]\quad\text{in } CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q},$$
that is, $f_*\,\tau_X(\alpha)=\tau_Y(f_!\,\alpha)$ for the Riemann–Roch map $\tau_X(\alpha)=(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_X))\cap[X]$.

hypotheses.text: $k$ is a field.
$X$ and $Y$ are smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ (in particular: smooth quasi-projective varieties).
$f$ factors as a closed immersion $X \to \mathbb P^n_Y$ followed by the projection to $Y$.

cards.proof: A projective $f$ is proper, so both sides are defined, and $f=\pi\circ i$ with $i:X\to\mathbb P^n_Y$ a closed immersion and $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ the projection; $\mathbb P^n_Y$ is again smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$. The Riemann–Roch formula holds for the closed immersion $i$ (deformation to the normal cone) and for the projection $\pi$ (twisted classes), and it is stable under composition; this is the reduction to closed immersions and projections.
cards.attack: The proof delivers exactly the capped statement in CH_*(Y)⊗ℚ for morphisms factoring through P^n_Y, as the card reads it; nothing is assumed beyond the statement, and no card leads back to the theorem. Numerical checks pass: P^1 → pt with O(d) gives d + 1; P^1 × P^1 → P^1, a double cover P^1 → P^1 and the blow-up of P^2 at a point (49 line bundles). The form in A^*(Y)⊗ℚ needs in addition that capping with [Y] is bijective (Stacks 0FC2), which is cited but not part of the Lean statement. Dropping smoothness makes the statement meaningless (θ is not onto for V(x²) in P^1). Not broken.

leanReading.note: grothendieck_riemann_roch binds only k, IsSmoothFT X and Y, f over k, IsProjectiveMorphism f and α in K'_0(X); unfolding tau and pushforwardK the two sides are f_*((ch(α)·td(T_X)) ∩ [X]) and (ch(f_!α)·td(T_Y)) ∩ [Y] in CH_*(Y)_ℚ. The A^* form would need Poincaré duality, which the Lean statement does not include.

cards.title: The Todd power series
cards.summary: Q(x) = x/(1 − e^{−x}), the generating series of the Bernoulli numbers, with e^{−x} and log Q.

leanReading.note: toddSeries is Mathlib's bernoulli' generating series (B₁ = +1/2), expNeg is exp rescaled by −1, logTodd is log(1+X) substituted at toddSeries − 1; the closed form x/(1−e^{−x}) is a remark proved on another card.

cards.title: $Q(x)\,(1-e^{-x}) = x$
cards.summary: The defining relation of the Todd series.
cards.statement: In $\mathbb Q[[x]]$, the Todd series $Q$ satisfies $Q(x)\cdot(1-e^{-x}) = x$.
cards.proof: The generating series of the Bernoulli numbers $B^+_n$ satisfies $Q\cdot(e^x-1)=x\,e^x$ (Mathlib's `bernoulli'PowerSeries_mul_exp_sub_one`). Multiply by $e^{-x}$ and use $e^x e^{-x}=1$: the left side becomes $Q\cdot(1-e^{-x})$ and the right side $x$.
cards.attack: Computed Q exactly with B⁺_1 = +1/2 and checked Q·(1 − e^{−x}) = x through x⁴⁰; with B_1 = −1/2 the identity fails in degree 2, so the convention matters and is the right one. The proof has no gap; there are no hypotheses to drop.

leanReading.note: Exactly toddSeries * (1 − expNeg) = X in ℚ⟦X⟧.

cards.title: The coefficient of $x^n$ in $e^{dx}Q^{n+1}$ is $\binom{n+d}{n}$
cards.summary: Riemann–Roch on projective space as an identity of power series.
cards.statement: For all natural numbers $n$ and $d$, the coefficient of $x^n$ in $e^{dx}\cdot Q(x)^{n+1}$ is the binomial coefficient $\binom{n+d}{n}$.
cards.proof:
Write $a(n,d)$ for the coefficient. 

*Step 1.* Differentiating $Q\,(1-e^{-x})=x$ and multiplying by $Q$ gives $x\,Q' = Q - e^{-x}Q^2$, hence $x\,(Q^n)' = n\,Q^n - n\,e^{-x}Q^{n+1}$. Taking the coefficient of $x^n$ for $n\ge 1$: the left side has coefficient $n\cdot[x^n]Q^n$, so $n\cdot[x^n]\big(e^{-x}Q^{n+1}\big)=0$ and therefore $[x^n]\big(e^{-x}Q^{n+1}\big)=0$ for $n \ge 1$.

*Step 2.* From $Q\,(1-e^{-x})=x$: $e^{(d+1)x}Q^{n+2}-e^{dx}Q^{n+2} = x\,e^{(d+1)x}Q^{n+1}$; taking the coefficient of $x^{n+1}$ gives $a(n+1,d+1)=a(n+1,d)+a(n,d+1)$. Likewise $Q^{n+2}-e^{-x}Q^{n+2}=x\,Q^{n+1}$; taking the coefficient of $x^{n+1}$ and using Step 1 gives $a(n+1,0)=a(n,0)$.

*Step 3.* $a(0,d)=1$ since $Q$ and $e^{x}$ have constant term $1$. By induction on $n$ and then on $d$, using Pascal's rule $\binom{n+d+2}{n+1}=\binom{n+d+1}{n+1}+\binom{n+d+1}{n}$, $a(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{n}$.
cards.attack: Checked the identity exactly for all 0 ≤ n, d ≤ 8 (81 cases); for negative d the coefficient is (d+1)…(d+n)/n!, as χ(ℙⁿ, O(d)) should be. Steps 1 and 3 are right. Found an index slip in Step 2 of the written proof (the displayed identity needed exponent n+2 to read off a(n+1,·)); the recurrence itself is true, and the proof text has been corrected.

leanReading.note: ∀ n d : ℕ, coeff n (exp ℚ ^ d * toddSeries ^ (n+1)) = (n+d).choose n; (eˣ)^d is e^{dx} and the indices match the card.

cards.title: The coefficient of $x^n$ in $e^{-jx}Q^{n+1}$ vanishes for $1\le j\le n$
cards.summary: The power-series shadow of the vanishing of the cohomology of O(−j) on projective n-space.
cards.statement: For natural numbers $1\le j\le n$, the coefficient of $x^n$ in $e^{-jx}\cdot Q(x)^{n+1}$ is $0$.
cards.proof: Write $b(n,j)$ for the coefficient. The case $j=1$ is Step 1 of the previous card: $[x^n]\big(e^{-x}Q^{n+1}\big)=0$ for $n\ge1$. From $Q\,(1-e^{-x})=x$ one gets $e^{-jx}Q^{n+1} = e^{-(j+1)x}Q^{n+1} + x\,e^{-jx}Q^{n}$, hence $b(n,j+1)=b(n,j)-b(n-1,j)$ for $n\ge1$. By induction on $j$: if $b(m,j)=0$ for all $m\ge j\ge 1$, then for $n\ge j+1$ both $b(n,j)$ and $b(n-1,j)$ vanish, so $b(n,j+1)=0$.
cards.attack: Checked the vanishing for all 1 ≤ j ≤ n ≤ 8. The range is sharp: j = 0 gives 1, j = n+1 gives (−1)ⁿ, j = n+2 gives (−1)ⁿ(n+1), matching χ(ℙⁿ, O(−j)). The recurrence and the induction on j are sound.

leanReading.note: For n j : ℕ with 1 ≤ j and j ≤ n, coeff n (expNeg ^ j * toddSeries ^ (n+1)) = 0, where (e^{−x})^j = e^{−jx}.

cards.title: $Q=\exp(\log Q)$, coefficient by coefficient
cards.summary: The n-th coefficient of Q is that of the truncated exponential of log Q.
cards.statement: For every $n$, the coefficient of $x^n$ in the Todd series $Q$ equals the coefficient of $x^n$ in $\sum_{j=0}^{n}\dfrac{(\log Q)^j}{j!}$.
cards.proof: Mathlib proves $\exp(\log(1+u))=1+u$ as a substitution of power series. Substituting $u=Q-1$ (allowed since $Q-1$ has no constant term) and using that substitution composes gives $\exp(\log Q)=Q$. The coefficient of $x^n$ in the substitution $\exp(\log Q)$ is $\sum_{j\ge0}\frac1{j!}[x^n](\log Q)^j$, and $(\log Q)^j$ is divisible by $x^j$ because $\log Q$ has no constant term, so only $j\le n$ contribute.
cards.attack: Computed log Q = x/2 − x²/24 + x⁴/2880 − … exactly and checked the identity for every n ≤ 24. The cut-off j ≤ n is needed and enough: stopping at j ≤ n−1 misses ℓ_1ⁿ/n! (n = 5 gives −1/3840 instead of Q_5 = 0). The proof is correct.

leanReading.note: ∀ n, coeff n toddSeries = coeff n (∑_{j ∈ range (n+1)} (j!)⁻¹ • logTodd ^ j), exactly the card.

cards.title: Graded-complete rings
cards.summary: Rings whose elements are families of components multiplied by a Cauchy product.

leanReading.note: The structure's fields are the ℚ-modules M n, linear comp n, ofComps with comp_ofComps and ext (item 1), smul_mul/mul_smul (2), mul_congr (3), mul_hom (4), comp_one (5); IsHom n a says all other components vanish.

cards.title: Exponential, power series at an element, Todd operation
cards.summary: exp(x), F(h), degreewise rescaling and Td(c) = exp(Σ n! ℓ_n c_n) in a graded-complete ring.
cards.statement:
Let $R$ be a graded-complete ring.

- For $x\in R$, $\exp(x)$ is the element whose degree-$n$ component is that of $\sum_{j=0}^{n}x^j/j!$ (the usual exponential when $x$ has no degree-$0$ component).
- For a power series $F=\sum_jF_jt^j\in\mathbb Q[[t]]$ and $h\in R$, $F(h)$ is the element whose degree-$n$ component is that of $\sum_{j=0}^{n}F_jh^j$.
- For weights $w:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q$ and $a\in R$, the rescaling $w\cdot a$ is the element with components $w_na_n$.
- The **Todd operation** is $\operatorname{Td}(c)=\exp(w^{\mathrm{td}}\cdot c)$ with $w^{\mathrm{td}}_n=n!\,\ell_n$, where $\ell_n$ is the coefficient of $x^n$ in $\log Q$, $Q$ the Todd series.

leanReading.note: gexp, ev and weight are ofComps of the stated degree-n components (sums over j ≤ n), toddWeight n = n! · coeff n logTodd, and toddOf c = gexp (weight toddWeight c): each bullet is the body.

cards.title: $\exp(x+y)=\exp(x)\exp(y)$ for commuting $x,y$
cards.summary: The exponential in a graded-complete ring turns sums of commuting elements into products.
cards.statement: In a graded-complete ring, let $x$ and $y$ have no degree-$0$ component and commute. Then $\exp(x+y)=\exp(x)\exp(y)$. Moreover $\exp(0)=1$, and for $x$ without degree-$0$ component $\exp(x)$ is a unit.
cards.proof: By axioms 3 and 4 a product of an element vanishing below degree $i$ and one vanishing below degree $j$ vanishes below degree $i+j$ (truncate both factors to degrees $\le n$, expand into homogeneous pieces). Hence $x^j$ vanishes below degree $j$, and the degree-$n$ component of $\exp(x)$ is that of $\sum_{j\le N}x^j/j!$ for every $N\ge n$. For commuting $x,y$ the binomial formula gives $\frac{(x+y)^j}{j!}=\sum_{a+b=j}\frac{x^a}{a!}\frac{y^b}{b!}$. In degree $n$, $\exp(x)\exp(y)$ is computed (axiom 3) from the partial sums $\sum_{a\le n}x^a/a!$ and $\sum_{b\le n}y^b/b!$, whose product is $\sum_{a,b\le n}\frac{x^ay^b}{a!b!}$; the terms with $a+b>n$ vanish in degree $n$, and the rest is $\sum_{j\le n}(x+y)^j/j!$. So both sides have the same components. $\exp(0)=1$ is immediate, and $\exp(x)\exp(-x)=\exp(0)=1=\exp(-x)\exp(x)$.

hypotheses.text: $x$ has no degree-$0$ component.
$y$ has no degree-$0$ component.
$xy=yx$.

cards.attack: Dropped each hypothesis in ℚ[[s]] and M₂(ℚ)[[s]]: without commutation x = E12·s, y = E21·s differ in degree 2; without x0 (x = 1, y = s²) the s²-coefficients are 2 and 1; so all three are needed for the product formula and the proof is right. Finding: for the last claim the hypothesis is not needed, since exp(x) always has degree-0 component 1 and is therefore a unit.

leanReading.note: gexp_add assumes comp 0 x = 0, comp 0 y = 0 and Commute x y and gives gexp (x+y) = gexp x * gexp y; gexp_zero is unconditional and isUnit_gexp assumes comp 0 x = 0, as in the card.

cards.title: $F\mapsto F(h)$ is a ring map
cards.summary: Evaluating power series at an element without constant term is additive, linear and multiplicative.
cards.statement: In a graded-complete ring let $h$ have no degree-$0$ component. Then for power series $F,G\in\mathbb Q[[t]]$ and $q\in\mathbb Q$: $(F+G)(h)=F(h)+G(h)$, $(qF)(h)=q\,F(h)$, $(FG)(h)=F(h)\,G(h)$, $1(h)=1$ and $t(h)=h$.
cards.proof: Additivity and linearity are componentwise. Since $h^j$ vanishes below degree $j$, the degree-$n$ component of $F(h)$ is that of $\sum_{j\le N}F_jh^j$ for any $N\ge n$. In degree $n$ the product $F(h)G(h)$ is computed from the partial sums up to $n$, whose product is $\sum_{a,b\le n}F_aG_bh^{a+b}$; terms with $a+b>n$ vanish in degree $n$ and the rest is $\sum_{j\le n}(FG)_jh^j$ by the Cauchy product of coefficients. The values on $1$ and $t$ are read off from the definition.

hypotheses.text: $h$ has no degree-$0$ component (needed for multiplicativity and for $t(h)=h$; additivity, linearity and $1(h)=1$ hold for every $h$).

cards.attack: Without h0 multiplicativity fails (h = 1 + s + s², F = G = t: s²-coefficients 3 and 1) and t(h) = h fails (h = 1 + s gives s), while 1(h) = 1 holds for every h. The hypothesis note used to say h0 was needed for 1(h) = 1; it has been corrected.

leanReading.note: ev_mul, ev_one and ev_X assume comp 0 h = 0; ev_add and ev_smul hold for every h, which is more general than the card.

cards.title: Commutation of components from commutation of scalings
cards.summary: If all 2^{in}-rescalings of c commute with c', every rescaling of c commutes with every rescaling of c'.
cards.statement: In a graded-complete ring let $c,c'$ be elements such that for every $i\ge0$ the rescaling $(2^{in}c_n)_n$ of $c$ commutes with $c'$. Then for all weights $w,w':\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q$ the rescalings $w\cdot c$ and $w'\cdot c'$ commute.
cards.proof: Fix a degree $m$. Write $c^{(p)}$ for the homogeneous piece of $c$ of degree $p$ (the element with the single component $c_p$) and put $v_p=\big(c^{(p)}c'^{(m-p)}-c'^{(m-p)}c^{(p)}\big)_m\in M_m$ for $0\le p\le m$. The degree-$m$ component of a product is the sum over $p$ of the degree-$m$ components of the products of pieces of degrees $p$ and $m-p$. So the hypothesis for $i$ says $\sum_{p=0}^m 2^{ip}v_p=0$. For $i=0,\dots,m$ this is a linear system with the Vandermonde matrix of the distinct nodes $2^0,\dots,2^m$, which is invertible over $\mathbb Q$; hence all $v_p=0$. The degree-$m$ components of $(w\cdot c)(w'\cdot c')$ and of $(w'\cdot c')(w\cdot c)$ differ by $\sum_p w_pw'_{m-p}v_p=0$.
cards.attack: In M₂(ℚ)[[s]], c = c' = E11·s + E12·s² commute (the hypothesis for i = 0 only), yet the rescalings (n+1)c_n and c do not, and the hypothesis indeed fails at i = 1: 'for every i' cannot be weakened. A positive instance with pairwise commuting pieces satisfied the conclusion for arbitrary weights.

leanReading.note: Hypothesis ∀ i : ℕ, Commute (weight (n ↦ 2^(i·n)) c) c'; conclusion ∀ w w', Commute (weight w c) (weight w' c'). Matches the card.

cards.title: $\exp(L(h))=T(h)$ when $T=\exp L$
cards.summary: The exponential is compatible with evaluation of power series.
cards.statement: In a graded-complete ring let $h$ have no degree-$0$ component. Let $L,T\in\mathbb Q[[t]]$ with $L(0)=0$ and such that for every $n$ the coefficient of $t^n$ in $T$ equals the coefficient of $t^n$ in $\sum_{j=0}^n L^j/j!$. Then $\exp(L(h))=T(h)$.
cards.proof: Since evaluation is a ring map, $L(h)^j=(L^j)(h)$, so the degree-$n$ component of $\exp(L(h))$ is that of $\big(\sum_{j\le n}L^j/j!\big)(h)$. The component of degree $n$ of $F(h)$ only involves the coefficients $F_i$, $i\le n$, and for $i\le n$ the coefficient of $t^i$ in $\sum_{j\le n}L^j/j!$ equals that in $\sum_{j\le i}L^j/j!$ (as $L^j$ is divisible by $t^j$), which is $T_i$ by hypothesis.
cards.attack: Dropped L(0) = 0: L = 1 + t forces T = eᵗ, and at h = s + s² the s²-coefficients are 5/2 and 3/2. Dropped h0: L = t, T = eᵗ, h = 1 + s + s² gives 3/2 against 5/2. With both hypotheses, L = log Q, T = Q gives equality for h = s + s² and for a non-commuting h.

leanReading.note: Assumes comp 0 h = 0, constantCoeff L = 0, and coeff n T = coeff n (∑_{j≤n} (j!)⁻¹ • L^j) for all n; concludes gexp (ev h L) = ev h T.

cards.title: The Todd operation turns sums into products
cards.summary: Td(c+c') = Td(c)Td(c') when the rescalings commute; Td(c) is a unit.
cards.statement: In a graded-complete ring: if the rescalings $w^{\mathrm{td}}\cdot c$ and $w^{\mathrm{td}}\cdot c'$ commute, then $\operatorname{Td}(c+c')=\operatorname{Td}(c)\operatorname{Td}(c')$. Moreover $\operatorname{Td}(0)=1$, $\operatorname{Td}(c)\operatorname{Td}(-c)=1$, and $\operatorname{Td}(c)$ is a unit.
cards.proof: $w^{\mathrm{td}}_0=0$ because $\log Q$ has no constant term, so $w^{\mathrm{td}}\cdot c$ has no degree-$0$ component, and rescaling is additive. Apply $\exp(x+y)=\exp(x)\exp(y)$ to $x=w^{\mathrm{td}}\cdot c$, $y=w^{\mathrm{td}}\cdot c'$. For the inverse take $c'=-c$: then $y=w^{\mathrm{td}}\cdot(-c)=-x$ commutes with $x$, and $\operatorname{Td}(c)\operatorname{Td}(-c)=\operatorname{Td}(0)=1$, likewise in the other order.
cards.attack: Non-commuting c = E12·s, c' = E21·s in M₂(ℚ)[[s]] give Td(c + c') ≠ Td(c)Td(c'), so the hypothesis is needed; Td(c)Td(−c) = 1 was confirmed for a c with non-commuting pieces. The proof's wording for the inverse (which rescalings commute) was imprecise and has been corrected.

leanReading.note: toddOf_add assumes Commute (weight toddWeight c) (weight toddWeight c'); toddOf_zero, toddOf_mul_toddOf_neg and isUnit_toddOf have no hypotheses, as in the card.

cards.title: $\operatorname{Td}(e^{h})=Q(h)$ in degree one
cards.summary: On the exponential of a homogeneous element of degree one, the Todd operation is the Todd series.
cards.statement: In a graded-complete ring let $h$ be homogeneous of degree one. Then $\operatorname{Td}(e^h)=Q(h)$, where $e^h$ is the value at $h$ of the exponential series and $Q(h)$ the value of the Todd series.
cards.proof: For $h$ homogeneous of degree one, $h^n$ is homogeneous of degree $n$, so the degree-$n$ component of $F(h)$ is $F_n\,(h^n)_n$. Hence $w^{\mathrm{td}}\cdot e^h$ has components $n!\,\ell_n\cdot\frac1{n!}(h^n)_n=\ell_n(h^n)_n$: it is $(\log Q)(h)$. By the previous card with $L=\log Q$, $T=Q$ and the identity $Q=\exp(\log Q)$ coefficient by coefficient, $\exp((\log Q)(h))=Q(h)$.
cards.attack: Checked Td(e^h) = Q(h) for h = s, 3s in ℚ[[s]] and h = E12·s in M₂(ℚ)[[s]]. The hypothesis is sharp: the identity fails for h = s + s² (not homogeneous) and for h = s² (homogeneous of degree 2).

leanReading.note: IsHom 1 h → toddOf (ev h (exp ℚ)) = ev h toddSeries, i.e. Td(e^h) = Q(h) for h homogeneous of degree one.

cards.title: $Q(h)\,(1-e^{-h})=h$
cards.summary: The rank-one Koszul identity in a graded-complete ring.
cards.statement: In a graded-complete ring let $h$ have no degree-$0$ component. Then $Q(h)\cdot\big(1-e^{-h}\big)=h$, where $e^{-h}$ is the value at $h$ of the series $e^{-x}$.
cards.proof: Apply the ring map $F\mapsto F(h)$ to the identity $Q\,(1-e^{-x})=x$ of power series.
cards.attack: Checked the identity for h = s + 3s² − s⁵ in ℚ[[s]] and for a non-commuting h. Without h0 it fails: h = 1 gives 0 ≠ 1, h = 2 + s gives s ≠ 2 + s. The proof (apply the ring map F ↦ F(h) to Q(1 − e^{−x}) = x) is correct.

leanReading.note: comp 0 h = 0 → ev h toddSeries * (1 − ev h expNeg) = h.

cards.title: Rational Chow groups, Chow cohomology, cap product, $[X]$
cards.summary: CH_*(X)⊗ℚ, A^*(X)⊗ℚ = ∏_p A^p(X)⊗ℚ, its action by cap product, and the fundamental class.
cards.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a scheme with a morphism $s_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally of finite type. Chow homology is that of Stacks (chapter 42) over the base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with dimension function $0$.

- $CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q\otimes CH_j(X)$, where $CH_j(X)$ is the group of $j$-cycles modulo rational equivalence.
- $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}=\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)\otimes\mathbb Q$ is the ring of rational Chow cohomology classes of Stacks (bivariant classes for the identity of $X$), with the Cauchy product.
- The **cap product**: $c\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ acts on $CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ by the total cap operation $\gamma\mapsto c\cap\gamma=\sum_pc_p\cap\gamma$ of Stacks.
- For $X$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, $[X]\in CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is the image of the fundamental class of $X$.

leanReading.note: CHQ = ⨁_j ℚ ⊗ chowGroup over Spec k with δ ≡ 0, AQ is Stacks' RationalTotalChowClass, cap is totalRationalChowCap (summing c_p ∩ for p ≤ k − inf δ, the full sum over a field since δ ≥ 0), fundamentalClass is rationalFundamentalClass.

cards.title: Smooth, separated, of finite type over $k$
cards.summary: How “smooth quasi-projective variety” is read in Lean: smooth, separated and quasi-compact over Spec k.
cards.statement: Let $k$ be a field. A scheme $X$ with structure morphism $s_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is **smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$** when $s_X$ is smooth, separated and quasi-compact. (A smooth morphism is locally of finite type, so $X$ is then of finite type over $k$.) This is the class of schemes for which the theorem is stated in Lean; every smooth quasi-projective variety over $k$ belongs to it, and neither integrality nor quasi-projectivity is required.

leanReading.note: IsSmoothFT has exactly the fields Smooth sX (Mathlib's), IsSeparated sX and QuasiCompact sX. The remark about smooth quasi-projective varieties is not part of the definition.

cards.title: Smooth varieties are smooth, separated, of finite type
cards.summary: A smooth variety in the sense of Stacks satisfies the Lean hypothesis.
cards.statement: Let $s_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a smooth variety over $k$ in the sense of Stacks: $X$ is integral and $s_X$ is separated, locally of finite type, quasi-compact and smooth. Then $X$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.
cards.proof: The three conditions (smooth, separated, quasi-compact) are among the defining conditions of a smooth variety.
cards.attack: The conclusion only forgets integrality (and 'locally of finite type', implied by smooth): the three conditions are among the defining conditions listed. Nothing to break; integrality is genuinely unused.

leanReading.note: IsSmoothVariety k sX extends IsVariety (IsIntegral X, IsSeparated, LocallyOfFiniteType, QuasiCompact) and Smooth sX, exactly the card's hypothesis; the conclusion is IsSmoothFT k sX.

cards.title: $K_0(X)$, $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$ and their identification
cards.summary: Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves, Grothendieck ring of vector bundles, and θ_X between them.
cards.statement:
- $K_0(X)$ is the Grothendieck group of the abelian category of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules (called $K'_0(X)$ in Stacks), with classes $[\mathcal F]$.
- $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$ is the Grothendieck ring of finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules (Stacks 0FDK), with classes $[\mathcal E]$ and product the tensor product.
- For $X$ smooth, separated and of finite type over a field $k$ (hence regular, quasi-compact, with affine diagonal), $\theta_X:K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)\to K_0(X)$ is the isomorphism of groups of Stacks for regular schemes (Stacks 0FDJ and 0FDI).

leanReading.note: CoherentKZero is KZero of the abelian category of coherent modules; VectorBundleKZero is the free group on all modules modulo non-locally-free generators and short exact sequences of locally free ones (isomorphic to K₀(Vect)); vectorBundleEquiv is Stacks' regularVectorBundleKZeroAddEquiv.

cards.title: $\theta_X[\mathcal E]=[\mathcal E]$
cards.summary: The identification K_0(Vect X) ≅ K_0(X) sends a vector bundle to its class as a coherent sheaf.
cards.statement: Let $X$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $\mathcal E$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module. Then $\mathcal E$ is coherent and $\theta_X([\mathcal E])=[\mathcal E]$ in $K_0(X)$.
cards.proof: This is the description of Stacks' isomorphism on classes of finite locally free modules (`regularVectorBundleKZeroAddEquiv_classOf'`), applied with the regularity of $X$ (smooth over a field).
cards.attack: On the Noetherian scheme X a finite locally free module is coherent, and θ_X is by construction the map sending [E] to [E]; smoothness is used only so that θ_X exists. Consistent on Spec k, where θ is the identity of ℤ. No gap.

leanReading.note: For E finite locally free, ∃ hcoh : IsCoherent E with vectorBundleEquiv (classOf E) = KZero.mk ⟨E, hcoh⟩.

cards.title: The Chern character
cards.summary: ch on K_0(Vect X) is Stacks' ring map; on K_0(X) it is ch ∘ θ_X^{-1}.
cards.statement:
- On vector bundles, $\operatorname{ch}:K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)\to A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is the ring homomorphism of Stacks 0FEM, with $\operatorname{ch}_p(\mathcal E)=P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$, $P_p$ the $p$-th power sum of the Chern roots.
- On coherent sheaves, for $X$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, $\operatorname{ch}:K_0(X)\to A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is the additive map $\operatorname{ch}\circ\theta_X^{-1}$.

leanReading.note: ch C sX is Stacks' rationalTotalChernCharacterRingHom, whose p-th component is (p!)⁻¹ ⊗ P_p by the library definition; chK is its composite with the inverse of vectorBundleEquiv.

cards.title: The Todd class
cards.summary: A^*(X)⊗ℚ is graded-complete, and td(a) = Td(ch(a)) = exp(Σ p! ℓ_p ch_p(a)).
cards.statement:
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology.

- The ring $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}=\prod_pA^p(X)\otimes\mathbb Q$, with components $c\mapsto c_p$, is a graded-complete ring.
- The **Todd class** of $a\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$ is $\operatorname{td}(a)=\operatorname{Td}(\operatorname{ch}(a))=\exp\big(\sum_{p\ge1}p!\,\ell_p\operatorname{ch}_p(a)\big)\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, where $\log\frac{x}{1-e^{-x}}=\sum_p\ell_px^p$. For a vector bundle with Chern roots $x_i$ this is $\prod_i\frac{x_i}{1-e^{-x_i}}$.

leanReading.note: chowGraded has M n = ℚ ⊗ A^n(X), comp n a = a n and ofComps = id; toddClass a = toddOf (ch a), and the p = 0 term drops because toddWeight 0 = 0. The Chern-root product is a remark not stated in Lean.

cards.title: Components of Chern characters commute
cards.summary: Rescalings of ch(a) and ch(b) commute in A^*(X)⊗ℚ, though the ring is not known to be commutative.
cards.statement: For $a,b\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$ and weights $w,w':\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q$, the elements $(w_p\operatorname{ch}_p(a))_p$ and $(w'_p\operatorname{ch}_p(b))_p$ of $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ commute.
cards.proof: The second Adams operation $\psi^2$ on $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$ satisfies $\operatorname{ch}_p(\psi^2a)=2^p\operatorname{ch}_p(a)$ (Stacks 0FEN, `chernCharacterVectorBundle_secondAdams`). So the rescaling of $\operatorname{ch}(a)$ by $2^{ip}$ is $\operatorname{ch}((\psi^2)^ia)$, which commutes with $\operatorname{ch}(b)$ because $\operatorname{ch}$ is a ring map out of the commutative ring $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$. Conclude by the card on commutation from scalings.
cards.attack: Proof checked step by step: iterating ch_p(ψ²a) = 2ᵖch_p(a) shows the 2^{ip}-rescaling of ch(a) is ch((ψ²)ⁱa), which commutes with ch(b) because ch is a ring map out of a commutative ring; the scaling lemma then gives all weights. No step fails.

leanReading.note: ∀ C sX w w' a b, Commute (weight w (ch a)) (weight w' (ch b)), over any Chow situation.

cards.title: The Todd class is multiplicative
cards.summary: td(a+b) = td(a)·td(b); on short exact sequences td(E) = td(E')·td(E'').
cards.statement: For $a,b\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$: $\operatorname{td}(a+b)=\operatorname{td}(a)\operatorname{td}(b)$ and $\operatorname{td}(0)=1$. Consequently, for a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E''\to0$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $\mathcal E'$, $\mathcal E''$ finite locally free, $\operatorname{td}([\mathcal E])=\operatorname{td}([\mathcal E'])\cdot\operatorname{td}([\mathcal E''])$.
cards.proof: $\operatorname{ch}$ is additive, and the rescalings of $\operatorname{ch}(a)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(b)$ commute, so the Todd operation turns the sum $\operatorname{ch}(a)+\operatorname{ch}(b)$ into the product. For a short exact sequence, $[\mathcal E]=[\mathcal E']+[\mathcal E'']$ in $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$.
cards.attack: Checked the Todd operation with Chern roots in ℚ[x1, x2] graded by total degree: Td(e^{x1} + e^{x2}) = Q(x1)Q(x2), Td(e^{x1} + e^{x2} + e^{x1+x2}) = Q(x1)Q(x2)Q(x1+x2), Td(e^{x1} − e^{x2})·Q(x2) = Q(x1), exact through degree 7. In the short-exact-sequence clause the local freeness of the middle term is left implicit but automatic.

leanReading.note: toddClass_add (∀ a b) and toddClass_zero; for S short exact in X.Modules with S.X₁ and S.X₃ finite locally free, td[S.X₂] = td[S.X₁] · td[S.X₃], exactly the card's hypotheses.

cards.title: Todd classes are units and commute with Chern characters
cards.summary: td(a)·td(−a) = 1, and td(a) commutes with every ch(b) and td(b).
cards.statement: For $a,b\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$: $\operatorname{td}(a)\operatorname{td}(-a)=1$, so $\operatorname{td}(a)$ is a unit of $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$; and $\operatorname{td}(a)$ commutes with $\operatorname{ch}(b)$ and with $\operatorname{td}(b)$.
cards.proof: The first statement is multiplicativity applied to $a+(-a)=0$. For the second: $\exp(x)$ is, in each degree, a polynomial in $x$, so it commutes with whatever commutes with $x$; apply this to $x=w^{\mathrm{td}}\cdot\operatorname{ch}(a)$, which commutes with $\operatorname{ch}(b)$ and with $w^{\mathrm{td}}\cdot\operatorname{ch}(b)$ by the previous card.
cards.attack: Checked in M₂(ℚ)[[s]]: when x (no degree-0 part) commutes with y, exp(x) commutes with y and with exp of its positive-degree part, and Td(c) commutes with c' and Td(c') for commuting families. The proof is correct; for td(a) with td(b) the commutation argument is applied twice, which the text compresses.

leanReading.note: td(a) · td(−a) = 1, IsUnit (td a), Commute (td a) (ch b) and Commute (td a) (td b), all for arbitrary a b.

cards.title: The first Chern class in $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$
cards.summary: c_1(L) of an invertible module, as an element of degree one.
cards.statement: For an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, $c_1(\mathcal L)\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is the image under $\prod_pA^p(X)\to\prod_pA^p(X)\otimes\mathbb Q$ of the total class of Stacks which is the first Chern class $c_1(\mathcal L)\in A^1(X)$ in degree one and zero in the other degrees.

leanReading.note: firstChernQ L = ofTotalChowClass (firstChernTotal L); firstChernTotal is c₁(L) ∈ A¹(X) in degree 1 and 0 elsewhere, and ofTotalChowClass is c ↦ (1 ⊗ c_p)_p.

cards.title: $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal L)=e^{c_1(\mathcal L)}$
cards.summary: The Chern character of a line bundle is the exponential of its first Chern class.
cards.statement: For an invertible module $\mathcal L$ on $X$: $c_1(\mathcal L)$ is homogeneous of degree one in $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, and $\operatorname{ch}([\mathcal L])$ is the value at $c_1(\mathcal L)$ of the exponential series, $\operatorname{ch}([\mathcal L])=e^{c_1(\mathcal L)}$.
cards.proof: For a module of rank one the power sums are $P_p(\mathcal L)=c_1(\mathcal L)^p$ (Stacks: `powerSumTotal_of_rank_one`), so $\operatorname{ch}_p(\mathcal L)=c_1(\mathcal L)^p/p!$. On the other side, $c_1(\mathcal L)$ being homogeneous of degree one, the degree-$p$ component of $e^{c_1(\mathcal L)}$ is $\frac1{p!}$ times that of $c_1(\mathcal L)^p$.
cards.attack: For rank one P_p(L) = c₁(L)ᵖ, so ch_p(L) = c₁ᵖ/p!; since c₁ is homogeneous of degree one the degree-p component of e^{c₁} is the same. Sanity check on ℙ¹: ch(O(d)) = 1 + d·pt, and with td(T) = 1 + pt this gives χ = d + 1. No gap.

leanReading.note: For invertible L: IsHom 1 (firstChernQ L), and ch (classOf L) = ev (firstChernQ L) (exp ℚ).

cards.title: $\operatorname{td}(\mathcal L)=\dfrac{c_1(\mathcal L)}{1-e^{-c_1(\mathcal L)}}$
cards.summary: The Todd class of a line bundle is the Todd series at its first Chern class.
cards.statement: For an invertible module $\mathcal L$ on $X$: $\operatorname{td}([\mathcal L])=Q(c_1(\mathcal L))$, the value of the Todd series $Q(x)=x/(1-e^{-x})$ at $c_1(\mathcal L)$.
cards.proof: $\operatorname{td}([\mathcal L])=\operatorname{Td}(\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal L])=\operatorname{Td}(e^{c_1(\mathcal L)})=Q(c_1(\mathcal L))$, by the two previous cards on line bundles and on the Todd operation in degree one.
cards.attack: Composite of the two previous facts; checked td(T_ℙ¹) = Q(2P) = 1 + P = Q(P)² mod P², and that the convention x/(1 − e^{−x}) is the right one: using Ω instead of T, or x/(eˣ − 1), gives χ(O_ℙ¹) = −1. No gap.

leanReading.note: For invertible L, toddClass (classOf L) = ev (firstChernQ L) toddSeries, i.e. td[L] = Q(c₁(L)).

cards.title: Pullback of Chow cohomology classes; graded maps
cards.summary: f^* on A^*⊗ℚ, degree by degree the restriction of bivariant classes; graded ring maps.
cards.statement:
- A ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to R'$ between graded-complete rings is **graded** if for every $n$ there is a $\mathbb Q$-linear map $\psi_n:M_n\to M'_n$ with $\varphi(a)_n=\psi_n(a_n)$ for all $a$.
- For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology, the **pullback** $f^*:A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\to A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is the ring homomorphism which in each degree $p$ is the restriction of bivariant classes $A^p(Y)\to A^p(X)$ of Stacks, tensored with $\mathbb Q$.

leanReading.note: IsGradedHom φ says ∀ n, ∃ ψ : M n →ₗ[ℚ] M' n, ∀ a, comp n (φ a) = ψ (comp n a); pullbackAQ is a ring map whose degree-p part is the ℚ-base change of Stacks' restriction A^p(Y) → A^p(X) (0B7F).

cards.title: Graded maps commute with $\exp$, evaluation and $\operatorname{Td}$
cards.summary: φ(exp x) = exp(φx), φ(F(h)) = F(φh), φ(Td c) = Td(φc).
cards.statement: Let $\varphi:R\to R'$ be a graded ring homomorphism between graded-complete rings. Then for $x,h,a,c\in R$, weights $w$ and $F\in\mathbb Q[[t]]$: $\varphi(\exp x)=\exp(\varphi x)$, $\varphi(w\cdot a)=w\cdot\varphi(a)$, $\varphi(F(h))=F(\varphi h)$ and $\varphi(\operatorname{Td}(c))=\operatorname{Td}(\varphi c)$.
cards.proof: Compare components in each degree $n$: $\varphi(a)_n=\psi_n(a_n)$ with $\psi_n$ linear, so $\varphi$ is $\mathbb Q$-linear, and being a ring map it sends $\sum_{j\le n}q_jx^j$ to $\sum_{j\le n}q_j\varphi(x)^j$. The degree-$n$ components of $\exp$, of a rescaling and of $F(h)$ are defined through such finite sums. The Todd operation is the composite of a rescaling and $\exp$.
cards.attack: With the graded endomorphism x1 ↦ 2x1, x2 ↦ 3x1 − x2 of ℚ[x1, x2], φ commutes with exp and Td even on an element with a degree-0 part; the ring map x1 ↦ x1 + x1², which is not graded, does not commute with Td, so 'graded' is necessary.

leanReading.note: Under IsGradedHom G G' φ and no other hypothesis: φ (gexp x) = gexp (φ x), φ (weight w a) = weight w (φ a), φ (ev h F) = ev (φ h) F, φ (toddOf c) = toddOf (φ c).

cards.title: $f^*\operatorname{ch}(a)=\operatorname{ch}(f^*a)$ and $f^*\operatorname{td}(a)=\operatorname{td}(f^*a)$
cards.summary: Chern character and Todd class commute with pullback.
cards.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over the base. The pullback $f^*:A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\to A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is a graded ring homomorphism whose degree-$p$ component is the rational restriction of bivariant classes, and for every $a\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$: $f^*\operatorname{ch}(a)=\operatorname{ch}(f^*a)$ and $f^*\operatorname{td}(a)=\operatorname{td}(f^*a)$, where $f^*a\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$ is the pullback of vector bundle classes.
cards.proof: That $f^*$ is a ring map is checked on lifts to $\mathbb Q\otimes\prod_pA^p$, where it is induced by the integral restriction ring map of Stacks. It is graded by construction. Compatibility with $\operatorname{ch}$ holds in each degree (Stacks: `rationalChowCohomologyRestriction_chernCharacterVectorBundle`). Since $\operatorname{td}=\operatorname{Td}\circ\operatorname{ch}$ and graded maps commute with $\operatorname{Td}$, the Todd class follows.
cards.attack: Checked the logic: f* is degreewise restriction (graded by construction), multiplicative because induced on lifts by the integral restriction ring map, compatible with ch by the cited Stacks lemma, and td = Td∘ch then follows from the card on graded maps. No gap.

leanReading.note: pullbackAQ is a RingHom whose p-th component is the ℚ-base change of the Stacks restriction (pullbackAQ_apply), it is graded, and it sends ch a to ch (pullback f a) and td a to td (pullback f a); stated over any Chow base.

cards.title: Projection formula for the cap product
cards.summary: f_*(f^*c ∩ γ) = c ∩ f_*γ on rational Chow groups.
cards.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology, and suppose the dimension function $\delta$ is bounded below on $X$ and on $Y$. Then for $c\in A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ and $\gamma\in CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$: $f_*\big(f^*c\cap\gamma\big)=c\cap f_*\gamma$ in $CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$.
cards.proof: It suffices to take $\gamma$ in a single degree $j$. Because $\delta$ is bounded below, the total cap of $c$ on a class of degree $j$ is a finite sum of the caps with the components $c_p$, with one finite index set serving both $X$ and $Y$. For each component the formula is the projection formula for bivariant classes, part of their definition (Stacks: `rationalProperChowPushforward_comp_rationalChowCap`).

hypotheses.text: $f$ is proper.
$\delta$ is bounded below on $X$ and on $Y$ (automatic over a field, where $\delta\ge0$).

cards.attack: Checked the reduction to a class of one degree j: if δ ≥ lo on X and Y then c_p ∩ (degree-j class) lies in CH_{j−p} = 0 for p > j − lo on either side, so one finite index set serves both, and each component is the bivariant compatibility with proper pushforward. Properness and boundedness are both used.

leanReading.note: For any Chow situation, f proper over the base and BddBelow of the relative dimension on X and on Y (the card's two hypotheses): f_*(cap(f^*c) γ) = cap(c)(f_* γ) with the same total cap operation.

cards.title: Proper pushforward on rational Chow groups
cards.summary: f_* : CH_*(X)⊗ℚ → CH_*(Y)⊗ℚ for proper f.
cards.statement: For a proper morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes locally of finite type over the base, $f_*:CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}\to CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ is, in each degree, the proper pushforward of cycles of Stacks 02R5 (which passes to rational equivalence classes, Stacks 02S2), tensored with $\mathbb Q$.

leanReading.note: The body applies, in each degree k, Stacks' properChowPushforward (the pushforward of k-cycles weighted by residue degrees, descended to rational equivalence classes) base-changed to ℚ.

cards.title: The pushforward $f_!$ on $K_0$
cards.summary: f_![F] = Σ (−1)^i [R^i f_* F] for proper f.
cards.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism with $Y$ locally Noetherian and quasi-compact.

- $R^if_*\mathcal F$ is the value on $\mathcal F$ of the $i$-th right derived functor of $f_*$ on $\mathcal O_X$-modules; for coherent $\mathcal F$ it is coherent (Stacks 02O5).
- $N_f$ is a natural number such that $R^if_*\mathcal F=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ and every $i\ge N_f$ (it exists by Stacks 01XJ).
- $f_!:K_0(X)\to K_0(Y)$ is the group homomorphism with $f_![\mathcal F]=\sum_{i<N_f}(-1)^i[R^if_*\mathcal F]$ for every coherent $\mathcal F$.

leanReading.note: higherDirectImage is rightDerivedPlus i of the pushforward functor; higherDirectImageCoh is that object with its coherence; cohomologicalBound is chosen with the stated vanishing; pushforwardK is KZero.lift of the alternating sum over i < N_f.

cards.title: $f_!$ is well defined
cards.summary: The alternating sum of higher direct images is additive on short exact sequences, and any vanishing bound may be used.
cards.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper with $Y$ locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. The assignment $\mathcal F\mapsto\sum_{i<N_f}(-1)^i[R^if_*\mathcal F]$ is additive on short exact sequences of coherent modules, so it defines the homomorphism $f_!:K_0(X)\to K_0(Y)$; and for every coherent $\mathcal F$ and every $N$ such that $R^if_*\mathcal F=0$ for $i\ge N$, $f_![\mathcal F]=\sum_{i<N}(-1)^i[R^if_*\mathcal F]$.
cards.proof: A short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ of coherent modules is short exact as modules, and the higher direct images form a $\delta$-functor: there is a long exact sequence $0\to f_*\mathcal F'\to f_*\mathcal F\to f_*\mathcal F''\to R^1f_*\mathcal F'\to\cdots$ of coherent modules which is zero from index $N_f$ on. In a Grothendieck group the alternating sum of the classes of an exact sequence that starts with a monomorphism and ends in zeros vanishes (split it into short exact sequences through the images), which is the additivity. Two bounds give the same sum because the extra terms are classes of zero objects.
cards.attack: Checked the argument (long exact sequence of R^i f_* starting with a monomorphism, zero from N_f on, split through images; independence of the bound since extra terms are zero). Example ℙ¹ → Spec k: f_![O(d)] = (d+1)[k] is additive on 0 → O(−1) → O² → O(1) → 0. Correct.

leanReading.note: All three declarations assume exactly f proper, Y locally Noetherian and compact: additivity of F ↦ ∑_{i<N_f} (−1)^i [R^i f_* F] on short exact sequences of coherent modules, the formula with the uniform bound, and the formula with any vanishing bound.

cards.title: $i_![\mathcal F]=[i_*\mathcal F]$ for a closed immersion
cards.summary: For a closed immersion the pushforward on K_0 is the direct image.
cards.statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion with $X$ locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module. Then $i_![\mathcal F]=[i_*\mathcal F]$ in $K_0(X)$.
cards.proof: A closed immersion is finite, so $R^qi_*\mathcal F=0$ for $q>0$ (Stacks: `isZero_higherDirectImage_of_isFinite`) and $R^0i_*\mathcal F\cong i_*\mathcal F$. Use the formula for $f_!$ with the bound $N=1$.
cards.attack: A closed immersion is finite, so R^q i_*F = 0 for q > 0 and R⁰i_*F ≅ i_*F; the formula with N = 1 applies. Example: p ∈ ℙ¹ gives i_![k] = [O_p] = [O] − [O(−1)]. No gap.

leanReading.note: For a closed immersion i with X locally Noetherian and compact and F coherent on Z, pushforwardK i (mk F) = mk (pushforwardCoherentModules i F), the direct image as a coherent module.

cards.title: $(g\circ i)_!=g_!\circ i_!$ for a closed immersion $i$
cards.summary: Functoriality of f_! for a closed immersion followed by a proper morphism.
cards.statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion and $g:X\to Y$ a proper morphism, with $X$ and $Y$ locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Then $(g\circ i)_!=g_!\circ i_!$ as homomorphisms $K_0(Z)\to K_0(Y)$.
cards.proof: It suffices to check on classes $[\mathcal F]$. For a closed immersion $i$ there are isomorphisms $R^n(g\circ i)_*\mathcal F\cong R^ng_*(i_*\mathcal F)$ (Stacks: `ClosedImmersionRelativeLeray.rightDerivedPushforwardCompIso`). With a common vanishing bound, $(g\circ i)_![\mathcal F]=\sum(-1)^n[R^ng_*(i_*\mathcal F)]=g_![i_*\mathcal F]=g_!(i_![\mathcal F])$.
cards.attack: R^n(g∘i)_*F ≅ R^n g_*(i_*F) holds since i_* is exact and sends injectives to g_*-acyclic sheaves; with a common bound the sums agree. Check: p ∈ ℙ¹ → Spec k gives [k] on both sides. Correct; the restriction to closed immersions is a library choice, not a mathematical need.

leanReading.note: pushforwardK (i ≫ g) = (pushforwardK g).comp (pushforwardK i) for a closed immersion i and proper g with X and Y locally Noetherian and compact; i ≫ g is g ∘ i.

cards.title: $T_X$ and $\operatorname{td}(T_X)$
cards.summary: The tangent sheaf is the dual of Ω_{X/k}; td(T_X) is the Todd class of its class.
cards.statement: For $X$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$: the tangent sheaf $T_X$ is the dual $\mathcal Hom(\Omega_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)$ of the sheaf of differentials; $[T_X]\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$ is its class; and $\operatorname{td}(T_X)=\operatorname{td}([T_X])\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$.

leanReading.note: tangentSheaf is the dual (internal Hom into O_X) of relativeDifferentials sX, tangentClass its classOf, toddTangent the toddClass of that. Caveat: classOf is 0 on modules that are not finite locally free, so this is the true class because T_X is locally free in the smooth case.

cards.title: The Riemann–Roch map $\tau_X$
cards.summary: τ_X(α) = (ch(α)·td(T_X)) ∩ [X].
cards.statement: For $X$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, $\tau_X:K_0(X)\to CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is the additive map $\tau_X(\alpha)=\big(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_X)\big)\cap[X]$.

leanReading.note: tau is an additive map K'₀(X) →+ CH_*(X)⊗ℚ with tau α = cap (chK α * toddTangent) (fundamentalClass), the factors in the card's order.

cards.title: The Riemann–Roch formula for a morphism
cards.summary: f_* τ_X(α) = τ_Y(f_! α) for all α.
cards.statement: Let $X$, $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism over $k$. **The Riemann–Roch formula holds for $f$** if for every $\alpha\in K_0(X)$: $f_*\,\tau_X(\alpha)=\tau_Y(f_!\,\alpha)$ in $CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$.

leanReading.note: RiemannRochFor k sX sY f hf := ∀ α, rationalProperChowPushforward … hf (tau k sX α) = tau k sY (pushforwardK f α), with IsSmoothFT on X and Y, f proper and f ≫ sY = sX.

cards.title: Projective space over $Y$ and projective morphisms
cards.summary: P^n_Y is the base change of Proj Z[T_0..T_n]; f is projective if it is a closed immersion into P^n_Y followed by the projection.
cards.statement: $\mathbb P^n_Y$ is the base change to $Y$ of $\operatorname{Proj}\mathbb Z[T_0,\dots,T_n]$, with its projection $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is **projective** if there are $n\ge0$ and a closed immersion $i:X\to\mathbb P^n_Y$ with $\pi\circ i=f$.

leanReading.note: projectiveSpaceOver n S is the fibre product over the terminal scheme of S and Proj of the standard-graded polynomial ring in n+1 variables over (ULift) ℤ, with projection pullback.fst; IsProjectiveMorphism f is ∃ n i, IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ π = f.

cards.title: $(p\circ i)_*=p_*\circ i_*$ on $CH_*\otimes\mathbb Q$
cards.summary: Proper pushforward of rational Chow classes is functorial.
cards.statement: Let $X,P,Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $i:X\to P$, $p:P\to Y$ proper morphisms over $k$. Then for $\gamma\in CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$: $(p\circ i)_*\gamma=p_*(i_*\gamma)$.
cards.proof: Both sides are $\mathbb Q$-linear in $\gamma$; on a class $q\otimes\alpha$ with $\alpha\in CH_j(X)$ this is the functoriality of proper pushforward of Chow classes of Stacks (`properChowPushforward_comp`).
cards.attack: This is functoriality of proper pushforward of cycles, extended ℚ-linearly; true for proper i, p between any schemes locally of finite type over k. Finding: smoothness and separatedness of X, P, Y are never used mathematically (in Lean they only supply 'locally of finite type') — redundant but harmless.

leanReading.note: With X, P, Y IsSmoothFT, i and p proper and the over-k equations, (i ≫ p)_* γ = p_*(i_* γ) on CHQ; the third equation follows from the other two.

cards.title: Riemann–Roch composes
cards.summary: If the formula holds for a closed immersion i and a proper p, it holds for p∘i.
cards.statement: Let $X,P,Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, $i:X\to P$ a closed immersion and $p:P\to Y$ a proper morphism, both over $k$. If the Riemann–Roch formula holds for $i$ and for $p$, it holds for $p\circ i$.
cards.proof: For $\alpha\in K_0(X)$: $(p\circ i)_*\tau_X(\alpha)=p_*i_*\tau_X(\alpha)=p_*\tau_P(i_!\alpha)=\tau_Y(p_!i_!\alpha)=\tau_Y((p\circ i)_!\alpha)$, using functoriality of $f_*$, the two hypotheses, and $(p\circ i)_!=p_!\circ i_!$ for a closed immersion $i$.
cards.attack: Chain checked: (p∘i)_* = p_*i_*, the formula for i at α, the formula for p at i_!α, and (p∘i)_! = p_!∘i_!, which needs P and Y Noetherian and quasi-compact — given. The hypotheses are used for the right morphisms and classes. Requiring i to be a closed immersion is a limitation of the functoriality proved for f_!, not of the mathematics.

leanReading.note: With IsSmoothFT on X, P, Y, i a closed immersion, p proper and the over-k equations: RiemannRochFor i → RiemannRochFor p → RiemannRochFor (i ≫ p). The hypotheses are exactly the card's.

cards.title: $\mathbb P^n_Y$ is again smooth, separated, of finite type
cards.summary: Projective space over an admissible Y is admissible, and its projection is proper.
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$. Then $\mathbb P^n_Y$, with structure morphism $\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, and the projection $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ is proper.
cards.proof: $\pi$ is smooth, proper (hence separated) and quasi-compact (Stacks: `projectiveSpaceOver.smooth`, `isProper_projectiveSpaceOver`), and these properties are stable under composition with $s_Y$.
cards.attack: π is the base change of ℙⁿ_ℤ → Spec ℤ, hence smooth and proper, and smooth, separated and quasi-compact morphisms are stable under composition with s_Y. The case n = 0 is consistent. No gap.

leanReading.note: isSmoothFT_projectiveSpaceOver gives IsSmoothFT k ((ℙⁿ_Y → Y) ≫ sY) for every n; isProper_projectiveSpaceOver_hom gives properness of ℙⁿ_Y → Y for every scheme Y (more general).

cards.title: Reduction to closed immersions and projections
cards.summary: GRR for projective morphisms follows from GRR for closed immersions into P^n_Y and for the projections P^n_Y → Y.
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$. Suppose that the Riemann–Roch formula holds (a) for every closed immersion $i:X\to\mathbb P^n_Y$ over $k$ with $X$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, and (b) for every projection $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$. Then it holds for every projective morphism $f:X\to Y$ over $k$ with $X$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.
cards.proof: By definition of projective, $f=\pi\circ i$ with $i:X\to\mathbb P^n_Y$ a closed immersion. $\mathbb P^n_Y$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, so (a) applies to $i$ and (b) to $\pi$; conclude because Riemann–Roch composes.
cards.attack: Checked quantifiers: f = π∘i, i is automatically over k, (a) is used for this i, whose target ℙⁿ_Y must be smooth, separated and of finite type for τ to make sense (provided), and (b) for this n. Projective implies proper, so the formula for f is meaningful. Correct.

leanReading.note: The hypotheses are the formula for every closed immersion X → ℙⁿ_Y over k with X IsSmoothFT (all n) and for every projection ℙⁿ_Y → Y; the conclusion is the formula for every f with IsProjectiveMorphism f. [IsProper f] follows from the factorisation.

cards.title: The twisted classes on $\mathbb P^n_Y$ and three statements about them
cards.summary: g_j(β) = [O(−j)]·π^*β, and the statements (P1) pushforward, (P2) generation, (P3) Riemann–Roch map.
cards.statement:
Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ the projection, and $\mathcal O(d)$ the twisting sheaves (pulled back from $\operatorname{Proj}\mathbb Z[T_0,\dots,T_n]$).

- $[\mathcal O(d)]\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,\mathbb P^n_Y)$ is the class of $\mathcal O(d)$.
- For $j\ge0$ and $\beta\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$ the **twisted class** is $g_j(\beta)=\theta\big([\mathcal O(-j)]\cdot\pi^*\beta\big)\in K_0(\mathbb P^n_Y)$.
- **(P1)** for all $0\le j\le n$ and $\beta$: $\pi_!\,g_j(\beta)=\theta_Y(\beta)$ if $j=0$, and $=0$ otherwise.
- **(P2)** for every $\alpha\in K_0(\mathbb P^n_Y)$ there are an integer $N>0$ and classes $\beta_0,\dots,\beta_n\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$ with $N\alpha=\sum_{j=0}^n g_j(\beta_j)$.
- **(P3)** for all $0\le j\le n$ and $\beta$: $\pi_*\,\tau_{\mathbb P^n_Y}(g_j(\beta))=\tau_Y(\theta_Y\beta)$ if $j=0$, and $=0$ otherwise.

leanReading.note: twistClass is the class of twistOver n Y d (O(d) pulled back from ℙⁿ over ℤ); twistedPullback j β = θ(twistClass(−j) · π^*β); the three Props are (P1), (P2), (P3) with j ≤ n, sums over range (n+1) and N > 0.

cards.title: Riemann–Roch for $\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ from (P1), (P2), (P3)
cards.summary: The projection case reduces to computing both sides on twisted classes and to their rational generation.
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $n\ge0$. If (P1), (P2) and (P3) hold for $(Y,n)$, then the Riemann–Roch formula holds for the projection $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$.
cards.proof: Let $\alpha\in K_0(\mathbb P^n_Y)$ and choose $N>0$, $\beta_j$ as in (P2). On each twisted class, (P3) and (P1) give $\pi_*\tau(g_j(\beta_j))=\tau_Y(\pi_!g_j(\beta_j))$ (both are $\tau_Y(\theta_Y\beta_j)$ for $j=0$ and $0$ otherwise). Both sides of the formula are additive in $\alpha$, so $N\cdot\pi_*\tau(\alpha)=N\cdot\tau_Y(\pi_!\alpha)$, and $N$ can be cancelled in the $\mathbb Q$-vector space $CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$.
cards.attack: Checked: on each g_j(β_j) both sides are τ_Y(θ_Yβ_j) (j = 0) or 0 (1 ≤ j ≤ n), the ranges of j in (P1)–(P3) match, and additivity gives N·π_*τ(α) = N·τ_Y(π_!α). Cancelling N is valid: N > 0 and the target is a ℚ-vector space.

leanReading.note: For IsSmoothFT Y and n : ℕ, ProjectionPushforwardFormula → ProjectionGeneration → ProjectionTauFormula → RiemannRochFor for ℙⁿ_Y → Y over k, with no other hypotheses.

cards.title: Normal sheaf of a closed immersion and the statement (E)
cards.statement:
Let $X$ and $P$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $i:X\to P$ a closed immersion over $k$.

- The **conormal sheaf** $C_{X/P}$ is the first term of the conormal sequence $0\to C_{X/P}\to i^*\Omega_{P/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}\to0$ of Stacks 06AA.
- The **normal sheaf** is its dual $N_{X/P}=\mathcal Hom(C_{X/P},\mathcal O_X)$, with class $[N_{X/P}]\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$.
- **(E)**, Riemann–Roch without tangent bundles, is the statement: for every $\alpha\in K_0(X)$, $\operatorname{ch}(i_!\alpha)\cap[P]=i_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[N_{X/P}]))\cap[X]\big)$ in $CH_*(P)_{\mathbb Q}$. (Here $\operatorname{td}(-[N])=\operatorname{td}(N)^{-1}$.)

leanReading.note: conormalSheaf is the first term of Stacks' conormalShortComplex i sP, normalSheaf its dual, normalClass the classOf of that, and ClosedImmersionFormula is (E) for all α with the pushforward along i; the sheaves are defined without the smoothness assumption.

cards.title: The conormal sheaf is finite locally free
cards.summary: For a closed immersion of smooth schemes, C_{X/P} is a vector bundle.
cards.statement: Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$. Then the conormal sheaf $C_{X/P}$ is finite locally free.
cards.proof: Since $X$ is smooth over $k$, the conormal sequence $0\to C_{X/P}\to i^*\Omega_{P/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}\to0$ is short exact (Stacks 06AA). Its middle and right terms are finite locally free (differentials of smooth morphisms, and pullback), and the kernel of an epimorphism between finite locally free modules is finite locally free.
cards.attack: Both smoothness hypotheses are needed: for the union of the three coordinate axes in 𝔸³ the conormal module needs 3 generators at the origin but has rank 2 elsewhere, and for the x-axis on the cone xy = z² it has torsion.

leanReading.note: For X and P IsSmoothFT, i a closed immersion and i ≫ sP = sX, the conclusion is IsFiniteLocallyFree (conormalSheaf k sP i).

cards.title: $\operatorname{ch}_p(\mathcal E^\vee)=(-1)^p\operatorname{ch}_p(\mathcal E)$
cards.summary: The sign rule for the Chern character of a dual bundle.
cards.statement: Let $X$ be locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology and $\mathcal E$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module with dual $\mathcal E^\vee=\mathcal Hom(\mathcal E,\mathcal O_X)$. Then $\operatorname{ch}([\mathcal E^\vee])$ is the rescaling of $\operatorname{ch}([\mathcal E])$ by the weights $(-1)^p$: $\operatorname{ch}_p([\mathcal E^\vee])=(-1)^p\operatorname{ch}_p([\mathcal E])$ for all $p$.
cards.proof: On a locus where $\mathcal E$ has constant rank, the total Chern class of $\mathcal E^\vee$ is the image of that of $\mathcal E$ under the ring endomorphism of $\prod_pA^p$ multiplying degree $p$ by $(-1)^p$ (Stacks: `totalChern_dualSheaf`). The power sums $P_p$ are Newton polynomials in the Chern classes, so the same ring map carries $P_p(\mathcal E)$ to $P_p(\mathcal E^\vee)$; as $P_p$ is homogeneous of degree $p$ this is multiplication by $(-1)^p$. The case of arbitrary rank follows by restriction to the rank loci, on which total classes are determined, and $\operatorname{ch}_p=P_p/p!$.
cards.attack: With Chern roots, ch(E^∨) = Σe^{−x_i} is the (−1)ᵖ-rescaling of Σe^{x_i} (checked in ℚ[x1, x2]); ch₀ = rank is unchanged. The proof (the sign map is a ring endomorphism carrying c(E) to c(E^∨), hence Newton polynomials, extended over the rank loci) is sound.

leanReading.note: For any Chow situation and E finite locally free, ch[dualSheaf E] = weight (n ↦ (−1)^n) (ch[E]), whose p-th component is (−1)^p ch_p(E).

cards.title: $\operatorname{td}(T_X)=i^*\operatorname{td}(T_P)\cdot\operatorname{td}(N_{X/P})^{-1}$
cards.summary: The Todd class of a smooth subscheme in terms of the ambient one and the normal bundle.
cards.statement: Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, with normal sheaf $N_{X/P}$. Then in $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$: $\operatorname{td}(T_X)=i^*\operatorname{td}(T_P)\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[N_{X/P}])$.
cards.proof: The conormal sequence is short exact with finite locally free terms, so $\operatorname{ch}[i^*\Omega_P]=\operatorname{ch}[C_{X/P}]+\operatorname{ch}[\Omega_X]$. Rescale by the signs $(-1)^p$ and use the sign rule for duals three times: $\operatorname{ch}[T_X]=\sigma\operatorname{ch}[i^*\Omega_P]-\operatorname{ch}[N_{X/P}]$. Since $\operatorname{ch}[i^*\Omega_P]=i^*\operatorname{ch}[\Omega_P]$ and pullback is graded, $\sigma\operatorname{ch}[i^*\Omega_P]=i^*\operatorname{ch}[T_P]=\operatorname{ch}(i^*[T_P])$. So $\operatorname{ch}[T_X]=\operatorname{ch}(i^*[T_P]+(-[N_{X/P}]))$, and applying the Todd operation, multiplicativity of the Todd class and its compatibility with pullback give the claim.
cards.attack: Checked on rational curves (line, conic, twisted cubic, rational normal quartic): the right side has degree-1 part td_1(T_ℙ¹), whereas td(N) in place of its inverse gives 2, 5, 11, 19. For a degree-d surface in ℙ³ the integral of the right side is 1, 1, 1, 2, 5 for d = 1..5, which is χ(O_S).

leanReading.note: toddTangent X = pullbackAQ i (toddTangent P) * toddClass (−normalClass k sP i) for a closed immersion i over k of IsSmoothFT schemes.

cards.title: The cap product is an action
cards.summary: (c·d) ∩ γ = c ∩ (d ∩ γ) over a field.
cards.statement: Let $X$ be locally of finite type over a field $k$. For $c,d\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ the cap operations on $CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ satisfy $(c\cdot d)\cap\gamma=c\cap(d\cap\gamma)$.
cards.proof: This is the multiplicativity of the total cap operation of Stacks (`totalRationalChowCap_mul`), which requires $\delta$ bounded below; over a field $\delta\ge0$.
cards.attack: This is Stacks' multiplicativity of the total cap, valid when δ is bounded below (δ ≥ 0 over a field). The order convention matches the Lean statement and is used consistently in the closed-immersion reduction. No gap.

leanReading.note: cap (c * d) = cap c * cap d in the endomorphisms of CHQ, whose product is composition, for any scheme locally of finite type over Spec k.

cards.title: Riemann–Roch for a closed immersion from (E)
cards.summary: The formula without tangent bundles implies the Riemann–Roch formula for i.
cards.statement: Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$. If (E) holds for $i$, then the Riemann–Roch formula holds for $i$.
cards.proof: For $\alpha\in K_0(X)$: $\tau_P(i_!\alpha)=\operatorname{td}(T_P)\cap\big(\operatorname{ch}(i_!\alpha)\cap[P]\big)$ (Todd classes commute with Chern characters, and cap is an action) $=\operatorname{td}(T_P)\cap i_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(-[N]))\cap[X]\big)$ by (E) $=i_*\big(i^*\operatorname{td}(T_P)\cap((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(-[N]))\cap[X])\big)$ by the projection formula $=i_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot i^*\operatorname{td}(T_P)\operatorname{td}(-[N]))\cap[X]\big)=i_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(T_X))\cap[X]\big)=i_*\tau_X(\alpha)$, using $i^*\operatorname{td}(T_P)=\operatorname{td}(i^*[T_P])$, commutativity, and $\operatorname{td}(T_X)=i^*\operatorname{td}(T_P)\operatorname{td}(-[N])$.
cards.attack: Verified each equality: commute td(T_P) with ch(i_!α), cap action, (E), projection formula, cap action, move i*td(T_P) = td(i*[T_P]) past ch(α), then the Todd class of the subscheme. All steps hold. The compatibility of td with pullback was used but not listed among the cards it rests on; this has been added.

leanReading.note: ClosedImmersionFormula k sX sP i hi → RiemannRochFor k sX sP i hi, with exactly IsSmoothFT on X and P, i a closed immersion and i ≫ sP = sX.

cards.title: (E) for every closed immersion of smooth schemes
cards.summary: ch(i_! α) ∩ [P] = i_*((ch(α)·td(N)^{-1}) ∩ [X]) for closed immersions of smooth schemes.
cards.statement: For every closed immersion $i:X\to P$ over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, the statement (E) holds: $\operatorname{ch}(i_!\alpha)\cap[P]=i_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[N_{X/P}]))\cap[X]\big)$ for all $\alpha\in K_0(X)$.
cards.proof: The core case of (E) holds, by deformation to the normal cone and Riemann–Roch for the zero section of $\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O)$. The general case follows from the core case by cutting source and target into their parts of constant dimension.
cards.attack: About 290 exact checks of (E) and of the Riemann–Roch formula (points in P^1, P^2, P^3; a line and a conic in P^2 with all degrees from −8 to 9; diagonal and fibre in P^1 × P^1; a twisted cubic; X = P; X = ∅; disconnected X and P), no failure; with the conormal bundle in place of the normal bundle the answer is wrong (h + h²/2 against h − h²/2). The proof chains the core case and the reduction, whose hypotheses match. Not broken.

leanReading.note: closedImmersionFormula is unconditional: for every closed immersion i over k between IsSmoothFT schemes, ClosedImmersionFormula holds, whose printed body is ch(i_!α) ∩ [P] = i_*((ch(α)·td(−[N_{X/P}])) ∩ [X]) for all α in K'_0(X).

cards.title: Riemann–Roch for closed immersions
cards.summary: GRR holds for every closed immersion of smooth schemes.
cards.statement: The Riemann–Roch formula holds for every closed immersion $i:X\to P$ over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.
cards.proof: (E) holds for $i$, and the Riemann–Roch formula for a closed immersion follows from (E) for it.
cards.attack: Chains (E) for i with the reduction of Riemann–Roch for a closed immersion to (E); the hypotheses match and nothing else is assumed. Numerical checks as for (E): a line in P^2 → pt gives d + 1, odd-degree bundles on a conic give 2d + 2. Not broken.

leanReading.note: riemannRochFor_closedImmersion is unconditional: for every closed immersion i over k between IsSmoothFT schemes it gives RiemannRochFor k sX sP i hi, that is, i_* τ_X(α) = τ_P(i_! α) in CH_*(P)_ℚ for all α.

cards.title: (P1): the pushforward of the twisted classes
cards.summary: π_!([O(−j)]·π^*β) = β for j = 0 and 0 for 1 ≤ j ≤ n.
cards.statement: For every $Y$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and every $n\ge0$, the statement (P1) holds: $\pi_!\,g_j(\beta)=\theta_Y(\beta)$ for $j=0$ and $\pi_!\,g_j(\beta)=0$ for $1\le j\le n$, for all $\beta\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$.
cards.proof: $\mathbb P^n_Y$ is again smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $\pi$ is proper, so $\theta$ and $\pi_!$ are defined. Both sides are additive in $\beta$, so take $\beta=[\mathcal G]$ with $\mathcal G$ finite locally free. Then $[\mathcal O(-j)]\cdot\pi^*[\mathcal G]=[\mathcal O(-j)\otimes\pi^*\mathcal G]$, $\theta$ sends it to its class as a coherent sheaf, and by the projection formula $R^q\pi_*(\mathcal O(-j)\otimes\pi^*\mathcal G)\cong R^q\pi_*\mathcal O(-j)\otimes\mathcal G$. For $1\le j\le n$ every $R^q\pi_*\mathcal O(-j)$ vanishes (the higher direct images of the twists on projective space), so $\pi_!g_j(\beta)=0$. For $j=0$: $R^q\pi_*\mathcal O=0$ for $q>0$ and $\pi_*\mathcal O\cong\mathcal O_Y$, so $\pi_!g_0(\beta)=[\mathcal O_Y\otimes\mathcal G]=[\mathcal G]=\theta_Y(\beta)$.

leanReading.note: For every field k, Y with IsSmoothFT and n, the statement unfolds to (P1): for all j ≤ n and β, pushforwardK π (θ([O(−j)] · π^*β)) = θ_Y β if j = 0 and 0 otherwise, with no further hypothesis.

cards.attack: Computed π_![𝒪(−j)] = χ(ℙⁿ, 𝒪(−j)) over a point from h⁰ and hⁿ: on ℙ¹, j = 0..3 gives 1, 0, −1, −2; on ℙ², j = 0..4 gives 1, 0, 0, 1, 3, so 1 ≤ j ≤ n is exactly the vanishing range and j = n+1 already gives (−1)ⁿ (Rⁿπ_*𝒪(−n−1) ≅ 𝒪_Y). Every step holds: reduction to β = [𝒢] by additivity, θ on classes, the projection formula, vanishing of all R^qπ_*𝒪(−j) for 1 ≤ j ≤ n, and π_*𝒪 ≅ 𝒪_Y with R^{q>0}π_*𝒪 = 0;

cards.title: (P2): the twisted classes generate rationally
cards.summary: A positive multiple of every class of K_0(P^n_Y) is a sum of twisted classes.
cards.statement: For every $Y$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and every $n\ge0$, the statement (P2) holds: for every $\alpha\in K_0(\mathbb P^n_Y)$ there are $N>0$ and $\beta_0,\dots,\beta_n\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$ with $N\alpha=\sum_{j=0}^ng_j(\beta_j)$.
cards.proof: $\mathbb P^n_Y$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, so $\theta$ is bijective and Stacks 0FEY applies on it. Write $\alpha=\theta(a)$ with $a\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,\mathbb P^n_Y)$. By the rational projective bundle formula, $\Phi(1\otimes a)=\operatorname{ch}(a)\cap[\mathbb P^n_Y]=\sum_{i\le n}h^i\cap\pi^!y_i$. By Stacks 0FEY on $Y$, $y_i=\Phi_Y(w_i)$ with $w_i\in\mathbb Q\otimes K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$, and the Gysin pullback satisfies $\pi^!\Phi_Y(w)=\Phi_{\mathbb P^n_Y}(\pi^*w)$ (Stacks 0FF8). Modulo $x^{n+1}$ each $x^i$ is a rational combination of the $e^{-jx}$, $0\le j\le n$; since $h^{n+1}$ acts as zero and $\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal O(-j)]=e^{-jh}$, evaluating at $h$ (a ring map) shows that the operator $h^i\cap-$ is a rational combination of the operators $\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal O(-j)]\cap-$. As the cap product is an action, $\Phi(1\otimes a)=\Phi\big(\sum_j[\mathcal O(-j)]\cdot\pi^*W_j\big)$ for suitable $W_j\in\mathbb Q\otimes K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$, and injectivity of $\Phi$ on $\mathbb P^n_Y$ (0FEY again) gives $1\otimes a=\sum_j[\mathcal O(-j)]\cdot\pi^*W_j$ in $\mathbb Q\otimes K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,\mathbb P^n_Y)$. The kernel of $M\to\mathbb Q\otimes M$ is the torsion of $M$; clearing denominators, a positive multiple $Na$ equals $\sum_j[\mathcal O(-j)]\cdot\pi^*\beta_j$ with $\beta_j\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$. Apply $\theta$.

leanReading.note: For every k, Y with IsSmoothFT and n: for all α in K'₀(ℙⁿ_Y) there are N with 0 < N and β with N • α = ∑_{j ∈ range (n+1)} twistedPullback j (β j).

cards.attack: Over a point the matrix χ(𝒪(d−j)), 0 ≤ d, j ≤ n, is lower unitriangular (ℙ¹: [[1,0],[2,1]], ℙ²: [[1,0,0],[3,1,0],[6,3,1]], det 1), so [𝒪],…,[𝒪(−n)] are a ℤ-basis and N = 1 works there ([k(pt)] = [𝒪] − [𝒪(−1)] on ℙ¹, [𝒪] − 2[𝒪(−1)] + [𝒪(−2)] on ℙ²; [𝒪(d)] = (d+1)[𝒪] − d[𝒪(−1)] on ℙ¹, checked on all twists).

cards.title: (P3): the Riemann–Roch map on the twisted classes
cards.summary: π_* τ([O(−j)]·π^*β) = τ_Y(β) for j = 0 and 0 for 1 ≤ j ≤ n.
cards.statement: For every $Y$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and every $n\ge0$, the statement (P3) holds: $\pi_*\,\tau_{\mathbb P^n_Y}(g_j(\beta))=\tau_Y(\theta_Y\beta)$ for $j=0$ and $=0$ for $1\le j\le n$, for all $\beta\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$.
cards.proof: $\operatorname{ch}(g_j(\beta))=\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal O(-j)]\cdot\operatorname{ch}(\pi^*\beta)=e^{-jh}\cdot\pi^*\operatorname{ch}(\beta)$. With $\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n_Y})=\pi^*\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\cdot Q(h)^{n+1}$, and since Chern characters commute with each other ($\operatorname{ch}$ is a ring map from a commutative ring), Todd classes commute with Chern characters and evaluation at $h$ is a ring map, $\operatorname{ch}(g_j\beta)\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n_Y})=\pi^*\big(\operatorname{ch}(\beta)\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\big)\cdot F(h)$ with $F=e^{-jx}Q^{n+1}$. By the integral over the fibres, $\pi_*\tau(g_j\beta)=F_n\cdot\tau_Y(\theta_Y\beta)$, and the coefficient $F_n$ of $x^n$ is $1$ for $j=0$ and $0$ for $1\le j\le n$.

leanReading.note: ProjectionTauFormula k sY n unfolds to: for every j ≤ n and β, the pushforward along π of τ(θ([O(−j)]·π^*β)) is τ_Y(θ_Y β) if j = 0 and 0 otherwise; the twist has the right sign and there is no extra hypothesis.

cards.attack: Computed F_n = [xⁿ] e^{−jx}Q^{n+1} exactly: 1 for j = 0 and 0 for 1 ≤ j ≤ n for all n ≤ 7; for j = 0..n+2 on ℙ¹, ℙ², ℙ³ it is (1, 0, −1, −2), (1, 0, 0, 1, 3), (1, 0, 0, 0, −1, −4), equal to χ(𝒪(−j)), so (P3) matches (P1) and the range is sharp. Over Y = ℙ¹ (ring ℚ[u,h]/(u², h^{n+1}), td = (1+u)Q(h)^{n+1}) π_*τ(𝒪(a, −j)) = F_n·τ_Y(𝒪(a)) holds exactly for |a| ≤ 3, j ≤ n+1, n = 1, 2.

cards.title: Riemann–Roch for the projections $\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$
cards.summary: GRR holds for every projection of a projective space over a smooth base.
cards.statement: For every $Y$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and every $n\ge0$, the Riemann–Roch formula holds for the projection $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$.
cards.proof: By the reduction of the projection case to (P1), (P2), (P3), applied to $(Y,n)$.

leanReading.note: RiemannRochFor k (π ≫ sY) sY π rfl unfolds to π_* τ(α) = τ_Y(π_! α) for every α in K'₀(ℙⁿ_Y); the only hypotheses are k a field, IsSmoothFT k sY and n.

cards.attack: Pure reduction: proj-reduction for (Y, n) needs (P1), (P2), (P3) for that same (Y, n), and proj-pushforward, proj-generation and proj-tau give them for every Y smooth, separated, of finite type and every n ≥ 0, so the quantifiers match; the N of (P2) is cancelled in the ℚ-vector space CH_*(Y)_ℚ.

cards.title: The whole reduction in one statement
cards.summary: (E), (P1), (P2), (P3) together imply GRR for projective morphisms.
cards.statement: Suppose that (E) holds for every closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, and that (P1), (P2) and (P3) hold for every such $Y$ and every $n\ge0$. Then the Riemann–Roch formula holds for every projective morphism $f:X\to Y$ over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.
cards.proof: (E) gives the Riemann–Roch formula for closed immersions, (P1)–(P3) for the projections $\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$, and the reduction to these two cases gives it for projective morphisms.
cards.attack: Checked that each hypothesis is applied where needed: (E) to the closed immersion X → ℙⁿ_Y from the factorisation, (P1)–(P3) to that (Y, n), then the reduction. The universal quantification over Y, n and closed immersions is exactly what is used. Correct.

leanReading.note: Hypotheses: (E) for every closed immersion over k of IsSmoothFT schemes, and the three projection statements for every IsSmoothFT Y and every n; conclusion: RiemannRochFor for every f with IsProjectiveMorphism f.

cards.title: The Euler characteristic on $K_0$
cards.summary: χ : K_0(X) → ℤ, χ[F] = Σ (−1)^i dim H^i(X, F), for X proper over k.
cards.statement: For a scheme $X$ proper over $k$, $\chi:K_0(X)\to\mathbb Z$ is the group homomorphism with $\chi([\mathcal F])=\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\sum_i(-1)^i\dim_kH^i(X,\mathcal F)$ for coherent $\mathcal F$: the Euler characteristic of Stacks 0BEJ, which is additive on short exact sequences (Stacks 08AA).

leanReading.note: eulerK is KZero.lift of F ↦ eulerCharacteristic k sX F.obj for proper sX, where eulerCharacteristic is the alternating sum of the k-dimensions of the cohomology groups (Stacks 0BEJ).

cards.title: $\chi$ is compatible with the pushforward to the point
cards.summary: χ([F]) is the Euler characteristic, and χ(Spec k, (s_X)_! α) = χ(X, α).
cards.statement: Let $X$ be proper over $k$ with structure morphism $s_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Then $\chi([\mathcal F])=\chi(X,\mathcal F)$ for every coherent $\mathcal F$, and for every $\alpha\in K_0(X)$: $\chi\big(\operatorname{Spec}k,(s_X)_!\alpha\big)=\chi(X,\alpha)$.
cards.proof: The first statement is the definition of $\chi$ on generators. For the second take $\alpha=[\mathcal F]$: $(s_X)_![\mathcal F]=\sum_{i<N}(-1)^i[R^i(s_X)_*\mathcal F]$, and Stacks 0BEK (`eulerCharacteristic_eq_finsum_higherDirectImage`, with $f=s_X$ and $g=\mathrm{id}$) gives $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\sum_i(-1)^i\chi(\operatorname{Spec}k,R^i(s_X)_*\mathcal F)$, where the terms with $i\ge N$ vanish.
cards.attack: On Spec k, R^i(s_X)_*F is H^i(X, F), so χ(Spec k, (s_X)_![F]) is the alternating sum of dim H^i(X, F) (Stacks 0BEK with g = id), terms beyond the bound being zero. Example ℙ¹: s_![O(d)] = (d+1)[k] and χ = d + 1. Correct.

leanReading.note: eulerK_mk gives χ([F]) = eulerCharacteristic k sX F; eulerK_pushforwardK gives eulerK over the identity of Spec k of pushforwardK sX α = eulerK k sX α, both for proper sX.

cards.title: Riemann–Roch on the point
cards.summary: τ(γ) = χ(γ)·[Spec k] for γ in K_0(Spec k).
cards.statement: The point $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, and for every $\gamma\in K_0(\operatorname{Spec}k)$: $\tau_{\operatorname{Spec}k}(\gamma)=\chi(\gamma)\cdot[\operatorname{Spec}k]$ in $CH_*(\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathbb Q}$.
cards.proof: It suffices to take $\gamma=[\mathcal F]$. A coherent module on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite locally free of rank $r=\dim_kH^0(\mathcal F)$, and $\chi(\mathcal F)=r$ since the higher cohomology of an affine scheme vanishes. On the point $CH_j(\operatorname{Spec}k)=0$ for $j\ne0$, so capping $[\operatorname{Spec}k]$ with a class only involves its degree-$0$ component; that of $\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal F]$ is the rank $r$ and that of a Todd class is $1$. Hence $\tau(\gamma)=r\cdot[\operatorname{Spec}k]$.
cards.attack: CH_j(Spec k) = 0 for j ≠ 0, so only degree-0 components act on [Spec k]; the degree-0 component of ch·td is rank·1; and χ = rank = dim H⁰ because higher cohomology vanishes on an affine scheme. Correct.

leanReading.note: isSmoothFT_id gives IsSmoothFT k (identity of Spec k); tau_point gives tau γ = (eulerK γ : ℚ) • fundamentalClass of Spec k.

cards.title: Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch from the formula for $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$
cards.summary: If GRR holds for the structure morphism, the pushforward of τ_X(α) to the point is χ(X, α)·[Spec k].
cards.statement: Let $X$ be smooth, separated, of finite type and proper over $k$, with structure morphism $s_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. If the Riemann–Roch formula holds for $s_X$, then for every $\alpha\in K_0(X)$: $(s_X)_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_X))\cap[X]\big)=\chi(X,\alpha)\cdot[\operatorname{Spec}k]$ in $CH_*(\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathbb Q}$.
cards.proof: $(s_X)_*\tau_X(\alpha)=\tau_{\operatorname{Spec}k}((s_X)_!\alpha)=\chi(\operatorname{Spec}k,(s_X)_!\alpha)\cdot[\operatorname{Spec}k]=\chi(X,\alpha)\cdot[\operatorname{Spec}k]$, by the hypothesis, Riemann–Roch on the point, and the compatibility of $\chi$ with the pushforward.
cards.attack: The chain (the formula for s_X, Riemann–Roch on the point, compatibility of χ) is sound and every hypothesis is used. Sanity: on ℙ² it gives χ(O(d)) = 3, 1, 0, 0, 1, 3, 6, 10 for d = −4..3, and on a genus-g curve deg L + 1 − g. Correct.

leanReading.note: For sX IsSmoothFT and proper: RiemannRochFor k sX (identity of Spec k) sX → ∀ α, (sX)_*(tau k sX α) = (eulerK k sX α) • [Spec k], with the pushforward along sX.

cards.title: Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch
cards.summary: χ(X, F) = ∫_X ch(F)·td(T_X) for a smooth projective variety X.
cards.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over a field $k$ and $\mathcal F$ a coherent sheaf on $X$. Then $$\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\int_X\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)\,\operatorname{td}(T_X).$$

**How it is read in Lean.** $X$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and its structure morphism $s_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is projective. The integral is the pushforward to the point: the statement is $(s_X)_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_X))\cap[X]\big)=\chi(X,\mathcal F)\cdot[\operatorname{Spec}k]$ in $CH_*(\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathbb Q}$.
cards.proof: The point $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, and $s_X$ is projective, hence proper. Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch for $f=s_X$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the Riemann–Roch formula for $s_X$; apply the previous card to $\alpha=[\mathcal F]$.
cards.attack: The reading is faithful: classes of positive dimension push forward to zero groups on the point, so the pushforward is the degree of the 0-dimensional part, and smooth projective varieties satisfy the Lean hypotheses. The card rests on the main theorem, which is conditional on (E).

leanReading.note: hirzebruch_riemann_roch binds only k, IsSmoothFT X, IsProjectiveMorphism sX and α in K'_0(X), with properness derived from projectivity; it states (s_X)_*((ch α · td(T_X)) ∩ [X]) = χ(X, α)·[Spec k], for any class α, more general than a coherent sheaf.

cards.title: Todd polynomials in a commutative Chow ring
cards.summary: Defining td by Todd polynomials in the Chern classes needs a commutative ring that Stacks does not provide.
cards.statement: Define $\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E)$ by evaluating the Todd polynomials at the Chern classes of $\mathcal E$, inside a commutative $\mathbb Q$-algebra structure on $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$.
cards.why: Stacks gives `RationalTotalChowClass` only `Ring` and `Module ℚ` instances; `CommRing` and `Algebra ℚ` fail to synthesize (checked by a probe compile), because Stacks, like the source, does not assert that $A^*(X)$ is commutative. The definition used instead is $\operatorname{td}=\exp\big(\sum_pp!\,\ell_p\operatorname{ch}_p\big)$; its multiplicativity only needs the components of Chern characters to commute, which follows from the Adams operation $\psi^2$.

cards.title: Importing Stacks' own $f_!$
cards.summary: Stacks has a proper pushforward on K'_0 (0FDL), but its module is not compiled on this machine.
cards.statement: Use Stacks' `AlgebraicGeometry.ProperPushforwardKZero.properPushforward` (tag 0FDL) as $f_!$, with its projection formula 0FDM.
cards.why: The module `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/GrothendieckGroupProperPushforward` is not among the compiled modules, so importing it fails with a missing object file; the same holds for `Perfect/ProjectionFormulaKZero/*` and `Perfect/CoherentKGroupModule` (0FDM). $f_!$ was therefore built here from compiled ingredients (coherence 02O5, uniform vanishing 01XJ, the $\delta$-functor of higher direct images), without consulting the uncompiled file.

cards.title: Integral $K$-theory of projective bundles
cards.summary: Generating K_0(P^n_Y) over K_0(Y) by the O(−j) integrally is out of reach of the compiled library.
cards.statement: Prove that $K_0(\mathbb P^n_Y)$ is generated over $K_0(Y)$ by the classes of $\mathcal O(-j)$, $0\le j\le n$, by Quillen's resolution of regular sheaves, by Beilinson's resolution of the diagonal, or by localization and homotopy invariance.
cards.why: The compiled library has none of the ingredients: no localization sequence $K_0(Z)\to K_0(X)\to K_0(U)\to0$ for schemes, no homotopy invariance of $K_0$, no Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity (searched `08A2`, `regularity`), and the resolution of the diagonal (`DiagonalResolution`) is not compiled. Replaced by the rational statement (P2), which suffices because $\tau$ takes values in a $\mathbb Q$-vector space and which follows from Stacks 0FEY and the projective bundle formula for Chow groups.

cards.title: Closed immersions from Stacks 0FEG and 0FEH
