cards.summary: Stacks' Riemann–Roch without denominators gives only the leading term, and only for the structure sheaf.
cards.statement: Deduce (E) for a closed immersion of smooth schemes from Stacks' computation of the localized Chern classes of $i_*\mathcal O_Z$ for a regular immersion (tags 0FEG, 0FEH).
cards.why: Those theorems (`regularImmersionStructureSheafSituation_capFundamentalClass`) give $\operatorname{ch}_t(i_*\mathcal O_Z)\cap[X]=0$ for $t<r$ and $=[Z]$ for $t=r$, the leading term only, and only for the structure sheaf of $Z$. (E) needs all degrees and all vector bundles on the subscheme, that is the full Koszul computation $\sum_p(-1)^p\operatorname{ch}(\Lambda^pN^\vee)=c_r(N)\operatorname{td}(N)^{-1}$ on the projective completion of the normal bundle, which Stacks does not carry out.

cards.title: Tensoring with a module
cards.summary: The functor − ⊗ H on O_Z-modules.
cards.statement: For a scheme $Z$ and an $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal H$, $-\otimes\mathcal H$ is the functor $\mathcal A\mapsto\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z}\mathcal H$ on $\mathcal O_Z$-modules (the tensor product of sheaves of modules).

leanReading.note: The body is tensorRight H, sending A to A ⊗ H; the monoidal structure (hidden by the printout, explicit in the source) is Stacks' sheafified tensor product of O_Z-modules (01CA).

cards.title: Projection formula for higher direct images
cards.summary: R^n f_*(F ⊗ f^*G) ≅ R^n f_*F ⊗ G for G finite locally free (Stacks 01E8).
cards.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $\mathcal G$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module. For every integer $n$ there is an isomorphism, natural in the $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$: $R^nf_*\big(\mathcal F\otimes f^*\mathcal G\big)\cong R^nf_*\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G$.
cards.proof: A finite locally free module is dualizable: with its dual it has a unit and a counit satisfying the triangle identities (Stacks 0FNV). Hence $-\otimes\mathcal G$ and $-\otimes f^*\mathcal G$ are both left and right adjoint to tensoring with the dual; they are exact and preserve injective modules (Stacks 01E7). In degree $0$ the isomorphism $f_*(\mathcal F\otimes f^*\mathcal G)\cong f_*\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G$ is the projection formula for a dualizable object along the monoidal adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$. Because tensoring is exact and preserves injectives, both sides in degree $n$ are computed from an injective resolution of $\mathcal F$, and the degree-$0$ isomorphism extends to all $n$.

leanReading.note: For any f, any finite locally free G and any n : ℤ it gives an isomorphism of functors (− ⊗ f^*G) ⋙ R^n f_* ≅ R^n f_* ⋙ (− ⊗ G), so naturality in F is expressed; no extra hypotheses.

cards.attack: Simple cases hold: f = id (both sides ℱ⊗𝒢 in degree 0, zero above), 𝒢 = 𝒪^r and Y a point (both sides (Rⁿf_*ℱ)^r by additivity). Both halves of 'finite locally free' are needed: for 𝒢 = k(0) on Y = 𝔸¹, π: ℙ¹×𝔸¹ → 𝔸¹ and ℱ the extension of 𝒪(2) by 𝒪(−2) with class t·e, e ≠ 0 (non-split, h⁰ = 2, for t ≠ 0; 𝒪(2)⊕𝒪(−2), h⁰ = 3, at t = 0), π_*(ℱ⊗π^*k(0)) = k³ but π_*ℱ⊗k(0) = k² (π_*ℱ is free of rank 2);

cards.title: $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)\otimes\mathbb Q\cong CH_*(X)\otimes\mathbb Q$ on regular schemes
cards.summary: a ↦ ch(a) ∩ [X] is bijective rationally, for regular X.
cards.statement: Let $X$ be a regular quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal, locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology, with $\delta$ bounded on $X$. Then $\Phi_X:\mathbb Q\otimes K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)\to CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, $q\otimes a\mapsto q\cdot(\operatorname{ch}(a)\cap[X])$, is bijective.
cards.source: Stacks Project, Tag 0FEY; in the compiled Lean library `Stacks.Chow.bijective_rationalChernCharacterCapFundamentalClass`. Used for $\mathbb P^n_Y$ (injectivity) and for $Y$ (surjectivity) in the proof of (P2).

cards.title: The Gysin map of a flat morphism is flat pullback
cards.summary: For flat lci f of relative dimension m, f^! = f^* on Chow groups.
cards.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a flat local complete intersection morphism of relative dimension $m$ between schemes locally of finite type over the base. Then its Gysin map is flat pullback: $f^!\beta=f^*\beta\in CH_{k+m}(X)$ for $\beta\in CH_k(Y)$.
cards.source: Stacks Project, Tag 0FF4. Stacks' Lean proof is in the module `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/WeilCohomology/Concrete/ProjectiveBundleRationalChow`, which is not compiled on this machine; its two lemmas (`lciGysinMapComponent_eq_single`, `lciGysinRational_of_tmul_of_flat`) are reproduced from that module in `GRR/ProjectionGen.lean`, where they compile from compiled modules. Used to identify the Gysin pullback along $\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ with flat pullback.

cards.title: Gysin pullback between smooth schemes
cards.summary: f^! : CH_*(Y)⊗ℚ → CH_*(X)⊗ℚ for a morphism of smooth k-schemes.
cards.statement: For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ over $k$ between Noetherian schemes with affine diagonal that are smooth over $k$, $f^!:CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\to CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is the Gysin homomorphism of Stacks for the local complete intersection morphism $f$, tensored with $\mathbb Q$.

leanReading.note: The body is Stacks' lciGysinRational (the Gysin map of 0FF3, degree by degree, tensored with ℚ); the Lean needs only smoothness and local finite type, which is more general than the card.

cards.title: Powers of $x$ through the series $e^{-jx}$
cards.summary: Modulo x^{n+1}, every x^m is a rational combination of e^{−jx}, 0 ≤ j ≤ n.
cards.statement: For all $n,m\ge0$ there are rational numbers $c_0,\dots,c_n$ and a power series $G\in\mathbb Q[[x]]$ with $x^m=\sum_{j=0}^nc_j\,e^{-jx}+x^{n+1}G$, where $e^{-jx}=(e^{-x})^j$.
cards.proof: Call a series *good* if it is a rational combination of the $e^{-jx}$, $0\le j\le n$, plus a multiple of $x^{n+1}$; good series are stable under sums and rational multiples, and multiples of $x^{n+1}$ are good. Since $1-e^{-x}=x\,u$ with $u(0)=1$, $(1-e^{-x})^m=x^m+x^{m+1}U_m$ for a series $U_m$, and for $m\le n$ the binomial expansion shows $(1-e^{-x})^m$ is good. By descending induction on $m$ from $n+1$ to $0$, every multiple $x^mG$ of $x^m$ is good: $x^mG=G(0)(1-e^{-x})^m+x^{m+1}G'$ for some $G'$, and both terms are good. In particular $x^m$ is good.

leanReading.note: For all n, m it gives c : ℕ → ℚ and G with X^m = ∑_{j ∈ range (n+1)} c j • expNeg^j + X^(n+1) * G; only c_0..c_n enter.

cards.attack: Solved for the c_j exactly for all n ≤ 5, m ≤ 7 (Vandermonde in the nodes 0, −1, …, −n): always solvable, remainder divisible by x^{n+1} (e.g. n = 3, m = 2: x² ≡ 2 − 5e^{−x} + 4e^{−2x} − e^{−3x}, G = 11/12 − x + …). With only j ≤ n−1 the system is inconsistent for every 1 ≤ m ≤ n (n ≤ 5) and solvable only for m = 0 (the defect is the Stirling number c(n, m) ≠ 0), so n+1 exponentials are needed.

cards.title: $\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal O(-j)]=e^{-jh}$ on $\mathbb P^n_Y$
cards.summary: The Chern character of the negative twists in terms of h = c_1(O(1)).
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))\in A^*(\mathbb P^n_Y)_{\mathbb Q}$. For every $j\ge0$: $\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal O(-j)]$ is the value at $h$ of the series $(e^{-x})^j$.
cards.proof: In $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,\mathbb P^n_Y)$, $[\mathcal O(a)]\cdot[\mathcal O(b)]=[\mathcal O(a+b)]$ (because $\mathcal O(a)\otimes\mathcal O(b)\cong\mathcal O(a+b)$, compiled in Stacks) and $[\mathcal O(0)]=1$, so $[\mathcal O(-j)]=[\mathcal O(-1)]^j$ and $[\mathcal O(-1)]\cdot[\mathcal O(1)]=1$. Since $\operatorname{ch}$ is a ring map and $\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal O(1)]=e^{h}$, $\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal O(-1)]$ is the inverse of $e^h$, which is $e^{-h}$ because evaluation at $h$ is a ring map and $e^xe^{-x}=1$. Take $j$-th powers.

leanReading.note: For every k, Y with IsSmoothFT, n and j: ch (twistClass Y n (−j)) = ev h (expNeg^j) with h = firstChernQ (twistOver n Y 1).

hypotheses.text: $Y$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.
hypotheses.redundant: Never used: the computation takes place in $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,\mathbb P^n_Y)$ and $A^*(\mathbb P^n_Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ and works for every $Y$ locally of finite type over $k$. It is kept because the twisted classes are only used over such $Y$.

cards.attack: On ℙ¹ and ℙ², ∫e^{−jh}e^{dh}Q(h)^{n+1} = χ(𝒪(d−j)) exactly whenever |d−j| ≤ 9, so the sign is right (e^{+jh} would give χ(𝒪(d+j))). The proof is valid in a possibly non-commutative ring: ch[𝒪(−1)]·e^h = 1 and e^h·e^{−h} = 1 force ch[𝒪(−1)] = e^{−h}, then j-th powers by ev-ring.

cards.title: Projective bundle formula for $\mathbb P^n_Y$, rationally
cards.summary: Every class of CH_*(P^n_Y)⊗ℚ is Σ_{i≤n} h^i ∩ π^! y_i.
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ the projection and $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. Every $x\in CH_*(\mathbb P^n_Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ can be written $x=\sum_{i=0}^{n}h^i\cap\pi^!y_i$ with $y_0,\dots,y_n\in CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$, where $\pi^!$ is the Gysin pullback and $h^i\cap$ the $i$-fold cap with $h$.
cards.proof: $\mathbb P^n_Y$ is smooth over $k$ and Noetherian with affine diagonal, so $\pi^!$ is defined. With $\mathcal O(1)$, $\pi$ is a projective tower of fibre dimension $n$ in the sense of Stacks (`isProjectiveTower_projectiveSpaceOver`), for which the projective bundle formula (Stacks 02TX) holds: $(\beta_i)\mapsto\sum_{i\le n}c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*\beta_i$ is surjective onto the Chow groups of $\mathbb P^n_Y$ (`bundleMap_surjective`). The Gysin map of the smooth morphism $\pi$ is flat pullback (Stacks 0FF4), and Stacks' cap with the first Chern class is the cap with $h$. Tensor with $\mathbb Q$ and sum over the degrees.

leanReading.note: For every x it gives y : Fin (n+1) → CHQ Y with x = ∑_i (cap h)^i (smoothGysinRational along π (y i)); the Gysin map is along π (forced by the rfl proof) and (cap h)^i is the i-fold cap.

cards.attack: On ℙⁿ_k (n = 1, 2) CH_* has basis [ℙ^{n−i}] = hⁱ∩π^*[pt], i ≤ n, and on ℙ¹×ℙⁿ (Y = ℙ¹) the classes uᵃhⁱ∩[ℙ¹×ℙⁿ] give rank 2(n+1) = (n+1)·rank CH(ℙ¹): the map is onto, and i ≤ n cannot be lowered (rank n+1 over a point). The proof (Stacks 02TX along the projective tower, 0FF4 to identify π^! with flat pullback for the smooth π, c₁-cap = h-cap) is sound.

cards.title: $h^{n+1}$ acts as zero on $\mathbb P^n_Y$
cards.summary: The (n+1)-fold cap with c_1(O(1)) vanishes on CH_*(P^n_Y)⊗ℚ.
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ on $\mathbb P^n_Y$. The $(n+1)$-fold cap with $h$ is zero on $CH_*(\mathbb P^n_Y)_{\mathbb Q}$.
cards.proof: For a projective tower of fibre dimension $n$ with line bundle $L$, $c_1(L)^{n+1}\cap\pi^*\beta=0$ for every $\beta$ on the base, by induction along the tower: for $n=0$ the bundle is trivial, and in general $c_1(L)\cap\pi^*\beta$ is pushed forward from the zero scheme of a section of $L$, which is a tower of fibre dimension $n-1$ (`capPow_bundlePullback_eq_zero`). By the previous card every class is $\sum_{i\le n}h^i\cap\pi^!y_i$, where $\pi^!$ is flat pullback $\pi^*$ (Stacks 0FF4), and the caps with $h$ commute with each other, so $h^{n+1}$ kills every class.

leanReading.note: For every k, Y with IsSmoothFT and n: cap (firstChernQ (twistOver n Y 1)) ^ (n+1) = 0 as an endomorphism of CHQ ℙⁿ_Y.

hypotheses.text: $Y$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.
hypotheses.redundant: The statement holds for every $Y$ locally of finite type over $k$: quote the projective bundle formula with flat pullback $\pi^*$ instead of $\pi^!$. Smoothness enters this proof only because the bundle formula is used in its Gysin form.

cards.attack: On ℙⁿ_k and ℙ¹×ℙⁿ (n = 1, 2) h^{n+1} = 0 while hⁿ∩[ℙ¹×ℙⁿ] = [ℙ¹×pt] ≠ 0, so the exponent n+1 is sharp; the hypothesis 'Y smooth, separated, of finite type' is not needed. The tower induction (c₁(𝒪(1))∩π^*β is pushed forward from the zero scheme ℙ^{n−1}_Y of a section) and the final step (powers of h∩ commute) are sound.

cards.title: The Euler sequence on projective space over a ring
cards.summary: 0 → Ω → O(−1)^{n+1} → O → 0 on P^n over a ring.
cards.statement: On $\mathbb P^n_R=\operatorname{Proj}R[T_0,\dots,T_n]$ over a commutative ring $R$ there is a short exact sequence $0\to\Omega_{\mathbb P^n_R/R}\to\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus(n+1)}\to\mathcal O\to0$.
cards.source: Standard (SGA 7 XVII 5.1; Hartshorne II 8.13). In the compiled Stacks library: `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjEulerSequence.shortExact_eulerSequence`. Used over $R=\mathbb Z$ and pulled back to $\mathbb P^n_Y$.

cards.title: Flat pullback of the fundamental class of a smooth scheme
cards.summary: f^*[X] = [Y] for a flat f : Y → X of relative dimension r over a smooth X.
cards.statement: Let $X$ be smooth over $k$ and $f:Y\to X$ a flat morphism of relative dimension $r$, with $Y$ locally of finite type over $k$. Then flat pullback sends the fundamental class of $X$ to that of $Y$: $f^*[X]_m=[Y]_{m+r}$ for every $m$ ($X$ need not be equidimensional). In particular $\pi^*[Y]=[\mathbb P^n_Y]$ for the projection $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ over a smooth $Y$.
cards.source: Stacks proves this as `Stacks.WeilCohomology.flatPullbackChow_fundamentalChowClass_of_smooth` in the module `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/WeilCohomology/Concrete/ProjectiveBundleDiagonal`, which is not compiled on this machine; its proof is reproduced from that module, using compiled modules only, in `GRR/ProjectionTau.lean` (`flatPullbackChow_fundamentalChowClass_smooth` and four helper lemmas), where it compiles.

cards.title: $\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n_Y})=\pi^*\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\cdot Q(h)^{n+1}$
cards.summary: The Todd class of projective space over Y, from the Euler sequence.
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ the projection and $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. Then in $A^*(\mathbb P^n_Y)_{\mathbb Q}$: $\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n_Y})=\pi^*\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\cdot Q(h)^{n+1}$, where $Q(h)$ is the value of the Todd series at $h$.
cards.proof: Since $\pi$ is smooth the relative cotangent sequence $0\to\pi^*\Omega_{Y/k}\to\Omega_{\mathbb P^n_Y/k}\to\Omega_{\mathbb P^n_Y/Y}\to0$ is short exact, so $[\Omega_{\mathbb P^n_Y/k}]=\pi^*[\Omega_{Y/k}]+[\Omega_{\mathbb P^n_Y/Y}]$ in $K_0(\mathrm{Vect})$. The Euler sequence on $\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb Z}$ gives $[\Omega_{\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb Z}/\mathbb Z}]=(n+1)[\mathcal O(-1)]-1$; pulling back along $\mathbb P^n_Y\to\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb Z}$ and using base change of differentials, $[\Omega_{\mathbb P^n_Y/Y}]=(n+1)[\mathcal O(-1)]-1$. Apply $\operatorname{ch}$ and the sign rule for duals, which multiplies the component of degree $p$ by $(-1)^p$ and so sends $\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal O(-1)]=e^{-h}$ to $e^{h}=\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal O(1)]$: $\operatorname{ch}[T_{\mathbb P^n_Y}]=\pi^*\operatorname{ch}[T_Y]+(n+1)\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal O(1)]-1$. Apply the Todd operation: it is multiplicative, compatible with pullback, $\operatorname{td}(1)=1$ because $\operatorname{ch}(1)$ has only a degree-$0$ component, and $\operatorname{td}[\mathcal O(1)]=Q(h)$.

leanReading.note: toddTangent k (π ≫ sY) = pullbackAQ along π of toddTangent k sY, times (ev (firstChernQ (twistOver n Y 1)) toddSeries)^(n+1), the power applied to the evaluated series; only IsSmoothFT k sY is assumed.

cards.attack: ℙ¹: Q(h)² ≡ 1 + h; ℙ²: Q(h)³ ≡ 1 + 3h/2 + h²; ℙ³: 1 + 2h + 11h²/6 + h³ — equal to the Todd polynomials c₁/2, (c₁²+c₂)/12, c₁c₂/24 with c_i = C(n+1, i)hⁱ, and ∫td = 1; over Y = ℙ¹, td = (1+u)Q(h)^{n+1} gives χ(𝒪(a,b)) = (a+1)χ(ℙⁿ, 𝒪(b)) for |a| ≤ 4, |b| ≤ 5, n = 1, 2.

cards.title: Integration over the fibres of $\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ the projection and $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. For every power series $F\in\mathbb Q[[t]]$ and every $c\in A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$: $\pi_*\big((\pi^*c\cdot F(h))\cap[\mathbb P^n_Y]\big)=F_n\cdot(c\cap[Y])$ in $CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$, where $F_n$ is the coefficient of $t^n$ in $F$.
cards.proof: By the projection formula and because the cap product is an action, it suffices to show $\pi_*\big(F(h)\cap[\mathbb P^n_Y]\big)=F_n\,[Y]$. Since $h$ is homogeneous of degree one, $F(h)\cap\gamma=\sum_mF_m\,h^m\cap\gamma$ (a finite sum on each class), and $[\mathbb P^n_Y]=\pi^*[Y]$. For the projective tower $\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ with $\mathcal O(1)$: $\pi_*(h^m\cap\pi^*\beta)=0$ for $m<n$ and $=\beta$ for $m=n$ (Stacks 02TW), and $h^{n+1}$ acts as zero on $CH_*(\mathbb P^n_Y)_{\mathbb Q}$, so the terms with $m>n$ vanish as well.

leanReading.note: For arbitrary F and c, the pushforward along π of cap (π^*c · F(h)) [ℙⁿ_Y] equals coeff n F • cap c [Y], with h = firstChernQ of O(1) and the factors in the card's order; only IsSmoothFT k sY is assumed.

cards.attack: Over a point (n = 1, 2, 3) π_*(F(h)∩[ℙⁿ]) = F_n gives ∫e^{dh}Q^{n+1} = C(n+d, n) = (d+1)…(d+n)/n! for every |d| ≤ 9, negative d included; over Y = ℙ¹ with c = 2/3 − (5/7)u and F_k = (k²−3)/(k+2), π_*((π^*c·F(h))∩[P]) = F_n·c exactly.

cards.title: Exterior powers and the top Chern class
cards.summary: Λ^p E for an O_X-module, and c_r(E) as a class of degree r.
cards.statement: For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$, $\Lambda^p\mathcal E$ is its $p$-th exterior power (Stacks). For $\mathcal E$ finite locally free of constant rank $r$ on $X$ locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology, $c(\mathcal E)\in\prod_pA^p(X)$ is the total Chern class of Stacks (components $c_j(\mathcal E)$, $j\le r$), and the top Chern class $c_r(\mathcal E)$ is its homogeneous component of degree $r$, viewed as a total class concentrated in degree $r$.

leanReading.note: exteriorPower F n is the degree-n piece of the sheaf exterior algebra (indexed by ℤ, harmless); totalChern is Stacks' total Chern class of a module of rank r and homComponent r its part of degree r as a total class.

cards.title: The Koszul identity for Chern characters
cards.statement: Let $X$ be locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology and $\mathcal Q$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of constant rank $r$, with dual $\mathcal Q^\vee$. Then in $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$: $$\sum_{p=0}^{r}(-1)^p\operatorname{ch}\big[\Lambda^p(\mathcal Q^\vee)\big]=c_r(\mathcal Q)\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal Q]),$$ where $c_r(\mathcal Q)$ is the image in $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ of the top Chern class of $\mathcal Q$.
cards.proof: Both sides are compatible with pullback, and pullback to a splitting space is injective on $A^*_{\mathbb Q}$ (Stacks' splitting principle for integral classes and flatness of $\mathbb Q$), so one may assume that $V=\mathcal Q^\vee$ has a filtration with invertible quotients $L_1,\dots,L_r$. For an extension $0\to N\to V\to V'\to0$ with $N$ invertible, $[\Lambda^{p+1}V]=[N][\Lambda^pV']+[\Lambda^{p+1}V']$ (Stacks), hence $\lambda_{-1}(V):=\sum_p(-1)^p[\Lambda^pV]=(1-[N])\lambda_{-1}(V')$ and, by induction, $\lambda_{-1}(V)=\prod_i(1-[L_i])$. In rank one, with $h=c_1(L^\vee)=-c_1(L)$: $\operatorname{ch}(1-[L])\operatorname{td}[L^\vee]=(1-e^{-h})Q(h)=h=-c_1(L)$. All the classes commute and the Todd class is multiplicative, so $\operatorname{ch}(\lambda_{-1}V)\operatorname{td}[V^\vee]=\prod_i(-c_1(L_i))=(-1)^rc_r(V)$ by the Whitney formula. Now $V=\mathcal Q^\vee$: $c_r(\mathcal Q^\vee)=(-1)^rc_r(\mathcal Q)$, and $\operatorname{td}[\mathcal Q^{\vee\vee}]=\operatorname{td}[\mathcal Q]$ by the sign rule for $\operatorname{ch}$ applied twice. So $\operatorname{ch}(\lambda_{-1}\mathcal Q^\vee)\operatorname{td}[\mathcal Q]=c_r(\mathcal Q)$; multiply by $\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal Q])$.

leanReading.note: For any Chow situation and Q of rank r: ∑_{p ∈ range (r+1)} (−1)^p ch[Λ^p (dualSheaf Q)] = ofTotalChowClass (homComponent r (totalChern Q r)) · td(−[Q]); no hypothesis beyond the card's.

cards.attack: With Chern roots x₁..x_r of 𝒬 (r ≤ 3, exact through total degree 7), Σ(−1)^p e_p(e^{−x_i}) = Πx_i·Π(1−e^{−x_i})/x_i holds, and every sign is forced: Λ^p𝒬 instead of Λ^p𝒬^∨ fails for r ≥ 1, c_r(𝒬^∨) instead of c_r(𝒬) fails for r = 1, 3 (agrees for even r), td(+[𝒬]) and td(−[𝒬^∨]) fail, r = 0 gives 1 = 1.

cards.title: Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch from (E) alone
cards.summary: With the projection case proved, GRR for projective morphisms follows from (E).
cards.statement: Suppose (E) holds for every closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$. Then the Riemann–Roch formula holds for every projective morphism $f:X\to Y$ over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.
cards.proof: A projective morphism is proper, so the Riemann–Roch formula is defined for it. (P1), (P2) and (P3) are proved for every $Y$ and $n$; insert them in the reduction of the whole theorem to (E), (P1), (P2), (P3).

leanReading.note: The hypothesis is exactly ClosedImmersionFormula for every closed immersion over k between IsSmoothFT schemes, and nothing else; the conclusion is RiemannRochFor for every f with IsProjectiveMorphism f.

cards.attack: Logic: assembly needs (E) for all closed immersions of smooth schemes and (P1)–(P3) for all (Y, n); the hypothesis supplies the first and the three proposition cards the rest, so the quantifiers match and nothing is assumed beyond the hypothesis. Two silent points, neither a gap: 'projective' must give 'proper' for the formula to be defined (now cited), and the hypothesis is stronger than used (only (E) for closed immersions into some ℙⁿ_Y is needed).

cards.title: Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch on projective space
cards.summary: χ(P^n_k, α) = ∫ ch(α)·td(T) on projective space, unconditionally.
cards.statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$ and $s:\mathbb P^n_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the structure morphism. For every $\alpha\in K_0(\mathbb P^n_k)$: $s_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n_k}))\cap[\mathbb P^n_k]\big)=\chi(\mathbb P^n_k,\alpha)\cdot[\operatorname{Spec}k]$ in $CH_*(\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathbb Q}$.
cards.proof: $\mathbb P^n_k$ is smooth, separated, of finite type and proper over $k$. $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, so the Riemann–Roch formula holds for the projection $\mathbb P^n_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is the structure morphism. Apply the card deducing Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch from the formula for the structure morphism.

leanReading.note: For ℙⁿ_k = projectiveSpaceOver n (Spec k) with structure map s: the pushforward along s of tau k s α equals (eulerK k s α : ℚ) • [Spec k], with eulerK the alternating sum of dim_k H^i(ℙⁿ_k, −); no hypothesis.

cards.attack: Checked HRR on ℙⁿ_k exactly: ∫e^{dh}Q(h)^{n+1} = χ(𝒪(d)) for n = 1, 2, 3 and |d| ≤ 9 (negative d through hⁿ), and ∫(1−e^{−h})^{n−m}Q^{n+1} = 1 = χ(𝒪_{ℙ^m}) for every linear subspace m ≤ n. Logic: grr-projection with Y = Spec k (smooth by rr-point) gives the formula for π = s, then hrr-from-grr.

cards.title: Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch from (E)
cards.summary: HRR for a smooth projective X follows from (E).
cards.statement: Suppose (E) holds for every closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$. Let $X$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ with projective structure morphism $s_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Then for every $\alpha\in K_0(X)$: $(s_X)_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_X))\cap[X]\big)=\chi(X,\alpha)\cdot[\operatorname{Spec}k]$ in $CH_*(\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathbb Q}$.
cards.proof: The projective morphism $s_X$ is proper, so $\chi(X,-)$ is defined. Under the hypothesis the Riemann–Roch formula holds for the projective morphism $s_X$ onto the point, which is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$; apply the card deducing Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch from the formula for the structure morphism.

leanReading.note: The hypothesis is exactly (E) for every closed immersion between IsSmoothFT schemes over k; the conclusion holds for every X with IsSmoothFT k sX and IsProjectiveMorphism sX: (sX)_* τ_X(α) = χ(X, α)·[Spec k].

cards.attack: Logic: grr-from-e with Y = Spec k (smooth by rr-point) and f = s_X gives the formula for s_X, and hrr-from-grr turns it into HRR; quantifiers are fine and the conclusion is true (it is HRR). Silent step, now cited: hrr-from-grr, and χ itself, need X proper over k, i.e. projective ⇒ proper for s_X (closed immersion followed by the proper ℙⁿ_k → Spec k).

cards.title: The tangent sheaf is a vector bundle
cards.summary: T_X is finite locally free for smooth X, so [T_X] is its class.
cards.statement: For $X$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, the tangent sheaf $T_X$ is finite locally free.
cards.proof: The sheaf of differentials of a smooth morphism is finite locally free, and so is the dual of a finite locally free module.

leanReading.note: For sX with IsSmoothFT k sX, tangentSheaf k sX (the dual of Ω_{X/k}) is IsFiniteLocallyFree; no extra hypothesis.

hypotheses.text: $X$ is smooth over $k$.
$X$ is separated and quasi-compact over $k$.
hypotheses.redundant: Never used: smoothness alone makes $\Omega_{X/k}$ finite locally free. Smoothness itself is needed: on the node $xy=0$ the tangent sheaf is $k[x]\oplus k[y]$, of fibre dimension $2$ at the origin and rank $1$ elsewhere.

cards.attack: Dropping smoothness breaks it: for the node A = k[x,y]/(xy), Der_k(A) = A·x∂_x ⊕ A·y∂_y ≅ k[x] ⊕ k[y] has fibre dimension 2 at the origin but rank 1 on each branch, so T_X is not locally free. Separatedness and quasi-compactness are never used (smooth over k suffices), so those hypotheses are redundant but harmless. The two-line proof is complete.

cards.title: Projective morphisms are proper
cards.summary: A closed immersion into P^n_S followed by the projection is proper.
cards.statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes that factors as a closed immersion $X\to\mathbb P^n_S$ followed by the projection $\mathbb P^n_S\to S$. Then $f$ is proper.
cards.source: Stacks Project, Tag 01W8 (H-projective morphisms) with the properness of $\mathbb P^n_S\to S$; in the compiled Stacks library `AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_of_isProjectiveMorphism` (module `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Proper/Projective`). Used so that $f_!$, $f_*$ and $\chi$ are defined for a projective morphism; the Lean statements that take a projective morphism carry properness as a separate instance.

cards.title: Higher direct images of the twists on $\mathbb P^n_Y$
cards.summary: R^iπ_*O(−j) = 0 for 1 ≤ j ≤ n, R^iπ_*O = 0 for i ≥ 1, π_*O = O_Y.
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme, $n\ge0$ and $\pi:\mathbb P^n_Y\to Y$ the projection. Then $R^i\pi_*\mathcal O(-j)=0$ for every $i\ge0$ when $1\le j\le n$; $R^i\pi_*\mathcal O=0$ for $i\ge1$; and $\pi_*\mathcal O\cong\mathcal O_Y$.

cards.title: The projective bundle formula along a projective tower
cards.summary: Classes on P are sums of c_1(L)^i ∩ π^*β_i, i ≤ n (surjectivity only).
cards.statement: Let $\pi:P\to U$ be a projective tower of fibre dimension $n$ with invertible sheaf $L$ in the sense of Stacks (for instance $\mathbb P^n_U\to U$ with $\mathcal O(1)$), with $P$ and $U$ locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology. Then for every $k$ the map $\bigoplus_{i=0}^nCH_{k-n+i}(U)\to CH_k(P)$, $(\beta_i)\mapsto\sum_ic_1(L)^i\cap\pi^*\beta_i$, is surjective. The same holds when $\pi$ is such a tower locally on $U$, for instance for the projective bundle $\mathbb P(\mathcal V)\to U$ of a finite locally free module $\mathcal V$ of constant rank $n+1$, with $L=\mathcal O(1)$.

cards.title: Pushing forward powers of the hyperplane class
cards.summary: π_*(c_1(L)^m ∩ π^*β) is 0 for m < n and β for m = n.
cards.statement: Let $\pi:P\to U$ be a projective tower of fibre dimension $n$ with invertible sheaf $L$ in the sense of Stacks, $\pi$ proper, and $\beta\in CH_k(U)$. Then $\pi_*\big(c_1(L)^m\cap\pi^*\beta\big)=0$ for $m<n$ and $=\beta$ for $m=n$. The same holds for the projective bundle $\mathbb P(\mathcal V)\to U$ of a finite locally free module $\mathcal V$ of constant rank $n+1$, with $L=\mathcal O(1)$.

cards.title: The Gysin map commutes with the Chern character
cards.summary: f^!(ch(a) ∩ β) = ch(f^*a) ∩ f^!β and f^![Y] = [X] between smooth schemes.
cards.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism over $k$ between Noetherian schemes smooth over $k$. For $a\in\mathbb Q\otimes K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$ and $\beta\in CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$: $f^!\big(\operatorname{ch}(a)\cap\beta\big)=\operatorname{ch}(f^*a)\cap f^!\beta$, and $f^![Y]=[X]$.

cards.title: The Chern character of a perfect complex
cards.summary: ch(K) has p-th component P_p(K)/p!, for K in D(O_Y) with defined Chern classes.
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology and $K\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ an object whose Chern classes are defined in the sense of Stacks (Tag 0F9E). Its **Chern character** is the element $\operatorname{ch}(K)\in A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}=\prod_pA^p(Y)\otimes\mathbb Q$ whose $p$-th component is $\frac1{p!}\otimes P_p(K)$, where $P_p(K)\in A^p(Y)$ is the $p$-th power sum class of $K$ of Stacks.

leanReading.note: Body: RationalTotalChowClass.ofFamily (an identity equivalence) of Stacks.Chow.perfectChernCharacter C sY hK, whose p-th component is (p!)⁻¹ ⊗ perfectPowerSum C sY hK p p, the class P_p(K) ∈ A^p(Y) of Stacks 0F9E(2).

cards.title: Properties of the Chern character of perfect complexes
cards.summary: Invariant under isomorphism, zero on 0, compatible with pullback, equal to ch[M] on M[0], multiplicative on derived tensor products.
cards.statement:
Let $Y$ be locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology and let $K,K',E,F\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ have defined Chern classes.

1. If $K\cong K'$ then $\operatorname{ch}(K)=\operatorname{ch}(K')$.
2. If $K$ is a zero object then $\operatorname{ch}(K)=0$.
3. For $g:Y'\to Y$ locally of finite type, $g^*\operatorname{ch}(K)=\operatorname{ch}(Lg^*K)$.
4. If $K\cong M[0]$ with $M$ a finite locally free module, then $\operatorname{ch}(K)=\operatorname{ch}[M]$, the Chern character of the class of $M$ in $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$.
5. If $E\otimes^LF$ has defined Chern classes, then $\operatorname{ch}(E\otimes^{L}F)=\operatorname{ch}(E)\cdot\operatorname{ch}(F)$.
cards.proof: Each item is the corresponding statement of Stacks on the power sum classes, divided by $p!$. For 1 and 2: $P_p$ is invariant under isomorphism and vanishes on zero objects. For 3: $P_p(Lg^*K)$ is the restriction of $P_p(K)$ along $g$, and $g^*$ on $A^*_{\mathbb Q}$ is restriction in each degree. For 4: $P_p(K)$ is the $p$-th power sum of the Chern classes of $M$, and $\frac1{p!}$ times it is the $p$-th component of $\operatorname{ch}[M]$ by the definition of the Chern character on $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,Y)$. For 5: $P_m(E\otimes^LF)=\sum_{a+b=m}\binom maP_a(E)P_b(F)$; divide by $m!$ and use $\binom ma\frac1{m!}=\frac1{a!}\cdot\frac1{b!}$: the result is the degree-$m$ component of the product $\operatorname{ch}(E)\operatorname{ch}(F)$ in $\prod_pA^p(Y)\otimes\mathbb Q$.
cards.attack: Checked on a point and on P^1 (ch O(a)·ch O(b) = ch O(a+b); pullback to a point), and exactly in Python: C(m,a)/m! = 1/(a!b!) for m ≤ 14, and the product formula for power sums on 200 random sets of Chern roots and 100 virtual classes, no failure. No commutativity of bivariant classes is used. 'Defined Chern classes' is needed (O_node on a nodal curve is not perfect). Redundant: in item 5 the hypothesis on E⊗F follows from those on E and F, in item 1 the one on K' follows from K ≅ K'. Item 3 silently uses that Lg^*K again has defined Chern classes. Not broken.

leanReading.note: Item 1 is perfectCh_congr; 2 is perfectCh_eq_zero (IsZero K); 3 is pullbackAQ_perfectCh, where pullbackAQ is restriction along g and the elided proof is hK.derivedPullback g, so the right side is ch(Lg^*K); 4 is perfectCh_single; 5 is perfectCh_derivedTensor.

cards.title: The Chern character of a coherent sheaf is that of its perfect complex
cards.summary: On a smooth Y, ch[F] = ch(F[0]) for every coherent F.
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module. Then $\mathcal F[0]\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ has defined Chern classes, and for every $K\cong\mathcal F[0]$ with defined Chern classes, $\operatorname{ch}([\mathcal F])=\operatorname{ch}(K)$: the left side is the Chern character of the class of $\mathcal F$ in $K_0(Y)$ (defined through $\theta^{-1}$), the right side the Chern character of the perfect complex $K$.
cards.proof: $Y$ is regular, quasi-compact and has affine diagonal. By Stacks there are a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite locally free modules with $\mathcal F[0]\cong E^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal O_Y)$ and $\theta^{-1}[\mathcal F]=\sum_n(-1)^n[E^n]$. In particular $\mathcal F[0]$ is perfect, and on the quasi-compact $Y$ its Chern classes are defined (Stacks 0GUE). For $K\cong\mathcal F[0]\cong E^\bullet$, the power sum classes of $K$ are those of $\sum_n(-1)^n[E^n]$ (Remark 0FEU), so $\operatorname{ch}(K)=\operatorname{ch}\big(\sum_n(-1)^n[E^n]\big)=\operatorname{ch}(\theta^{-1}[\mathcal F])$, which is $\operatorname{ch}([\mathcal F])$ by definition.
cards.attack: Computed on P^1 and P^2: O_p gives 1 − e^{−h} = [pt]; a line and a point of P^2 through their Koszul resolutions; I_p by additivity. Smoothness is needed (O_node on a nodal curve is not perfect). Separatedness is needed for θ to be onto: on the plane with doubled origin a skyscraper at one origin is not in the image of θ. Found unlisted inputs, now cited: perfect on a quasi-compact scheme has defined Chern classes (Stacks 0GUE(4)); the card on θ was listed but not used (removed). Not broken.

leanReading.note: hasDefinedChernClasses_single_coherent: for Y with IsSmoothFT k sY (smooth, separated, quasi-compact over k) and F coherent, F[0] has defined Chern classes; chK_mk_eq_perfectCh: chK [F] = perfectCh hK for every K ≅ F[0] with defined Chern classes.

cards.title: (E) follows from its case of vector bundles
cards.summary: It suffices to prove (E) on the classes of finite locally free E, where ch(i_! θ[E]) is the Chern character of (i_*E)[0].
cards.statement:
Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, with normal sheaf $N$.

(a) For a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ and every $K\cong(i_*\mathcal E)[0]$ in $D(\mathcal O_P)$ with defined Chern classes, $\operatorname{ch}(i_!\,\theta[\mathcal E])=\operatorname{ch}(K)$.

(b) If for every finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ $$\operatorname{ch}(i_!\,\theta[\mathcal E])\cap[P]=i_*\big((\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal E]\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[N]))\cap[X]\big),$$ then (E) holds for $i$.
cards.proof:
(a) $\theta[\mathcal E]$ is the class of $\mathcal E$ as a coherent sheaf, and $i_!$ of it is $[i_*\mathcal E]$, a closed immersion having no higher direct images. Apply the previous card to the coherent sheaf $i_*\mathcal E$ on $P$.

(b) Both sides of (E) are additive in $\alpha\in K_0(X)$. The map $\theta$ is onto and $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$ is generated by the classes $[\mathcal E]$ of finite locally free modules, so it suffices to check (E) on $\alpha=\theta[\mathcal E]$, where $\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)=\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal E]$.
cards.attack: Target formula checked exactly on P^2 for curves of degree 1..5 with O(d), |d| ≤ 4, and for points; X = P and X = ∅ trivial. (a): θ[E] = [E], i_![E] = [i_*E], then the bridge on P for the coherent i_*E. (b): both sides are homomorphisms on K_0(X) and θ is bijective, so agreement on the classes [E] suffices; bijectivity of θ was used without being listed (now rests on the definition of ch). X smooth and P smooth are both needed. Not broken.

leanReading.note: (a) is chK_pushforwardK_classOf_eq_perfectCh: chK(i_! θ[E]) = ch(K) for E finite locally free and every K ≅ (i_*E)[0] with defined Chern classes (it does not even assume i ≫ sP = sX); (b) is closedImmersionFormula_of_bundles.

cards.title: The blowup at infinity of a closed immersion
cards.summary: Stacks' deformation space W: its fibre over 0, W_∞ = E + X', the closed immersion P^1_X → W, and E = P(C ⊕ O).
cards.statement:
Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion of schemes over $k$ and $W$ the blowup of $\mathbb P^1_P$ in $\infty(X)$, the copy of $X$ in the fibre over $\infty$, with $b:W\to\mathbb P^1_P$.

1. $b$ is an isomorphism over $\mathbb A^1_P$; in particular the fibre of $W$ over $0$ maps isomorphically to $P$.
2. The fibre $W_\infty$ over $\infty$ is an effective Cartier divisor of $W$, and its ideal is the product of the ideal of the exceptional divisor and the ideal of the strict transform $X'$ of $\{\infty\}\times P$.
3. The inclusion $\mathbb P^1_X\to\mathbb P^1_P$ lifts to a closed immersion $i':\mathbb P^1_X\to W$. Its image does not meet $X'$. The square formed by $i'$, the inclusion $W_\infty\times_PX\to W$, the section $\infty:X\to\mathbb P^1_X$ and the vertex $X\to W_\infty\times_PX$ of the normal cone is cartesian, and $\mathbb P^1_X$ and $W_\infty\times_PX$ are Tor independent over $W$.
4. If $i$ is a regular immersion and $X$ is locally Noetherian, there is a canonical isomorphism $\varphi$ over $X$ from $W_\infty\times_PX$ to the projective completion $\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X)$ of the normal bundle, $\mathcal C$ being the dual of the normal bundle. If moreover the conormal module has constant rank, $\varphi$ composed with the vertex, and the zero section $\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X)$, are closed immersions with the same ideal sheaf.
cards.source: Stacks Project, Tags 0FBG and 0F9K (Chow homology: blowing up at infinity). In the compiled Stacks library (namespace `Stacks.Chow`): `blowupAtInfinity`, `isIso_pullback_snd_blowupAtInfinityToProjectiveLineProduct`, `fibreIdealAtInfinity_eq_mul_strictTransformIdealAtInfinity`, `lineToBlowupAtInfinity`, `comap_strictTransformIdealAtInfinity_lineToBlowupAtInfinity`, `isPullback_vertex_lineToBlowupAtInfinity`, `torIndependent_lineToBlowupAtInfinity_exceptionalFibre`, `exceptionalFibreIsoProjectiveCompletion`, `ker_vertex_comp_exceptionalDivisorIsoProjectiveCompletion_hom` (from the proof of Tag 0FEG). Used for the deformation to the normal cone.

cards.title: The deformation space $W$ and the complex $Q$
cards.summary: W is the blowup of P^1_P in ∞(X), with q, i_0, e, a; and Q = (i'_* pr^* E)[0].
cards.statement:
Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion of schemes over $k$ and $\mathcal E$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module.

- $W$ is the blowup of $\mathbb P^1_P$ in $\infty(X)$ (Stacks' blowup at infinity of the ideal of $i$), with $b:W\to\mathbb P^1_P$.
- $q:W\to P$ is $b$ followed by the projection $\mathbb P^1_P\to P$.
- $i_0:P\to W$ is the **section at zero**: the inverse of the isomorphism from the fibre of $W$ over $0$ to $P$, followed by the inclusion of that fibre.
- $e:W_\infty\times_PX\to W$ is the first projection followed by the inclusion of the fibre $W_\infty$ over $\infty$; its source is the **exceptional divisor**, read as $W_\infty\times_PX$.
- $a:X'\to W$ is the inclusion of the **strict transform** $X'$ of $\{\infty\}\times P$ into $W_\infty$, followed by $W_\infty\to W$.
- $\operatorname{pr}:\mathbb P^1_X\to X$ is the projection, $X$ being identified with the closed subscheme of $P$ cut out by the ideal of $i$.
- $Q=\big(i'_*\operatorname{pr}^*\mathcal E\big)[0]\in D(\mathcal O_W)$, where $i':\mathbb P^1_X\to W$ is the closed immersion of Stacks lifting $\mathbb P^1_X\to\mathbb P^1_P$.

leanReading.note: Bodies agree with the Stacks objects: W = blowupAtInfinity (ker i), the blowup of P^1_P in ∞(V(ker i)); proj = b followed by the projection to P, with b landing in P ×_k P^1_k (a canonical identification); the other five bodies were traced to the Stacks terms.

cards.title: The deformation space is smooth and $i$ is a regular immersion
cards.summary: W is again smooth, separated and of finite type over k; a closed immersion of smooth schemes is regular.
cards.statement: Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$. Then (a) $W$, with structure morphism $W\xrightarrow{q}P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$; (b) $i$ is a regular immersion.
cards.proof:
(a) $\mathbb P^1_P$ and $\infty(X)\cong X$ are smooth over $k$ and $\infty(X)\to\mathbb P^1_P$ is a closed immersion, so the blowup $W$ of $\mathbb P^1_P$ in $\infty(X)$ is smooth over $k$ (Stacks 0FUT, `smooth_blowUpToBase_comp`). The morphism $q$ is separated and quasi-compact (it is proper: a blowup of a Noetherian scheme followed by $\mathbb P^1_P\to P$), and so is $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; hence so is their composition.

(b) A closed immersion between schemes smooth over a base is a regular immersion (Stacks 067U, `isRegularImmersion_of_smooth_of_smooth`).
cards.attack: Worked out W for a point in A^1 (two charts A^2), X = P, X = ∅, a point in a surface. X smooth is needed: X = V(x^2) in A^1 gives an A_1 singularity on W. 'Over k' is needed for (a): k = F_p(t), X = V(x^p − t) in A^1 with another smooth structure map gives W regular but not smooth over k. (b) fails for V(x^2, xy) in A^2. The proof's inputs (Stacks 0FUT, 067U) were not among its sources; now cited. Not broken.

leanReading.note: (a) isSmoothFT_blowupAtInfinity: for X, P with IsSmoothFT, i a closed immersion and i ≫ sP = sX, IsSmoothFT k (proj sP i ≫ sP); (b) isRegularImmersion_of_isSmoothFT gives Stacks' IsRegularImmersion i under the same hypotheses.

cards.title: Derived base change for Tor independent squares
cards.summary: Lf^* Rj_* K → Ri'_* Lg^* K is an isomorphism for a closed immersion j Tor independent of f.
cards.statement: Consider a cartesian square of schemes with $j:Z\to X$ a closed immersion, $f:X'\to X$ any morphism, and base changes $i':Z'\to X'$, $g:Z'\to Z$, such that $Z$ and $X'$ are Tor independent over $X$. Then for every $K\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ the base change map $Lf^*Rj_*K\to Ri'_*Lg^*K$ is an isomorphism.
cards.source: Stacks Project, Tag 0E23 (with the base change map of Tag 08HY). In the compiled Stacks library `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedBaseChangeIsoOfTorIndependent` (module `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/PseudoCoherent/RelativeTorIndependentBaseChange`). Used with $K=\mathcal G[0]$ for a flat module $\mathcal G$.

cards.title: Base change of a flat module pushed forward along a closed immersion
cards.summary: Lf^*((j_*G)[0]) ≅ (i'_* g^* G)[0] in a Tor independent cartesian square, G flat.
cards.statement: Consider a cartesian square of schemes with $j:Z\to X$ a closed immersion, $f:X'\to X$ any morphism, and base changes $i':Z'\to X'$, $g:Z'\to Z$, such that $Z$ and $X'$ are Tor independent over $X$. For every flat $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ there is an isomorphism $Lf^*\big((j_*\mathcal G)[0]\big)\cong\big(i'_*g^*\mathcal G\big)[0]$ in $D(\mathcal O_{X'})$.
cards.proof: Apply derived base change for Tor independent squares to $K=\mathcal G[0]$: $Lf^*Rj_*(\mathcal G[0])\cong Ri'_*Lg^*(\mathcal G[0])$. Since $j$ and its base change $i'$ are closed immersions, their pushforwards are exact, so $Rj_*$ and $Ri'_*$ of a module placed in degree $0$ are its pushforward placed in degree $0$. Since $\mathcal G$ is flat, $Lg^*(\mathcal G[0])=(g^*\mathcal G)[0]$.
cards.attack: Checked on A^1 with f: t ↦ t^2 and G = k. Re-derived the cited base change on stalks, so no quasi-coherence is needed. Flatness of G is needed (Z = X = A^1, X' = {0}, G = k[t]/(t) gives k ⊕ k[1]); Tor independence is needed (Z = X' = {0} in A^1 gives k ⊕ k[1]). Each step of the proof holds. Not broken.

leanReading.note: IsPullback i' g f j makes Z' = X' ×_X Z with projections i' and g; the hypotheses are IsClosedImmersion j, TorIndependent j f and IsFlat G, and the output is the isomorphism Lf^*((j_*G)[0]) ≅ (i'_*(g^*G))[0], given as data.

cards.title: $Q$ restricts to $i_*\mathcal E$ on the fibre over $0$
cards.statement: Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion of schemes over $k$ and $\mathcal E$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module. For the section at zero $i_0:P\to W$ there is an isomorphism $Li_0^*Q\cong(i_*\mathcal E)[0]$ in $D(\mathcal O_P)$.
cards.proof: Let $U=b^{-1}(\mathbb A^1_P)$, an open subscheme of $W$ with inclusion $c$. Over $\mathbb A^1_P$ the blowup is an isomorphism, so $q\circ c:U\to P$ is flat and $i'^{-1}(U)=X\times_PU$. For a closed immersion the base change map $f^*i_*\mathcal E\to i'_*g^*\mathcal E$ is an isomorphism for every module $\mathcal E$ and every $f$, as one checks on stalks. Applied to $i$ and the flat morphism $q\circ c$, both the restriction $Lc^*Q=Q|_U$ and $L(qc)^*\big((i_*\mathcal E)[0]\big)=\big((qc)^*i_*\mathcal E\big)[0]$ are the pushforward to $U$ of the pullback of $\mathcal E$ to $X\times_PU$, placed in degree $0$. The section $i_0$ factors as $\sigma:P\to U$ followed by $c$, with $q\circ c\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_P$. Hence $Li_0^*Q\cong L\sigma^*Lc^*Q\cong L\sigma^*L(qc)^*\big((i_*\mathcal E)[0]\big)\cong(i_*\mathcal E)[0]$.
cards.attack: Checked for a point in A^1, for A^1 in A^2 with a non-flat E, for X = P and X = ∅. i'^{-1}(U) = X ×_P U holds as a cartesian square, from the cited items. No hypothesis on E is needed: for a closed immersion the base change map is an isomorphism for every module (stalks); the textbook flat base change is only for quasi-coherent modules, so the proof now says which form it uses. Not broken.

leanReading.note: deformationZeroFibreIso gives L(sectionAtZero sP i)^*(Q i E) ≅ (i_*E)[0] in D(O_P) for every O_X-module E, with i a closed immersion and P over k through sP. The isomorphism is data, and no k-structure on X is used (harmless generality).

cards.title: $Q$ restricts to the zero-section sheaf on the exceptional divisor
cards.summary: L e^* Q ≅ Lφ^*((s_* ρ^* E)[0]) on the exceptional divisor, identified with P(C ⊕ O).
cards.statement: Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion of schemes over $k$ that is a regular immersion, with $X$ locally Noetherian and conormal module of constant rank $r$, and let $\mathcal E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module. Let $e:D\to W$ be the exceptional divisor $D=W_\infty\times_PX$, $\overline P=\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X)$ the projective completion of the normal bundle ($\mathcal C$ the dual of the normal bundle of $i$), $\varphi:D\to\overline P$ the canonical isomorphism of Stacks (Tag 0F9K), $s:\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)\to\overline P$ the zero section and $\rho:\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)\to X$ the projection. Then there is an isomorphism $Le^*Q\cong L\varphi^*\big((s_*\rho^*\mathcal E)[0]\big)$ in $D(\mathcal O_D)$.
cards.proof:
Let $v:X\to D$ be the vertex of the normal cone. The square formed by $v$, the section $\infty:X\to\mathbb P^1_X$, $i'$ and $e$ is cartesian, and $\mathbb P^1_X$ and $D$ are Tor independent over $W$ (Stacks). The module $\operatorname{pr}^*\mathcal E$ is finite locally free, hence flat, so by the previous base change lemma $Le^*Q\cong(v_*\infty^*\operatorname{pr}^*\mathcal E)[0]\cong(v_*\mathcal E)[0]$, because $\operatorname{pr}\circ\infty=\mathrm{id}_X$.

Under the canonical $\varphi$ the vertex is the zero section: $\varphi\circ v$ and $s$ are closed immersions with the same ideal (Stacks, from the proof of Tag 0FEG), so $\varphi\circ v=s\circ\vartheta$ for an isomorphism $\vartheta:X\to\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)$, and $\rho\circ\vartheta=\mathrm{id}_X$. The square formed by $v$, $\vartheta$, $\varphi$ and $s$ is cartesian, its vertical maps being isomorphisms, and $\varphi$ is flat. As $\rho^*\mathcal E$ is flat, the same lemma gives $L\varphi^*\big((s_*\rho^*\mathcal E)[0]\big)\cong(v_*\vartheta^*\rho^*\mathcal E)[0]\cong(v_*\mathcal E)[0]$. Compose the two isomorphisms.

hypotheses.text: $i$ is a regular immersion and $X$ is locally Noetherian.
The conormal module of $i$ has constant rank $r$.
hypotheses.redundant: Not needed for the statement: $X$ is the disjoint union of the open and closed loci where the rank is constant, and $D$ lies over $X$, so both sides decompose accordingly. It is kept because the Stacks lemma that identifies the vertex with the zero section is stated for constant rank.

hypotheses.text: $\mathcal E$ is finite locally free.
hypotheses.redundant: The statement holds for every $\mathcal O_X$-module: $L\infty^*(\operatorname{pr}^*\mathcal E)=\mathcal E[0]$ because the local equation of $\infty(X)$ in $\mathbb P^1_X$ is a non-zero-divisor on $\operatorname{pr}^*\mathcal E$, and $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. This proof uses the flatness of $\operatorname{pr}^*\mathcal E$ and $\rho^*\mathcal E$ instead.

cards.attack: Checked for a point in A^1 (the strict transform of P^1 × {0} meets D = P(C ⊕ O) in the point [0:1], the zero section), X = P, X = ∅, X = V(x^2). Found: the statement is true only for Stacks' canonical isomorphism φ; for φ composed with a translation of P^1 the two sides are skyscrapers at different points, and the cited source only gave 'isomorphic'. The card now names the canonical φ and cites the vertex-to-zero-section compatibility. ρ∘ϑ = id is derivable; both squares are cartesian. Constant rank and 'E finite locally free' are not needed for the statement. Not broken once φ is the canonical one.

leanReading.note: A def giving an isomorphism L e^*(Q i E) ≅ Lφ^*((s_*ρ^*E)[0]) in D(O_D), with e = exceptionalInclusion, φ = Stacks.Chow.exceptionalFibreIsoProjectiveCompletion sP i hreg, s the zeroSection and ρ = bundleProj (unitModule X); the isomorphism is data.

cards.title: $Q$ vanishes on the strict transform
cards.statement: Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion of schemes over $k$ and $\mathcal E$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module. For the inclusion $a:X'\to W$ of the strict transform, $La^*Q$ is a zero object of $D(\mathcal O_{X'})$.
cards.proof: The image of $i':\mathbb P^1_X\to W$ does not meet $X'$: the ideal of $X'$ pulls back to the unit ideal on $\mathbb P^1_X$ (Stacks). The stalks of the module $i'_*\operatorname{pr}^*\mathcal E$ vanish outside the closed image of $i'$, hence at every point of $a(X')$. The stalk of a derived pullback at $x$ is the derived tensor product of the stalk at $a(x)$ with $\mathcal O_{X',x}$, so all stalks of the cohomology sheaves of $La^*Q$ vanish, and $La^*Q=0$.
cards.attack: Checked on the blowup of P^1 × P^1 in a point: the image of i' is H_x − E, X' = H_t − E, intersection number 0, so they are disjoint; X = P gives X' empty. The stalk formula for derived pullback holds on ringed spaces, so La^*Q has zero cohomology sheaves. No hypothesis on E is needed. Not broken.

leanReading.note: isZero_deformationStrictTransform: IsZero (L a^*(Q i E)) for a = strictTransformInclusion sP i = (X' → W_∞) ≫ (W_∞ → W), every O_X-module E and i a closed immersion. No discrepancy.

cards.title: Specialization at infinity and the localization sequence
cards.summary: (i_∞)_*(C ∩ α) = (i_0)_* α for a modification of X × P^1, and exactness of CH(Z) → CH(V) → CH(V ∖ Z).
cards.statement:
1. (Stacks 0F9J) Let $X$ be locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology and $b:W\to X\times\mathbb P^1$ a proper morphism that is an isomorphism over $X\times\mathbb A^1$, with section at zero $i_0:X\to W$ and fibre at infinity $i_\infty:W_\infty\to W$. There is a cap operation $C\cap-:CH_k(X)\to CH_k(W_\infty)$ with $(i_\infty)_*(C\cap\alpha)=(i_0)_*\alpha$ in $CH_k(W)$. If $\dim_\delta X\le n$ and $W_\infty$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $W$, then $C\cap[X]_n=[W_\infty]_n$.
2. (Stacks 02RX) Let $a:Z\to V$ be a closed immersion and $m:N\to V$ an open immersion onto the complement of $Z$. A class in $CH_n(V)$ restricts to zero on $N$ if and only if it is pushed forward from $CH_n(Z)$.
cards.source: Stacks Project, Tags 0F9J and 02RX. In the compiled Stacks library (namespace `Stacks.Chow`): `chowPushforward_gysinCapOfLift`, `gysinCapOfLift_fundamentalChowClass`, `exact_chowPushforward_chowGroupRestrict`. Used to specialize the fundamental class of $P$ in the deformation space.

cards.title: Specialization of $[P]$ in the deformation space
cards.summary: (i_0)_*[P] = e_*[D] + a_*β in CH_*(W)⊗ℚ, for P of pure dimension n.
cards.statement: Let $P$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and of pure dimension $n$, and $i:X\to P$ a closed immersion. With $W$, the section at zero $i_0:P\to W$, the exceptional divisor $e:D=W_\infty\times_PX\to W$ and the strict transform $a:X'\to W$, there is $\beta\in CH_*(X')_{\mathbb Q}$ with $$(i_0)_*[P]=e_*[D]+a_*\beta\quad\text{in }CH_*(W)_{\mathbb Q}.$$ Here $[D]$ is the fundamental class of the scheme $D$, which need not be smooth or reduced: the sum over $m$ of $1\otimes[D]_m$, where $[D]_m$ is the cycle of the irreducible components of $\delta$-dimension $m$ with their multiplicities.
cards.proof: $W\to P\times\mathbb P^1$ is a proper morphism (the blowup of a Noetherian scheme in a closed subscheme is projective) that is an isomorphism over $P\times\mathbb A^1$, its fibre at infinity is an effective Cartier divisor and $\dim_\delta P\le n$, so by Stacks 0F9J $(i_0)_*[P]_n=(i_\infty)_*[W_\infty]_n$ in $CH_n(W)$. The ideal of $W_\infty$ is the product of the ideals of the exceptional divisor and of $X'$, so the open subscheme $W_\infty\smallsetminus X'$ of $W_\infty$ is also an open subscheme of $D$; the classes $[W_\infty]_n$ and the pushforward of $[D]_n$ therefore have the same restriction to it, and by the localization sequence (Stacks 02RX) $[W_\infty]_n=e'_*[D]_n+a'_*\beta$ in $CH_n(W_\infty)$ for some $\beta\in CH_n(X')$, where $e':D\to W_\infty$ and $a':X'\to W_\infty$ are the inclusions. Push forward to $W$. Finally $P$ is of pure dimension $n$, and so is $D$: the generic points of $W$ lie over $\mathbb A^1_P$ and have $\delta=n+1$, and $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $W$, so its generic points have $\delta=n$. Hence $[P]=1\otimes[P]_n$ and $[D]=1\otimes[D]_n$ in the rational Chow groups, which gives the formula.

hypotheses.text: $P$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.
$P$ is of pure dimension $n$.
hypotheses.redundant: For smooth $P$ the statement holds without it: $P$ is the disjoint union of its open and closed parts of constant dimension, and $W$, $D$ and $X'$ decompose accordingly. This proof uses purity to read $[P]$ and $[D]$ in the single degree $n$.

cards.attack: Checked on the blowup of P^1 × P^1 in a point ((i_0)_*[P] = H_t = E + (H_t − E)), on the non-reduced X = V(x^2) in A^1 (W_∞ = X' + 2E_red and D = 2E_red: multiplicities agree off X'), a point in P^2, a point plus a line in P^2, X = P and X = ∅. All terms lie in CH_n(W). D is of pure dimension n in every case. Gaps found and fixed in the text: [D] is the fundamental class of a possibly singular scheme; properness of the blowup; 'generic points' refers to W. Purity of P is not needed for smooth P. Not broken.

leanReading.note: Specialization.lean shows the three hidden pushforwards are along i_0 = modificationSectionAtZero, e = pullback.fst _ i ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity and a = strictTransformToFibreAtInfinity ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity; [D] is Stacks' rational fundamental class of the scheme D.

cards.title: The zero section of a projective completion: Koszul resolution and top Chern class
cards.summary: Stacks: the Koszul complex resolves s_*O, π_*(c_r(K) ∩ π^*β) = (−1)^r β and ξ ∩ c_r(K) ∩ π^*β = 0.
cards.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\mathcal C$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of constant rank $r$, $\pi:\overline P=\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X)\to X$ its projective completion, $s:\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)\to\overline P$ the zero section, $\xi$ the cap with $c_1(\mathcal O_{\overline P}(1))$ and $\mathcal K=\pi^*\mathcal C\otimes\mathcal O_{\overline P}(-1)$.

1. The Koszul complex of the tautological map $\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_{\overline P}$, with $\Lambda^n\mathcal K$ in degree $-n$, represents $s_*\mathcal O$ in $D(\mathcal O_{\overline P})$.
2. If $X$ is locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology and $\beta\in CH_m(X)$, then $\pi_*\big(c_r(\mathcal K)\cap\pi^*\beta\big)=(-1)^r\beta$ and $\xi\cap\big(c_r(\mathcal K)\cap\pi^*\beta\big)=0$.
cards.source: Stacks Project, Tag 0FEF (Koszul resolution of the zero section), with Tags 02TW, 02U6, 02UD, 02UG for the top Chern class. In the compiled Stacks library: `Stacks.ProjectiveCompletion.koszulResolutionZeroSection`, `Stacks.Chow.pushforward_chernCap_tensorDual_bundlePullback`, `Stacks.Chow.capOnChow_chernCap_koszulModule_bundlePullback` (modules under `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Chow/ZeroSectionKoszul/`). Used for the zero-section formula.

cards.title: The projective completion, its zero section and the Koszul module
cards.summary: P̄ = P(C ⊕ O), π, the zero section s, ρ, the module K = π^*C ⊗ O(−1), and λ_{-1}.
cards.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal C$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module.

- The **projective completion** is $\overline P=\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X)$, the projective bundle of the module $\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X$, with projection $\pi:\overline P\to X$.
- The **zero section** is the closed immersion $s:\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)\to\overline P$ of projective bundles induced by the projection $\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X$; $\rho:\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)\to X$ is the projection of $\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)$.
- The **Koszul module** is $\mathcal K=\pi^*\mathcal C\otimes\mathcal O_{\overline P}(-1)$, where $\mathcal O_{\overline P}(-1)$ is the dual of the twisting sheaf.
- For a module $\mathcal M$ on a scheme and $r\ge0$: $\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal M)=\sum_{p=0}^{r}(-1)^p[\Lambda^p\mathcal M]\in K_0(\mathrm{Vect})$.

leanReading.note: Bodies match the card: projectiveCompletion C = Stacks.Chow.bundle (C ⊞ O_X) (Proj_X Sym), projectiveCompletionProj = its bundleProj, zeroSection = bundleEmbedding of biprod.snd : C ⊕ O_X → O_X, koszulModule = π^*C ⊗ dual of the twist, lambdaNegOne the alternating sum of exterior powers up to r.

cards.title: The projective completion is smooth
cards.summary: P(C ⊕ O) over a smooth X is smooth, separated, of finite type; ρ is an isomorphism.
cards.statement: Let $X$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $\mathcal C$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of constant rank $r$. Then $\overline P=\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X)$, with structure morphism $\overline P\xrightarrow{\pi}X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$. If $X$ is locally Noetherian, the projection $\rho:\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)\to X$ is an isomorphism.
cards.proof: The projective bundle of a finite locally free module of constant rank $r+1$ is smooth and proper over its base (Stacks: locally on $X$ it is $\mathbb P^r_X$), so $\pi$ is smooth, separated and quasi-compact; compose with $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. For $\rho$: $\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)=\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal O_X[T])$ is locally $\mathbb P^0_X=X$.

hypotheses.text: $X$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.
$\mathcal C$ has constant rank $r$.

cards.title: The Chern character of a sheaf on the zero section
cards.statement: Let $X$ be locally of finite type over the base of Chow homology, $\mathcal C$ finite locally free of constant rank $r$ on $X$, and $\overline P$, $\pi$, $s$, $\rho$, $\mathcal K$ as above. Let $\mathcal E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module and $K\in D(\mathcal O_{\overline P})$ with defined Chern classes and $K\cong(s_*\rho^*\mathcal E)[0]$. Then in $A^*(\overline P)_{\mathbb Q}$: $$\operatorname{ch}(K)=\operatorname{ch}\big(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal K)\big)\cdot\operatorname{ch}[\pi^*\mathcal E].$$ In particular, for $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_X$: $\operatorname{ch}\big((s_*\mathcal O)[0]\big)=\operatorname{ch}(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal K))$.
cards.proof: The Koszul complex $\Lambda^\bullet\mathcal K$ is a bounded complex of finite locally free modules representing $s_*\mathcal O$ (Stacks). Tensoring with the finite locally free (hence flat) module $\pi^*\mathcal E$ is exact and preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so $\Lambda^\bullet\mathcal K\otimes\pi^*\mathcal E$ represents $s_*\mathcal O\otimes\pi^*\mathcal E\cong s_*(s^*\pi^*\mathcal E)=s_*\rho^*\mathcal E$ (projection formula for the closed immersion $s$, and $\pi\circ s=\rho$). It is again a bounded complex of finite locally free modules, so by the comparison of power sum classes with Euler characteristics, $\operatorname{ch}(K)=\operatorname{ch}\big(\sum_n(-1)^n[\Lambda^n\mathcal K\otimes\pi^*\mathcal E]\big)=\operatorname{ch}\big(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal K)\cdot[\pi^*\mathcal E]\big)$, and $\operatorname{ch}$ is a ring map.
cards.attack: Checked exactly for X a point (ch(λ_{-1}K) = (1 − e^{−h})^r is the Chern character of a point of P^r) and on Hirzebruch surfaces over P^1 with E = O(b). Two standard facts were used without being said and are now in the text: tensoring with a flat module preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and s_*O ⊗ π^*E ≅ s_*ρ^*E. Not broken.

cards.title: The top Chern class of the Koszul module is the zero section
cards.statement: Let $X$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, $\mathcal C$ finite locally free of constant rank $r$ on $X$, and $\overline P$, $\pi$, $s$, $\mathcal K$ as above. Then in $CH_*(\overline P)_{\mathbb Q}$: $$\big(\operatorname{ch}(\lambda_{-1}(\mathcal K))\cdot\operatorname{td}[\mathcal K^\vee]\big)\cap[\overline P]=s_*[\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)].$$
cards.proof: By the Koszul identity for Chern characters applied to $\mathcal Q=\mathcal K^\vee$ (so $\mathcal Q^\vee\cong\mathcal K$): $\operatorname{ch}(\lambda_{-1}\mathcal K)=c_r(\mathcal K^\vee)\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal K^\vee])$, hence, Todd classes being units, $\operatorname{ch}(\lambda_{-1}\mathcal K)\cdot\operatorname{td}[\mathcal K^\vee]=c_r(\mathcal K^\vee)=(-1)^rc_r(\mathcal K)$ (Stacks 0FA5 for the sign). It remains to show $c_r(\mathcal K)\cap[\overline P]_{m+r}=(-1)^rs_*[\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)]_m$ in every degree. Since $\pi$ is flat of relative dimension $r$ and $X$ is smooth, $[\overline P]_{m+r}=\pi^*[X]_m$. Put $y=c_r(\mathcal K)\cap\pi^*[X]_m-(-1)^rs_*[\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)]_m$. Then $\pi_*y=0$: $\pi_*(c_r(\mathcal K)\cap\pi^*[X]_m)=(-1)^r[X]_m$ (Stacks) and $\pi_*s_*[\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)]_m=\rho_*[\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)]_m=[X]_m$, $\rho$ being an isomorphism. And $\xi\cap y=0$: $\xi\cap c_r(\mathcal K)\cap\pi^*\beta=0$ (Stacks), and $\xi\cap s_*z=s_*(c_1(s^*\mathcal O(1))\cap z)=0$ because $s^*\mathcal O(1)$ is trivial. A class $y$ on the projective bundle $\overline P\to X$ with $\xi\cap y=0$ and $\pi_*y=0$ is zero. Indeed, write $y=\sum_{j\le r}\xi^j\cap\pi^*\beta_j$ by the projective bundle formula for $\overline P\to X$; then $\pi_*(\xi^a\cap y)=0$ for all $a\ge0$. Recall that $\pi_*(\xi^{a+j}\cap\pi^*\beta_j)$ is $0$ for $a+j<r$ and $\beta_j$ for $a+j=r$. For $a=0$ this gives $\beta_r=0$. For $a=1$ the terms are $\beta_{r-1}$ and $\pi_*(\xi^{r+1}\cap\pi^*\beta_r)$, which vanishes because $\beta_r=0$; so $\beta_{r-1}=0$. Continuing, at step $a$ every term with $a+j>r$ involves a $\beta_j$ already shown to be zero, so $\beta_{r-a}=0$. Hence $y=0$.
cards.attack: 46 split cases in exact arithmetic (X a point, P^1, P^2, P^3; C a sum of line bundles, r ≤ 4): the sign (−1)^r and the dual K^∨ are right, and with C in place of C^∨ the formula fails (on the Hirzebruch surface with a = 1, b = 2: 5/2 against 3/2). Gaps found and fixed in the text: for a + j > r the pushforward π_*(ξ^{a+j} ∩ π^*β_j) is not zero (π_*(ξ^2) = 3[pt] on P(O(3) ⊕ O)), the induction closes only because those β_j already vanish; the bundle formula is needed for projective bundles, not only for P^n_U; c_r(K^∨) = (−1)^r c_r(K) and td(a)td(−a) = 1 were unlisted. Not broken.

cards.statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $\mathcal C$ finite locally free of constant rank $r$ on $X$, and $s$, $\rho$, $\mathcal K$ as above. Then $s^*[\mathcal K^\vee]=\rho^*[\mathcal C^\vee]$ in $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X))$.

Pullback commutes with duals of finite locally free modules, so $s^*\mathcal K^\vee\cong\rho^*\mathcal C^\vee$.

cards.title: Riemann–Roch for the zero section of $\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O)$
cards.statement: Let $X$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, $\mathcal C$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of constant rank $r$, $\pi:\overline P=\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X)\to X$, $s$ the zero section and $\rho=\pi\circ s$. For every finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ and every $K\in D(\mathcal O_{\overline P})$ with defined Chern classes and $K\cong(s_*\rho^*\mathcal E)[0]$: $$\pi_*\big(\operatorname{ch}(K)\cap[\overline P]\big)=\big(\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal E]\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal C^\vee])\big)\cap[X]\quad\text{in }CH_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}.$$
cards.proof: Write $t=\operatorname{td}[\mathcal K^\vee]$, a unit commuting with Chern characters, with inverse $\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal K^\vee])$. By the Chern character on the zero section, $\operatorname{ch}(K)=\operatorname{ch}(\lambda_{-1}\mathcal K)\cdot\operatorname{ch}[\pi^*\mathcal E]=\big(\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal K^\vee])\cdot\operatorname{ch}[\pi^*\mathcal E]\big)\cdot\big(\operatorname{ch}(\lambda_{-1}\mathcal K)\cdot t\big)$. Cap with $[\overline P]$: the second factor gives $s_*[\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)]$, and by the projection formula for $s$, $$\operatorname{ch}(K)\cap[\overline P]=s_*\Big(s^*\big(\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal K^\vee])\operatorname{ch}[\pi^*\mathcal E]\big)\cap[\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)]\Big).$$ Now $s^*\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal K^\vee])=\operatorname{td}(-s^*[\mathcal K^\vee])=\operatorname{td}(-\rho^*[\mathcal C^\vee])=\rho^*\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal C^\vee])$ and $s^*\operatorname{ch}[\pi^*\mathcal E]=\rho^*\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal E]$. Apply $\pi_*$ and use $\pi_*s_*=\rho_*$, the projection formula for $\rho$ and $\rho_*[\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)]=[X]$ ($\rho$ is an isomorphism, so $\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)$ is smooth like $X$ and its fundamental class maps to that of $X$): the result is $\big(\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal C^\vee])\cdot\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal E]\big)\cap[X]$, and Todd classes commute with Chern characters.
cards.attack: Checked exactly for X a point, and for X = P^1, C = O(a), E = O(b) on the Hirzebruch surface: both sides agree, with td(−[C^∨]); with td(−[C]) they differ whenever C is nontrivial, and the self-intersection −a of the zero section confirms that its normal bundle is C^∨. r = 0 is consistent. Unlisted: P(O_X) is smooth and ρ_*[P(O_X)] = [X], now said. Not broken.

cards.title: The normal class is the class of the normal bundle of Stacks
cards.summary: [N_{X/P}] = [C^∨], C the dual of Stacks' normal bundle of the regular immersion i.
cards.statement:
Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.

(a) The conormal sheaf $C_{X/P}$ of the conormal sequence of differentials is isomorphic to Stacks' conormal module $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ of $i$.

(b) Suppose $i$ is a regular immersion, let $\mathcal N$ be the normal bundle of the regular immersion $i$ in the sense of Stacks and $\mathcal C=\mathcal N^\vee$. Then $[N_{X/P}]=[\mathcal C^\vee]$ in $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$.
cards.proof:
(a) The first term of the conormal sequence $0\to C_{X/P}\to i^*\Omega_{P/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}\to0$ is the kernel of $i^*\Omega_{P/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}$, and the conormal module $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ maps isomorphically onto that kernel, because the sequence $0\to\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\to i^*\Omega_{P/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}\to0$ is exact for $X$ smooth over $k$.

(b) By (a), $N_{X/P}=C_{X/P}^\vee\cong(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)^\vee$. The normal bundle $\mathcal N$ of Stacks is the dual of the conormal module, which is finite locally free, hence reflexive: $\mathcal C^\vee=\mathcal N^{\vee\vee}\cong\mathcal N=(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)^\vee$. Isomorphic modules have the same class.

hypotheses.text: $X$ and $P$ are smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $i$ is a closed immersion over $k$.
$i$ is a regular immersion (in (b)).
hypotheses.redundant: It follows from the first hypothesis: a closed immersion of schemes smooth over $k$ is a regular immersion (Stacks 067U). It is stated because the normal bundle of Stacks is attached to a regular immersion together with the proof that it is one.

cards.attack: Checked on a point in P^1 and a line in P^2: the duality bookkeeping is right (C ≅ I/I², C^∨ ≅ N = N_{X/P}); with C in place of C^∨ Riemann–Roch fails for a line in P^2 (H − H²/2 against H + H²/2). Smoothness of X is essential: for Spec k[x]/(x²) in A^1 the map I/I² → i^*Ω is not injective. Attacked in the wording before regularity was made an explicit hypothesis of (b); the mathematics is unchanged. Not broken.

cards.title: Deformation to the normal cone: from the zero section to $i$
cards.summary: If the zero-section formula holds on P(C ⊕ O) and [N] = [C^∨], then (E) holds for i on vector bundles.
cards.statement:
Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, with $P$ of pure dimension $n$ and conormal module of constant rank $r$. Let $\mathcal C$ be the dual of the normal bundle of $i$ (Stacks), $\pi:\overline P=\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X)\to X$, $s$ its zero section and $\rho=\pi\circ s$. Suppose that

1. for every finite locally free $\mathcal E$ on $X$ and every $K\cong(s_*\rho^*\mathcal E)[0]$ with defined Chern classes, $\pi_*\big(\operatorname{ch}(K)\cap[\overline P]\big)=\big(\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal E]\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal C^\vee])\big)\cap[X]$;
2. $[N_{X/P}]=[\mathcal C^\vee]$ in $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}\,X)$.

Then for every finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$: $$\operatorname{ch}(i_!\,\theta[\mathcal E])\cap[P]=i_*\big((\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal E]\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[N_{X/P}]))\cap[X]\big).$$
cards.proof:
Let $W$ be the deformation space, $q:W\to P$, and $Q=(i'_*\operatorname{pr}^*\mathcal E)[0]$. $W$ and $\overline P$ are smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, so the coherent modules $i'_*\operatorname{pr}^*\mathcal E$ and $s_*\rho^*\mathcal E$, placed in degree $0$, have defined Chern classes; write $\overline K=(s_*\rho^*\mathcal E)[0]$.

*Zero fibre.* $\operatorname{ch}(i_!\theta[\mathcal E])=\operatorname{ch}((i_*\mathcal E)[0])=\operatorname{ch}(Li_0^*Q)=i_0^*\operatorname{ch}(Q)$. The morphism $q$ is proper, and proper pushforward of cycles is functorial (no smoothness is needed for that). Since $q\circ i_0=\mathrm{id}_P$, every $\gamma\in CH_*(P)_{\mathbb Q}$ is $q_*(i_0)_*\gamma$, so by the projection formula $$\operatorname{ch}(i_!\theta[\mathcal E])\cap[P]=q_*(i_0)_*\big(i_0^*\operatorname{ch}(Q)\cap[P]\big)=q_*\big(\operatorname{ch}(Q)\cap(i_0)_*[P]\big).$$

*Specialization.* $(i_0)_*[P]=e_*[D]+a_*\beta$, so the right side is $q_*e_*\big(e^*\operatorname{ch}(Q)\cap[D]\big)+q_*a_*\big(a^*\operatorname{ch}(Q)\cap\beta\big)$.

*Strict transform.* $a^*\operatorname{ch}(Q)=\operatorname{ch}(La^*Q)=0$ because $La^*Q=0$.

*Exceptional divisor.* $e^*\operatorname{ch}(Q)=\operatorname{ch}(Le^*Q)=\operatorname{ch}(L\varphi^*\overline K)=\varphi^*\operatorname{ch}(\overline K)$. Moreover $q\circ e=i\circ\pi\circ\varphi$ ($\varphi$ is an isomorphism over $X$, and $D$ lies over $X$) and $\varphi_*[D]=[\overline P]$, $\varphi$ being an isomorphism. Hence $$q_*e_*\big(\varphi^*\operatorname{ch}(\overline K)\cap[D]\big)=i_*\pi_*\big(\operatorname{ch}(\overline K)\cap\varphi_*[D]\big)=i_*\pi_*\big(\operatorname{ch}(\overline K)\cap[\overline P]\big)=i_*\big((\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal E]\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[\mathcal C^\vee]))\cap[X]\big)$$ by hypothesis 1, and $[\mathcal C^\vee]=[N_{X/P}]$ by hypothesis 2.
cards.attack: The chain of equalities was checked line by line, each cap and pullback on its own scheme (D need not be smooth). Worked cases: X = P (r = 0, empty strict transform), X = ∅, and a point p in a curve on the blown-up P^1 × P^1, where the exceptional term gives [p] and the strict-transform term 0. Pure dimension enters only through the specialization, constant rank only through the exceptional divisor and hypothesis 1. Unlisted and now said: q is proper, pushforward is functorial without smoothness, φ is an isomorphism over X. Not broken.

cards.title: The core case of (E) holds
cards.summary: (E) on vector bundles for pure dimensions and constant codimension, by deformation to the normal cone.
cards.statement: The core case of (E) holds for every field $k$.
cards.proof: Let $i:X\to P$ be as in the core case. $P$ smooth of relative dimension $n$ is of pure dimension $n$. $i$ is a regular immersion and $X$ is Noetherian. Let $\mathcal C$ be the dual of the normal bundle of $i$; it is finite locally free of constant rank $r$, like the conormal module. The zero-section formula holds on $\mathbb P(\mathcal C\oplus\mathcal O_X)$ for $\mathcal C$, and $[N_{X/P}]=[\mathcal C^\vee]$. These are the two hypotheses of the deformation to the normal cone, whose conclusion is the claim.
cards.attack: Every hypothesis of the deformation card and of the zero-section formula is met where it is applied. Finding: the proof never uses that X is nonempty, that r ≥ 1, that n = m + r, or that X has pure dimension, so it proves the same formula for r = 0 and X = ∅ as well; the core case as defined is narrower than what is proved. Unlisted: relative dimension n gives pure dimension n; X is Noetherian; duals keep constant rank. Not broken.

cards.title: (E) under composition and cancellation
cards.summary: (E) for i and j gives (E) for j∘i; (E) for j∘i and j gives (E) for i when j_* is injective.
cards.statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{j}Q$ be closed immersions over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.

1. If (E) holds for $i$ and for $j$, it holds for $j\circ i$.
2. If (E) holds for $j\circ i$ and for $j$, and $j_*:CH_*(P)_{\mathbb Q}\to CH_*(Q)_{\mathbb Q}$ is injective, then (E) holds for $i$.
cards.proof:
From $\operatorname{td}(T_X)=i^*\operatorname{td}(T_P)\operatorname{td}(-[N_{X/P}])$ for $i$, $j$ and $j\circ i$, and since Todd classes are units: $\operatorname{td}(-[N_{X/Q}])=i^*\operatorname{td}(-[N_{P/Q}])\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[N_{X/P}])$. With the projection formula for $i$ this gives, for the right sides $R_i(\alpha)=i_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(-[N_{X/P}]))\cap[X]\big)$: $R_{ji}(\alpha)=j_*\big(\operatorname{td}(-[N_{P/Q}])\cap R_i(\alpha)\big)$. For the left sides $L_i(\alpha)=\operatorname{ch}(i_!\alpha)\cap[P]$: $(ji)_!=j_!i_!$ and $R_j(i_!\alpha)=j_*\big(\operatorname{td}(-[N_{P/Q}])\cap L_i(\alpha)\big)$.

1. $L_{ji}(\alpha)=L_j(i_!\alpha)=R_j(i_!\alpha)=j_*(\operatorname{td}(-[N_{P/Q}])\cap L_i(\alpha))=j_*(\operatorname{td}(-[N_{P/Q}])\cap R_i(\alpha))=R_{ji}(\alpha)$.

2. The same chain read backwards gives $j_*\big(\operatorname{td}(-[N_{P/Q}])\cap L_i(\alpha)\big)=j_*\big(\operatorname{td}(-[N_{P/Q}])\cap R_i(\alpha)\big)$. As $j_*$ is injective and the cap with the unit $\operatorname{td}(-[N_{P/Q}])$ is bijective, $L_i(\alpha)=R_i(\alpha)$.
cards.attack: The Todd identity td(−[N_{X/Q}]) = i^*td(−[N_{P/Q}])·td(−[N_{X/P}]) was checked on pt ⊂ line ⊂ P^2, line ⊂ P^2 ⊂ P^3, a ruling line of a quadric in P^3 (non-split sequence) and a conic; the chain of equalities in both directions, the inverse of the cap with a Todd class, and the use of injectivity of j_* all hold. Unlisted standard facts: (j∘i)^* = i^*∘j^* and j∘i is a closed immersion. Not broken.

cards.title: (E) for the inclusion of an open and closed subscheme
cards.summary: For V open and closed in a smooth Y, (E) holds for V → Y.
cards.statement: Let $Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and $V\subseteq Y$ an open and closed subscheme. Then $V$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ and (E) holds for the inclusion $\iota:V\to Y$.
cards.proof: An open and closed subscheme of $Y$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$ like $Y$: an open immersion is smooth, and a closed immersion is separated and quasi-compact. $\iota$ is an open immersion, so its conormal sheaf is zero, $[N]=0$ and $\operatorname{td}(-[N])=\operatorname{td}(0)=1$. Let $V'$ be the complement, also open and closed, so $[Y]=\iota_*[V]+\iota'_*[V']$. It suffices to treat $\alpha=\theta[\mathcal F]$ with $\mathcal F$ finite locally free on $V$. Then $\iota_*\mathcal F$ is finite locally free on $Y$ (it is $\mathcal F$ on $V$ and $0$ on $V'$), $\iota_!\theta[\mathcal F]=\theta[\iota_*\mathcal F]$, and $\operatorname{ch}[\iota_*\mathcal F]$ restricts to $\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal F]$ on $V$ and to $0$ on $V'$. By the projection formula, $\operatorname{ch}[\iota_*\mathcal F]\cap[Y]=\iota_*\big(\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal F]\cap[V]\big)+\iota'_*(0\cap[V'])=\iota_*\big(\operatorname{ch}[\mathcal F]\cap[V]\big)$.
cards.attack: Checked V = ∅, V = Y, and that ch[ι_*F] restricts to ch[F] on V and to 0 on the complement. Gap found and fixed: the proof relied on V being smooth, separated and of finite type without showing it. Unlisted and now cited: td(0) = 1 and the pullback of Todd classes. 'Open and closed' is needed (a nodal cubic in P^2 is closed but not smooth; A^1 in P^1 is not proper). Not broken.

cards.title: (E) can be checked on open and closed pieces
cards.summary: (E) for i follows from (E) on the pieces of a clopen decomposition of X; and (E) for i^{-1}(W) → W gives (E) for i^{-1}(W) → P.
cards.statement:
Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.

1. Let $X=\bigsqcup_{n\in\mathbb N}U_n$ be a decomposition into open and closed subschemes. If (E) holds for every $U_n\to X\xrightarrow{i}P$, then (E) holds for $i$.
2. Let $W\subseteq P$ be open and closed. If (E) holds for the restriction $i^{-1}(W)\to W$ of $i$, then it holds for the composite $i^{-1}(W)\to X\xrightarrow{i}P$.
cards.proof:
1. $X$ is quasi-compact, so only finitely many $U_n$ are nonempty; for an empty $U_n$ there is nothing to prove. It suffices to treat $\alpha=\theta[\mathcal E]$. A module is the direct sum of the pushforwards of its restrictions to the pieces, so $\theta[\mathcal E]=\sum_n(\iota_n)_!\theta[\mathcal E|_{U_n}]$ with $\iota_n:U_n\to X$. Write $L_g(\gamma)=\operatorname{ch}(g_!\gamma)\cap[\text{target}]$ and $R_g(\gamma)=g_*\big((\operatorname{ch}(\gamma)\operatorname{td}(-[N_g]))\cap[\text{source}]\big)$ for the two sides of (E) for a closed immersion $g$. For $\gamma\in K_0(U_n)$, the multiplicativity $\operatorname{td}(-[N_{i\iota_n}])=\iota_n^*\operatorname{td}(-[N_i])\cdot\operatorname{td}(-[N_{\iota_n}])$ (from the formula for $\operatorname{td}(T)$ of a closed subscheme, applied to $i$, $\iota_n$ and $i\iota_n$) and the projection formula give $R_{i\iota_n}(\gamma)=i_*\big(\operatorname{td}(-[N_i])\cap R_{\iota_n}(\gamma)\big)$ and $R_i((\iota_n)_!\gamma)=i_*\big(\operatorname{td}(-[N_i])\cap L_{\iota_n}(\gamma)\big)$. By (E) for the open and closed immersion $\iota_n$ these agree. Hence $R_i((\iota_n)_!\gamma)=R_{i\iota_n}(\gamma)=L_{i\iota_n}(\gamma)=L_i((\iota_n)_!\gamma)$, using the hypothesis and $(i\iota_n)_!=i_!(\iota_n)_!$. Sum over $n$.

2. The composite $i^{-1}(W)\to X\to P$ equals $i^{-1}(W)\to W\to P$. (E) holds for $W\to P$ by the previous card and for $i^{-1}(W)\to W$ by hypothesis; compose.
cards.attack: Checked on a point plus a line in P^2 and on pt ⊔ P^1 → P^2 ⊔ P^3. Gap found and fixed: the key step used an identity that was only inside the proof of the composition rule, not in its statement; the proof now derives it. The cards on i_! for closed immersions and on θ were used without being listed. Not broken.

leanReading.note: Part 1 is closedImmersionFormula_of_isClopenDecomposition: given U : ℕ → X.Opens with IsClopenDecomposition U and (E) for every composite (U n).ι ≫ i, it concludes (E) for i. Part 2 is closedImmersionFormula_of_restrict, which concludes about the composite i⁻¹(W) → X → P.
