cards.title: (E) in codimension zero, from the core case
cards.summary: For X and P of the same pure dimension, (E) follows from the core case through the zero section of P^1_P.
cards.statement: Suppose the core case of (E) holds for $k$. Let $i:X\to P$ be a closed immersion over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$, both smooth of the same relative dimension $n$, with $X$ nonempty. Then (E) holds for $i$.
cards.proof: Let $j:P\to\mathbb P^1_P$ be the zero section and $p:\mathbb P^1_P\to P$ the projection, so $p\circ j=\mathrm{id}_P$; $\mathbb P^1_P$ is smooth of relative dimension $n+1$ over $k$. Then $j$ and $j\circ i$ are closed immersions of codimension one between pure-dimensional smooth schemes: their conormal modules have constant rank $r$ with $n+1=r+n$, so $r=1$, and the core case applies to both on vector bundles; by the reduction to vector bundles (E) holds for $j$ and for $j\circ i$. The map $j_*$ on rational Chow groups is injective because $p_*j_*=\mathrm{id}$. By cancellation, (E) holds for $i$.

hypotheses.text: $X$ and $P$ are smooth of the same relative dimension $n$ over $k$, and $X$ is nonempty.
The core case of (E) holds for $k$.
hypotheses.redundant: Not needed for the statement: the conormal module of a closed immersion between smooth schemes of the same pure dimension is zero, so by Nakayama $X$ is open as well as closed in $P$, and (E) for $i$ is the case of an open and closed subscheme. The proof given here goes through the zero section of $\mathbb P^1_P$ instead.

cards.attack: Checked that j∘i has conormal rank 1, that P^1_P is smooth of pure dimension n+1 and that p_*j_* = id, so the core case applies to j and to j∘i. Finding: the hypothesis 'the core case holds' is not needed for the statement. Equal pure dimension forces the conormal module to vanish, so X is open as well as closed in P and (E) is the case of an open and closed subscheme. Recorded as redundant; the proof given goes through P^1_P. Not broken.

leanReading.note: closedImmersionFormula_of_codim_zero: CoreClosedImmersionFormula k → for IsSmoothFT X and P and a closed immersion i over k with SmoothOfRelativeDimension n sP, SmoothOfRelativeDimension n sX (the same n) and Nonempty X, (E) holds for i. This matches the card exactly.

cards.title: (E) for all closed immersions, from the core case
cards.summary: Cut P and X into their parts of constant dimension; each piece is the core case or codimension zero.
cards.statement: Suppose the core case of (E) holds for $k$. Then (E) holds for every closed immersion $i:X\to P$ over $k$ of schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$.
cards.proof: A scheme smooth over $k$ is the disjoint union of its open and closed parts of constant dimension (Stacks 02NM), and each part is again smooth, separated and of finite type over $k$. Let $P_n\subseteq P$ be the part of dimension $n$; the $i^{-1}(P_n)$ decompose $X$, so it suffices to prove (E) for each $i^{-1}(P_n)\to X\to P$, and for that it suffices to prove (E) for $i^{-1}(P_n)\to P_n$. So assume $P$ smooth of relative dimension $n$. Decompose $X$ into its parts $X_m$ of dimension $m$; it suffices to prove (E) for each $X_m\to P$. If $X_m$ is empty there is nothing to prove. Otherwise the conormal module of $X_m\to P$ is finite locally free of constant rank $r$ with $n=r+m$ (the conormal sequence is exact with terms of ranks $r$, $n$, $m$). If $r\ge1$ the core case gives (E) on vector bundles, hence (E); if $r=0$ this is the case of codimension zero.
cards.attack: Checked empty pieces, r = 0, the impossibility of infinitely many dimensions (quasi-compactness), and that the pieces i^{-1}(P_n) → P_n are again closed immersions of schemes in the class; tested on pt ⊔ P^1 → P^2 ⊔ P^3 both ways round and on two skew lines. The dependency graph of all cards has no cycle. Unlisted and now cited: the decomposition of a smooth scheme into parts of constant dimension (Stacks 02NM), the case of open and closed pieces, and C_{X/P} ≅ I/I^2. Not broken.

leanReading.note: closedImmersionFormula_of_core: CoreClosedImmersionFormula k → ClosedImmersionFormula k sX sP i hi for every closed immersion i : X → P over k of IsSmoothFT schemes. Apart from the card's setting, the only hypothesis is the core case, which the card itself assumes.

cards.title: Blowups and closed immersions of smooth schemes
cards.summary: The blowup of a smooth scheme in a smooth centre is smooth; a closed immersion of smooth schemes is regular.
cards.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme.

1. (Tag 0FUT) If $Z\to X$ is a closed immersion of schemes smooth over $S$, the blowup of $X$ in $Z$ is smooth over $S$.
2. (Tag 067U) A closed immersion between schemes smooth over $S$ is a regular immersion.
cards.source: Stacks Project, Tags 0FUT and 067U. In the compiled Stacks library `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_blowUpToBase_comp` and `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_of_smooth_of_smooth`. Used for the deformation space.

cards.title: Capping with the fundamental class is bijective on a smooth scheme
cards.summary: A^p(X) → CH_{d−p}(X), c ↦ c ∩ [X], is bijective for X smooth of dimension d over a field.
cards.statement: Let $X$ be smooth over a field $k$, of constant relative dimension $d$. Then for every $p$ the map $A^p(X)\to CH_{d-p}(X)$, $c\mapsto c\cap[X]_d$, is bijective.
cards.source: Stacks Project, Tag 0FC2, first clause; in the compiled Stacks library `Stacks.Chow.chowCohomologyCapFundamentalClass_bijective_of_smooth_field` (module `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Chow/SmoothChowCohomology`). Not used in any proof here: it is the reason why the theorem, stated in $CH_*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ after capping with $[Y]$, says the same as the classical statement in $A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$, on each part of $Y$ of constant dimension.

steps.say: The goal, with the way each object is read in Lean. Everything below serves the identity f_* τ_X(α) = τ_Y(f_! α).
First the receiving groups: rational Chow groups, the Chow cohomology ring of Stacks and its cap action, and the fundamental class.
Then the source: K_0 of coherent sheaves, identified with K_0 of vector bundles on a smooth scheme, which is where Stacks' Chern character lives.
The Todd class needs the series x/(1−e^{−x}); its identities are proved once, in pure algebra.
Stacks' ring A^*(X)⊗ℚ is not known to be commutative, so the Todd class is built as an exponential of a rescaled Chern character in an abstract graded-complete ring.
What replaces commutativity: components of Chern characters commute, by the Adams operation ψ² and a Vandermonde argument.
This gives the first property the theorem needs: the Todd class is multiplicative on short exact sequences.
And the second: on a line bundle it is the Todd series at the first Chern class.
With ch and td in place, the Riemann–Roch map τ_X is defined.
The other side needs f_!; it is built from higher direct images and shown well defined by the long exact sequence.
Its functoriality for a closed immersion followed by a proper map is exactly what the factorisation of a projective morphism uses.
Now the theorem reduces to two cases: closed immersions into P^n_Y and the projections P^n_Y → Y.
The projection case: both sides are additive, so it is enough to compute them on classes that generate K_0(P^n_Y) rationally.
On the twisted classes [O(−j)]·π^*β the pushforward π_! is computed from the cohomology of the twists and the projection formula.
These classes generate rationally: this follows from K_0 ⊗ ℚ ≅ CH_* ⊗ ℚ on regular schemes and the projective bundle formula, with no K-theory of projective bundles.
For the other side one needs the Todd class of projective space, from the Euler sequence.
And the integral over the fibres, which picks out the coefficient of h^n.
The coefficient of x^n in e^{−jx}Q^{n+1} is 1 for j = 0 and 0 for 1 ≤ j ≤ n, which matches the pushforward computed before.
So the Riemann–Roch formula holds for every projection P^n_Y → Y.
The closed immersion case starts from the conormal sequence: td(T_X) = i^*td(T_P)·td(N)^{-1}.
With the projection formula this reduces GRR for i to the formula (E) without tangent bundles.
(E) is additive, so it is enough to prove it on vector bundles E, and there the left side is the Chern character of the perfect complex (i_*E)[0], which can be restricted to subschemes.
The model case is a zero section. Its sheaf is resolved by a Koszul complex, whose Chern character is a top Chern class times an inverse Todd class.
That top Chern class caps the fundamental class of P(C ⊕ O) to the class of the zero section; this is where the geometry of the model case enters.
Together with the projection formula this is Riemann–Roch for the zero section of P(C ⊕ O).
A general closed immersion is deformed to that model on W, the blow-up of P^1_P along the copy of X at infinity, with a sheaf Q on W interpolating between the two.
Over 0 the sheaf Q restricts to i_*E, so its Chern character computes the left side of (E).
On the exceptional divisor, which is P(C ⊕ O), it restricts to the sheaf of the zero section: the model case.
On the other component of the fibre at infinity, the strict transform, it vanishes.
The class of the fibre over 0 equals that of the exceptional divisor plus a class supported on the strict transform, so the left side of (E) can be computed at infinity.
Assembling these four facts with the model case and [N] = [C^∨] gives (E) when dimensions and codimension are constant.
Cutting target and source into their parts of constant dimension reduces every closed immersion to that case, codimension zero being treated separately.
So (E) holds for every closed immersion of smooth schemes.
And with it the Riemann–Roch formula for closed immersions, the second of the two cases.
The reduction now applies with nothing left to assume: the theorem holds for every projective morphism.
Taking Y = Spec k gives Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch, where the pushforward to the point is the integral and f_! is the Euler characteristic.

stages.name: Pin down the statement
stages.does: Fixes how each object of the theorem is read in Lean on Stacks, as definition cards with their declarations.
stages.said: GRR is read as f_* τ_X(α) = τ_Y(f_! α) in CH_*(Y)⊗ℚ, τ_X(α) = (ch(α)·td(T_X)) ∩ [X], for schemes smooth, separated and of finite type over k and f a closed immersion into P^n_Y followed by the projection; quasi-projectivity and integrality turn out not to be needed.

stages.name: Survey Stacks and choose the route
stages.does: Reads the compiled part of the library to see what exists, records what was tried and abandoned, and names what is quoted from Stacks.
stages.said: Route: Fulton ch. 15 (reduce to closed immersions and projections; closed immersions by deformation to the normal cone), because Stacks has Chow groups, bivariant classes, the Chern character on K_0(Vect) and on perfect complexes, K_0(Vect) ≅ K'_0 on regular schemes, higher direct images and the blow-up at infinity. No Todd class, no f_! in the compiled part, no commutative ring structure on A^*: these were built or worked around. Four dead routes are kept, and sixteen results are quoted from Stacks.

stages.name: Algebra of the Todd series
stages.does: Proves the power-series identities the geometric steps consume.
stages.said: Q(1−e^{−x}) = x, the coefficients C(n+d,n) of e^{dx}Q^{n+1} and their vanishing for the twists O(−j), Q = exp(log Q), and x^m as a combination of the e^{−jx} modulo x^{n+1}.

stages.name: Exponentials in graded-complete rings
stages.does: Builds exp, evaluation of power series and the Todd operation in an abstract ring of families of components, without commutativity.
stages.said: exp(x+y) = exp(x)exp(y) for commuting x, y; commutation of components follows from commutation of 2^n-rescalings (a Vandermonde argument); Td(e^h) = Q(h); graded ring maps commute with all of it.

stages.name: The Todd class in A^*(X)⊗ℚ
stages.does: Defines td = Td ∘ ch on Stacks' rational Chow cohomology ring and proves its multiplicativity, its value on line bundles, duals, pullback and the projection formula.
stages.said: A^*(X)⊗ℚ is graded-complete; components of Chern characters commute thanks to the Adams operation ψ²; td is multiplicative on short exact sequences, td(L) = c_1/(1−e^{−c_1}), ch_p(E^∨) = (−1)^p ch_p(E), f^* td = td f^*, f_*(f^*c ∩ γ) = c ∩ f_*γ.

stages.name: The pushforward f_! on K_0
stages.does: Builds f_![F] = Σ (−1)^i [R^i f_* F] from the compiled higher direct images and proves what the reduction needs.
stages.said: Well defined by the long exact sequence and uniform vanishing; i_![F] = [i_*F] for closed immersions; (g∘i)_! = g_!∘i_!; and the projection formula R^n f_*(F ⊗ f^*G) ≅ R^n f_*F ⊗ G for vector bundles G.

stages.name: Reduction to closed immersions and projections
stages.does: Shows the Riemann–Roch formula composes and reduces a projective f to the two cases.
stages.said: GRR for projective morphisms follows from GRR for closed immersions into P^n_Y and for the projections; with the projection case proved, from the single statement (E) for closed immersions.

stages.name: Projections P^n_Y → Y
stages.does: Proves GRR for the projection by computing both sides on twisted classes that generate K_0(P^n_Y) rationally.
stages.said: (P1) from the cohomology of twists and the projection formula; (P2) from Stacks 0FEY and the projective bundle formula, avoiding the K-theory of projective bundles; (P3) from the Euler sequence and the integral over the fibres.

stages.name: Closed immersions: reduction to (E)
stages.does: Reduces GRR for a closed immersion to the formula (E) without tangent bundles and proves the Koszul identity (E) will need.
stages.said: td(T_X) = i^*td(T_P)·td(N)^{-1}, the reduction of GRR(i) to (E), and Σ(−1)^p ch[Λ^pQ^∨] = c_r(Q)·td(Q)^{-1}. (E) itself is proved in the next four stages.

stages.name: From coherent sheaves to perfect complexes
stages.does: Identifies the Chern character of a coherent class with Stacks' Chern character of a perfect complex, so that restriction to subschemes of the deformation space can be computed.
stages.said: ch[F] = ch(F[0]) on a smooth scheme; ch of perfect complexes is compatible with pullback and vanishes on zero objects; (E) reduces to vector bundles, where the left side is ch((i_*E)[0]).

stages.name: The zero section of P(C ⊕ O)
stages.does: Proves the model case of (E): Riemann–Roch for the zero section of the projective completion of a vector bundle.
stages.said: The Koszul complex gives ch(s_*ρ^*E) = ch(λ_{-1}K)·ch(π^*E); the Koszul identity turns ch(λ_{-1}K)·td(K^∨) into the top Chern class, which caps [P̄] to the zero section by a uniqueness argument in the projective bundle formula; the projection formula finishes.

stages.name: Deformation to the normal cone
stages.does: Transports the model case to a closed immersion of pure dimension and constant codimension on Stacks' blow-up of P^1_P at infinity.
stages.said: The sheaf Q on W restricts to i_*E over 0, to the zero-section sheaf on the exceptional divisor and to 0 on the strict transform; [W_0] specializes to the exceptional divisor plus a class on the strict transform; with [N] = [C^∨] this gives the core case of (E).

stages.name: From the core case to every closed immersion
stages.does: Removes the assumptions of pure dimension and constant codimension.
stages.said: (E) is stable under composition and can be cancelled along a section; it holds for open and closed subschemes and can be checked on the pieces of a decomposition; codimension zero is treated through the zero section of P^1_P. Cutting source and target by dimension gives (E), hence GRR for closed immersions and the theorem.

stages.name: Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch
stages.said: χ is a homomorphism on K_0 compatible with the pushforward to the point, and τ on the point is χ·[Spec k]; HRR follows from GRR for the structure morphism, unconditionally.

from.ask:
Formalize the Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch theorem, as a proof map, on top of Axiom's Stacks project. Activate the proof-semantics skill first, then use `declare_proof_map` / `update_proof_map` and `lean_check`, always with `setup: "stacks"`.

**Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch.** Let $k$ be a field and $f : X \to Y$ a projective morphism of smooth quasi-projective varieties over $k$. For every $\alpha \in K_0(X)$, in $A^*(Y)_{\mathbb{Q}}$:
$$\operatorname{ch}(f_!\,\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_Y) \;=\; f_*\big(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_X)\big),$$
where $K_0$ is the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves, $f_!\,[\mathcal F]=\sum_i(-1)^i[R^if_*\mathcal F]$, $\operatorname{ch}$ is the Chern character, $\operatorname{td}$ the Todd class, $f_*$ proper pushforward on Chow groups, and $A^*_{\mathbb Q}$ the rational Chow ring. State Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch ($Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$: $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\int_X\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)\operatorname{td}(T_X)$) as a corollary.

What the `stacks` setup has (Lean v4.35, Mathlib v4.35.0, Stacks at commit c496df0, use it freely):
- Chow groups and cycles of schemes, rational equivalence, proper pushforward, flat pullback, Gysin maps, projective bundles, the splitting principle (`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Chow/`, about 2,000 files). The parallel theory for algebraic spaces (`Spaces/Chow/`) is not built here: stay with schemes.
- Bivariant classes and the Chow cohomology algebra; Chern classes of finite locally free modules, the Whitney formula, tensor and dual rules, first Chern class caps, the Chern character on K-groups (`ChernClasses/`, `ChernWhitney/`, `ChernCharacterKGroup`, …).
- Deformation to the normal cone and normal cones (`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Divisors/NormalCone/`), higher direct images and their base change, Grothendieck groups and Euler characteristics (`StacksCore/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup`, `StacksFrontier/KTheory/Grothendieck/`), curve Riemann–Roch.
- A rational total Chern character ring map (`rationalTotalChernCharacterRingHom`) and a proper pushforward for coherent modules; check what each is defined on before relying on it.
- Only these parts of Stacks, and what they import, are compiled on this machine (17,548 modules). Importing a Stacks module outside them fails with a missing object file; that is not a gap in Stacks. If you need one, name it in your answer and it will be built.
- No Todd class, no GRR or HRR. Search the library before building anything: much of what you need may be there under another name. The sources are at `~/.groth/lean/stacks/.lake/packages/Stacks/`.

What you must build yourself (the test): the Todd class in $A^*(-)_{\mathbb Q}$, the Chern character there unless Stacks' fits, and their multiplicativity; $f_!$ on $K_0$; GRR for closed embeddings (via deformation to the normal cone) and for projections $\mathbb P^n_Y \to Y$; and the reduction of a projective $f$ to those two cases through $X \hookrightarrow \mathbb P^n_Y \to Y$. Choose the route deliberately and say why on the map (Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, ch. 15, is the standard one). State on the map how "smooth quasi-projective variety" and each object above are read in Lean.

Rules for the Lean side:
- Compile with `lean_check` and `setup: "stacks"` until it compiles. Make Formal every card you can. Keep your files in the folder `lean_check` names for this thread, and give large projects to the tools by `from` path.
- You may import Stacks and Mathlib. Do NOT use any result that states GRR, HRR, or anything downstream of them (Stacks' `asymptotic_riemann_roch` included), and do not copy from other outside projects.
- No `sorry`, no new axioms. Name declarations under the namespace `GRR`.
- Give every card its `kind` and list a statement's hypotheses in `hypotheses`. Give each `definition` card its Lean declaration, and pass those names to `lean_check` as `definitions` too: a theorem is Formal only once its definitions have been read against their bodies.
- This will not yield to one run. An honest partial map is a result; a proof you do not have is not. Build the groundwork as its own cards, leave an unproved step without a proof and say where you got stuck in its `attempt`; everything resting on it will read conditional. If a Lean theorem takes a hard step as a hypothesis, list it in `lean.assumes`. Never present a reduction as the theorem.
- Before you conclude that Stacks or Mathlib lacks something, test that belief: search the library or try a `lean_check`, and record what you tried as a dead route.
- Call `update_proof_map` whenever a part compiles, so the map survives a run that stops.
- Before finishing, have a separate agent read each Formal card's statement (and each definition's body) against its Lean (`leanReading`), and attack the derived cards, as the skill says.

How to work: you lead, others prove.
- You are the head of this work, not its only hand. Plan the map, split it into self-contained steps, and give the proving to helper agents on GPT-6.1, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, each at its highest effort (call `agent_models` for their exact ids and effort levels, then `spawn_agent` with `model` and `effort`). Do the hardest or most delicate steps yourself when that is quicker than explaining them.
- Give each helper a precise statement, the Lean context and files in your folder it needs, the namespace to use, and what to hand back: a compiling proof, a counterexample, a search result, or a plan. Run helpers in parallel on independent steps; set two on the same hard step by different routes when it matters. Keep at most four running at once: each compile against Stacks uses several gigabytes, and this machine has 24.
- You answer for correctness. Nothing a helper says counts until you have checked it: its Lean compiles through your own `lean_check` with `setup: "stacks"`, its statement says what the card says, and it uses nothing forbidden. Readings and attacks still go to separate agents, as the skill says.
- Do not stop at a conditional map while a step can still be attacked. When a route stalls, record it as a dead route and try another, or give it to a different model. The aim is every card Formal, the goal included.

When done, finish the map (`final: true`) and end your answer with one line:
`RESULT: <n Formal> / <n cards>, conditional: <n>, open steps: <n>, goal: formal|conditional|argued|open, Lean compiled: yes|no, forbidden results used: yes|no`

files.text:
import Mathlib

/-!
# The Todd power series

`GRR.toddSeries` is `x / (1 - e^{-x}) = ∑ B⁺_n x^n / n!` in `ℚ⟦X⟧`. This file proves the three
facts about it that Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch uses:

* `GRR.toddSeries_mul_one_sub_expNeg`: `Q · (1 - e^{-x}) = x` (the rank-one Koszul identity);
* `GRR.coeff_exp_pow_mul_toddSeries_pow`: `[x^n] (e^{d x} · Q^{n+1}) = C(n + d, n)`
  (Riemann–Roch on projective space);
* `GRR.coeff_toddSeries_eq_coeff_sum_logTodd_pow`: `Q = exp (log Q)`, coefficient by coefficient
  (the Todd class is the exponential of a linear function of the Chern character).
-/

open PowerSeries

namespace GRR

/-- The Todd power series `x / (1 - e^{-x}) = ∑ B⁺_n x^n / n!`, as the generating series of the
Bernoulli numbers `B⁺_n` (those with `B⁺_1 = 1/2`). -/
noncomputable def toddSeries : ℚ⟦X⟧ := bernoulli'PowerSeries ℚ

/-- The power series `e^{-x}`. -/
noncomputable def expNeg : ℚ⟦X⟧ := evalNegHom (exp ℚ)

theorem exp_mul_expNeg : exp ℚ * expNeg = 1 := exp_mul_exp_neg_eq_one

theorem expNeg_mul_exp : expNeg * exp ℚ = 1 := by rw [mul_comm, exp_mul_expNeg]

/-- The defining relation of the Todd series: `Q · (1 - e^{-x}) = x`. -/
theorem toddSeries_mul_one_sub_expNeg : toddSeries * (1 - expNeg) = X := by
  have h : toddSeries * (exp ℚ - 1) = X * exp ℚ := bernoulli'PowerSeries_mul_exp_sub_one ℚ
  have h1 : (exp ℚ - 1) * expNeg = 1 - expNeg := by rw [sub_mul, exp_mul_expNeg, one_mul]
  calc toddSeries * (1 - expNeg) = toddSeries * (exp ℚ - 1) * expNeg := by rw [mul_assoc, h1]
    _ = X * (exp ℚ * expNeg) := by rw [h, mul_assoc]
    _ = X := by rw [exp_mul_expNeg, mul_one]

/-- The Todd series has constant term `1`. -/
theorem constantCoeff_toddSeries : constantCoeff toddSeries = 1 := by
  simp [toddSeries, bernoulli'PowerSeries]

/-- The coefficients of `e^{-x}`. -/
theorem coeff_expNeg (n : ℕ) : coeff n expNeg = (-1) ^ n / (n.factorial : ℚ) := by
  simp [expNeg, evalNegHom, coeff_exp, div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm]

/-- `(e^{-x})' = -e^{-x}`. -/
theorem derivative_expNeg : d⁄dX expNeg = -expNeg := by
  ext n
  rw [coeff_derivative, map_neg, coeff_expNeg, coeff_expNeg, Nat.factorial_succ]
  have h : ((n.factorial : ℚ)) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_ne_zero n
  have h' : ((n : ℚ) + 1) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  push_cast
  field_simp
  ring

/-- `x · Q' = Q - e^{-x} · Q²`. -/
theorem X_mul_derivative_toddSeries :
    X * d⁄dX toddSeries = toddSeries - expNeg * toddSeries ^ 2 := by
  have h : d⁄dX (toddSeries * (1 - expNeg)) = d⁄dX (X : ℚ⟦X⟧) := by
    rw [toddSeries_mul_one_sub_expNeg]
  rw [Derivation.leibniz, map_sub, derivative_expNeg, derivative_X] at h
  simp only [smul_eq_mul, Derivation.map_one_eq_zero, zero_sub, neg_neg] at h
  -- h : toddSeries * expNeg + (1 - expNeg) * d⁄dX toddSeries = 1
  have h2 : toddSeries * (toddSeries * expNeg + (1 - expNeg) * d⁄dX toddSeries) = toddSeries := by
    rw [h, mul_one]
  have h3 : toddSeries * ((1 - expNeg) * d⁄dX toddSeries) = X * d⁄dX toddSeries := by
    rw [← mul_assoc, toddSeries_mul_one_sub_expNeg]
  rw [mul_add, h3] at h2
  linear_combination h2

/-- `x · (Q^n)' = n · Q^n - n · e^{-x} · Q^{n+1}`. -/
theorem X_mul_derivative_toddSeries_pow (n : ℕ) :
    X * d⁄dX (toddSeries ^ n) =
      (n : ℚ⟦X⟧) * toddSeries ^ n - (n : ℚ⟦X⟧) * (expNeg * toddSeries ^ (n + 1)) := by
  rcases n with _ | n
  · simp
  · rw [derivative_pow]
    have h := X_mul_derivative_toddSeries
    have : X * (((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℚ⟦X⟧) * toddSeries ^ (n + 1 - 1) * d⁄dX toddSeries) =
        ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℚ⟦X⟧) * toddSeries ^ n * (X * d⁄dX toddSeries) := by
      rw [Nat.add_sub_cancel]; ring
    rw [this, h]
    ring

/-- The coefficient of `x^n` in `e^{-x} · Q^{n+1}` vanishes for `n ≥ 1`. -/
theorem coeff_expNeg_mul_toddSeries_pow (n : ℕ) :
    coeff (n + 1) (expNeg * toddSeries ^ (n + 2)) = 0 := by
  have h := congrArg (coeff (n + 1)) (X_mul_derivative_toddSeries_pow (n + 1))
  rw [mul_comm X, coeff_succ_mul_X, coeff_derivative, map_sub] at h
  have e1 : ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℚ⟦X⟧) = C ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℚ) := by simp
  rw [e1, coeff_C_mul, coeff_C_mul] at h
  have hn : ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  have h' : ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℚ) * coeff (n + 1) (expNeg * toddSeries ^ (n + 1 + 1)) = 0 := by
    push_cast at h ⊢
    linear_combination h
  exact (mul_eq_zero.mp h').resolve_left hn

/-- `e^{(d+1)x} Q^{n+1} - e^{dx} Q^{n+1} = x · e^{(d+1)x} Q^n`. -/
theorem exp_pow_succ_mul_toddSeries_pow_succ (n d : ℕ) :
    exp ℚ ^ (d + 1) * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) =
      exp ℚ ^ d * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) + X * (exp ℚ ^ (d + 1) * toddSeries ^ n) := by
  have h := toddSeries_mul_one_sub_expNeg
  have h1 : exp ℚ ^ (d + 1) * expNeg = exp ℚ ^ d := by
    rw [pow_succ, mul_assoc, exp_mul_expNeg, mul_one]
  calc exp ℚ ^ (d + 1) * toddSeries ^ (n + 1)
      = exp ℚ ^ (d + 1) * expNeg * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) +
          exp ℚ ^ (d + 1) * toddSeries ^ n * (toddSeries * (1 - expNeg)) := by ring
    _ = exp ℚ ^ d * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) + X * (exp ℚ ^ (d + 1) * toddSeries ^ n) := by
        rw [h1, h]; ring

/-- `Q^{n+1} - e^{-x} Q^{n+1} = x · Q^n`. -/
theorem toddSeries_pow_succ (n : ℕ) :
    toddSeries ^ (n + 1) = expNeg * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) + X * toddSeries ^ n := by
  have h := toddSeries_mul_one_sub_expNeg
  calc toddSeries ^ (n + 1)
      = expNeg * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) + toddSeries ^ n * (toddSeries * (1 - expNeg)) := by ring
    _ = expNeg * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) + X * toddSeries ^ n := by rw [h]; ring

/-- **Riemann–Roch on projective space, as an identity of power series**: the coefficient of
`x^n` in `e^{d x} · (x / (1 - e^{-x}))^{n+1}` is the binomial coefficient `C(n + d, n)`, the
rank of the degree-`d` forms in `n + 1` variables. -/
theorem coeff_exp_pow_mul_toddSeries_pow (n d : ℕ) :
    coeff n (exp ℚ ^ d * toddSeries ^ (n + 1)) = ((n + d).choose n : ℚ) := by
  induction n generalizing d with
  | zero =>
    have : constantCoeff (exp ℚ ^ d * toddSeries ^ (0 + 1)) = 1 := by
      simp [constantCoeff_toddSeries]
    simpa using this
  | succ n ihn =>
    induction d with
    | zero =>
      have h := congrArg (coeff (n + 1)) (toddSeries_pow_succ (n + 1))
      rw [map_add, coeff_expNeg_mul_toddSeries_pow, zero_add, mul_comm X, coeff_succ_mul_X] at h
      have h0 := ihn 0
      simp only [pow_zero, one_mul, Nat.add_zero, Nat.choose_self, Nat.cast_one] at h0 ⊢
      rw [h, h0]
    | succ d ihd =>
      have h := congrArg (coeff (n + 1)) (exp_pow_succ_mul_toddSeries_pow_succ (n + 1) d)
      rw [map_add, mul_comm X, coeff_succ_mul_X, ihd, ihn (d + 1)] at h
      rw [h]
      have : (n + 1 + (d + 1)).choose (n + 1) = (n + 1 + d).choose (n + 1) + (n + (d + 1)).choose n := by
        rw [show n + 1 + (d + 1) = (n + 1 + d) + 1 by ring, Nat.choose_succ_succ,
          show n + (d + 1) = n + 1 + d by ring, add_comm]
      rw [this]
      push_cast
      ring

/-- `e^{-jx} Q^{n+1} - e^{-(j+1)x} Q^{n+1} = x · e^{-jx} Q^n`. -/
theorem expNeg_pow_mul_toddSeries_pow_succ (n j : ℕ) :
    expNeg ^ j * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) =
      expNeg ^ (j + 1) * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) + X * (expNeg ^ j * toddSeries ^ n) := by
  have h := toddSeries_mul_one_sub_expNeg
  calc expNeg ^ j * toddSeries ^ (n + 1)
      = expNeg ^ (j + 1) * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) +
          expNeg ^ j * toddSeries ^ n * (toddSeries * (1 - expNeg)) := by ring
    _ = expNeg ^ (j + 1) * toddSeries ^ (n + 1) + X * (expNeg ^ j * toddSeries ^ n) := by
        rw [h]; ring

/-- **Vanishing on projective space, as an identity of power series**: the coefficient of `x^n`
in `e^{-j x} · (x / (1 - e^{-x}))^{n+1}` vanishes for `1 ≤ j ≤ n` (the twists `𝒪(-j)`,
`1 ≤ j ≤ n`, of `ℙⁿ` have no cohomology). -/
theorem coeff_expNeg_pow_mul_toddSeries_pow {n j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) (hjn : j ≤ n) :
    coeff n (expNeg ^ j * toddSeries ^ (n + 1)) = 0 := by
  induction j generalizing n with
  | zero => omega
  | succ j ih =>
    obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = m + 1 := ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos j with rfl | hjpos
    · simpa using coeff_expNeg_mul_toddSeries_pow m
    · have h := congrArg (coeff (m + 1)) (expNeg_pow_mul_toddSeries_pow_succ (m + 1) j)
      rw [map_add, mul_comm X, coeff_succ_mul_X, ih hjpos (by omega), ih hjpos (by omega)] at h
      simpa using h.symm

/-! ### The logarithm of the Todd series -/

/-- The logarithm of the Todd series, `log (x / (1 - e^{-x})) = x/2 - x²/24 + ⋯`. -/
noncomputable def logTodd : ℚ⟦X⟧ := logOf toddSeries

theorem constantCoeff_logTodd : constantCoeff logTodd = 0 :=
  constantCoeff_logOf constantCoeff_toddSeries

theorem hasSubst_toddSeries_sub_one : HasSubst (toddSeries - 1) := by
  apply HasSubst.of_constantCoeff_zero'
  simp [constantCoeff_toddSeries]

theorem hasSubst_logTodd : HasSubst logTodd :=
  HasSubst.of_constantCoeff_zero' constantCoeff_logTodd

/-- `exp (log Q) = Q`, as a substitution of power series. -/
theorem exp_subst_logTodd : (exp ℚ).subst logTodd = toddSeries := by
  have h1 : (exp ℚ).subst logTodd =
      PowerSeries.subst (toddSeries - 1) ((exp ℚ).subst (log ℚ) : ℚ⟦X⟧) := by
    rw [logTodd, logOf_eq]
    exact (subst_comp_subst_apply HasSubst.log hasSubst_toddSeries_sub_one (exp ℚ)).symm
  rw [h1, subst_exp_log, subst_add hasSubst_toddSeries_sub_one,
    subst_X hasSubst_toddSeries_sub_one,
    ← coe_substAlgHom hasSubst_toddSeries_sub_one, map_one]
  ring

/-- Powers of `log Q` have no terms of low degree. -/
theorem coeff_logTodd_pow_of_lt {n d : ℕ} (h : n < d) : coeff n (logTodd ^ d) = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := X_dvd_iff.mpr constantCoeff_logTodd
  rw [hg, mul_pow, coeff_X_pow_mul', ite_eq_right_iff]
  intro h'
  exact absurd h' (by omega)

/-- **`Q = exp (log Q)`, coefficient by coefficient**: the coefficient of `x^n` in the Todd
series is that of the truncated exponential `∑_{j ≤ n} (log Q)^j / j!`. -/
theorem coeff_toddSeries_eq_coeff_sum_logTodd_pow (n : ℕ) :
    coeff n toddSeries =
      coeff n (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), ((j.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • logTodd ^ j) := by
  conv_lhs => rw [← exp_subst_logTodd, coeff_subst' hasSubst_logTodd]
  rw [finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset (s := Finset.range (n + 1))]
  · rw [map_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ ↦ ?_
    rw [coeff_exp, coeff_smul]
    simp
  · intro d hd
    simp only [Function.mem_support, ne_eq] at hd
    by_contra hd'
    simp only [Finset.coe_range, Set.mem_Iio, not_lt] at hd'
    exact hd (by rw [coeff_logTodd_pow_of_lt (by omega), smul_zero])

end GRR

import Mathlib
import GRR.ToddSeries

/-!
# Exponentials and power series in a graded-complete `ℚ`-algebra

`GRR.GradedComplete R` records that the elements of a ring `R` are the families `(a_n)_{n ≥ 0}` of
components `a_n ∈ M n`, multiplied by a Cauchy product (the degree-`n` component of a product
only sees the components of degree `≤ n` of the factors, and a product of homogeneous elements of
degrees `i`, `j` is homogeneous of degree `i + j`). The ring `∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ` is of this kind.

In such a ring this file defines the exponential `gexp x = ∑ x^j / j!` of an element without
constant term, the value `ev h F = ∑ F_j h^j` of a power series `F ∈ ℚ⟦X⟧` at such an element, and
the Todd operation `toddOf c = gexp (∑_n n! · ℓ_n · c_n)`, where `log (x / (1 - e^{-x})) = ∑ ℓ_n x^n`.
It proves `gexp (x + y) = gexp x * gexp y` for commuting `x`, `y`, that `ev h` is a ring map, and
`toddOf (e^h) = h / (1 - e^{-h})` for `h` homogeneous of degree one.
-/

open PowerSeries Finset

universe u v

namespace GRR

/-- A ring `R` whose elements are the families `(a_n)_{n ≥ 0}` with `a_n ∈ M n`, with a
`ℚ`-bilinear Cauchy product: the degree-`n` component of `a * b` only depends on the components
of degree `≤ n` of `a` and `b`, and a product of homogeneous elements of degrees `i` and `j` is
homogeneous of degree `i + j`. -/
structure GradedComplete (R : Type u) [Ring R] [Module ℚ R] where
  /-- The group of degree-`n` components. -/
  M : ℕ → Type v
  [addCommGroup : ∀ n, AddCommGroup (M n)]
  [module : ∀ n, Module ℚ (M n)]
  /-- The degree-`n` component of an element. -/
  comp : ∀ n, R →ₗ[ℚ] M n
  /-- The element with given components. -/
  ofComps : (∀ n, M n) → R
  comp_ofComps : ∀ (f : ∀ n, M n) (n : ℕ), comp n (ofComps f) = f n
  ext : ∀ a b : R, (∀ n, comp n a = comp n b) → a = b
  smul_mul : ∀ (q : ℚ) (a b : R), (q • a) * b = q • (a * b)
  mul_smul : ∀ (q : ℚ) (a b : R), a * (q • b) = q • (a * b)
  mul_congr : ∀ (n : ℕ) (a a' b b' : R), (∀ p ≤ n, comp p a = comp p a') →
    (∀ p ≤ n, comp p b = comp p b') → comp n (a * b) = comp n (a' * b')
  mul_hom : ∀ (i j : ℕ) (a b : R), (∀ p, p ≠ i → comp p a = 0) → (∀ p, p ≠ j → comp p b = 0) →
    ∀ p, p ≠ i + j → comp p (a * b) = 0
  comp_one : ∀ p, p ≠ 0 → comp p (1 : R) = 0

attribute [instance] GradedComplete.addCommGroup GradedComplete.module

namespace GradedComplete

variable {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Module ℚ R] (G : GRR.GradedComplete.{u, v} R)

/-- `a` has no component of degree `< n`. -/
def VanishBelow (n : ℕ) (a : R) : Prop := ∀ p, p < n → G.comp p a = 0

/-- `a` is homogeneous of degree `n`: its components of every other degree vanish. -/
def IsHom (n : ℕ) (a : R) : Prop := ∀ p, p ≠ n → G.comp p a = 0

/-! ### Homogeneous pieces and the Cauchy product formula -/

/-- The homogeneous element of degree `p` with degree-`p` component `m`. -/
noncomputable def single (p : ℕ) (m : G.M p) : R := G.ofComps (Pi.single p m)

theorem comp_single (p : ℕ) (m : G.M p) (n : ℕ) :
    G.comp n (G.single p m) = Pi.single (M := G.M) p m n :=
  G.comp_ofComps _ n

theorem comp_single_self (p : ℕ) (m : G.M p) : G.comp p (G.single p m) = m := by
  rw [comp_single, Pi.single_eq_same]

theorem comp_single_of_ne {p n : ℕ} (m : G.M p) (h : n ≠ p) : G.comp n (G.single p m) = 0 := by
  rw [comp_single, Pi.single_eq_of_ne h]

theorem isHom_single (p : ℕ) (m : G.M p) : G.IsHom p (G.single p m) :=
  fun _ hn ↦ G.comp_single_of_ne m hn

theorem single_zero (p : ℕ) : G.single p (0 : G.M p) = 0 :=
  G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ by rw [comp_single, Pi.single_zero, Pi.zero_apply, map_zero]

theorem single_smul (p : ℕ) (q : ℚ) (m : G.M p) : G.single p (q • m) = q • G.single p m :=
  G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ by rw [comp_single, map_smul, comp_single, Pi.single_smul, Pi.smul_apply]

/-- An element agrees up to degree `n` with the sum of its homogeneous pieces of degree `≤ n`. -/
theorem comp_sum_single (a : R) {n p : ℕ} (hp : p ≤ n) :
    G.comp p (∑ q ∈ range (n + 1), G.single q (G.comp q a)) = G.comp p a := by
  rw [map_sum]
  simp only [comp_single]
  rw [Finset.sum_pi_single, ite_eq_left (Finset.mem_range.mpr (by omega))]

/-- **The Cauchy product formula**: the degree-`n` component of `a * b` is the sum over `p ≤ n`
of the degree-`n` components of the products of the pieces of degrees `p` and `n - p`. -/
theorem comp_mul (n : ℕ) (a b : R) :
    G.comp n (a * b) = ∑ p ∈ range (n + 1),
      G.comp n (G.single p (G.comp p a) * G.single (n - p) (G.comp (n - p) b)) := by
  rw [G.mul_congr n a (∑ p ∈ range (n + 1), G.single p (G.comp p a)) b
      (∑ q ∈ range (n + 1), G.single q (G.comp q b))
      (fun p hp ↦ (G.comp_sum_single a hp).symm) (fun p hp ↦ (G.comp_sum_single b hp).symm),
    Finset.sum_mul_sum, map_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p hp ↦ ?_
  have hp' : p < n + 1 := Finset.mem_range.mp hp
  rw [map_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single (n - p)]
  · intro q _ hq
    exact G.mul_hom p q _ _ (G.isHom_single p _) (G.isHom_single q _) n (by omega)
  · intro hq
    exact absurd (Finset.mem_range.mpr (by omega)) hq

/-- The Cauchy product formula, indexed by the degree of the second factor. -/
theorem comp_mul_rev (n : ℕ) (a b : R) :
    G.comp n (a * b) = ∑ p ∈ range (n + 1),
      G.comp n (G.single (n - p) (G.comp (n - p) a) * G.single p (G.comp p b)) := by
  rw [comp_mul, ← Finset.sum_range_reflect]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p hp ↦ ?_
  have hp' : p < n + 1 := Finset.mem_range.mp hp
  rw [show n + 1 - 1 - p = n - p by omega, Nat.sub_sub_self (by omega : p ≤ n)]

theorem vanishBelow_smul {n : ℕ} (q : ℚ) {a : R} (ha : G.VanishBelow n a) :
    G.VanishBelow n (q • a) :=
  fun p hp ↦ by rw [map_smul, ha p hp, smul_zero]

/-- Orders add under multiplication. -/
theorem vanishBelow_mul {i j : ℕ} {a b : R} (ha : G.VanishBelow i a) (hb : G.VanishBelow j b) :
    G.VanishBelow (i + j) (a * b) := by
  intro n hn
  rw [comp_mul]
  refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun p hp ↦ ?_
  have hp' : p < n + 1 := Finset.mem_range.mp hp
  rcases lt_or_ge p i with hpi | hpi
  · rw [ha p hpi, single_zero, zero_mul, map_zero]
  · rw [hb (n - p) (by omega), single_zero, mul_zero, map_zero]

/-- A power of an element without constant term has no component of degree below the exponent. -/
theorem vanishBelow_pow {x : R} (hx : G.comp 0 x = 0) (j : ℕ) : G.VanishBelow j (x ^ j) := by
  induction j with
  | zero => exact fun p hp ↦ absurd hp (Nat.not_lt_zero p)
  | succ j ih =>
    rw [pow_succ]
    exact G.vanishBelow_mul ih fun p hp ↦ by rw [Nat.lt_one_iff.mp hp, hx]

/-- A power of a homogeneous element of degree one is homogeneous of degree the exponent. -/
theorem isHom_pow {h : R} (hh : G.IsHom 1 h) (j : ℕ) : G.IsHom j (h ^ j) := by
  induction j with
  | zero => rw [pow_zero]; exact G.comp_one
  | succ j ih => rw [pow_succ]; exact G.mul_hom j 1 _ _ ih hh

/-- In a sum `∑_{j ≤ N} f j` with `f j` of order `≥ j`, the degree-`n` component does not depend
on `N ≥ n`. -/
theorem comp_sum_range_of_le (f : ℕ → R) (hf : ∀ j, G.VanishBelow j (f j)) {n N : ℕ}
    (h : n ≤ N) :
    G.comp n (∑ j ∈ range (n + 1), f j) = G.comp n (∑ j ∈ range (N + 1), f j) := by
  rw [map_sum, map_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_subset (Finset.range_subset_range.mpr (by omega)) fun j _ hj ↦ ?_
  exact hf j n (by simp only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] at hj; omega)

/-- Truncated Cauchy products: if `u a * v b` has order `≥ a + b`, then in degree `n` the product
of the partial sums up to `n` is the partial sum of the Cauchy product. -/
theorem comp_sum_mul_sum (u v : ℕ → R) (huv : ∀ a b, G.VanishBelow (a + b) (u a * v b))
    (n : ℕ) :
    G.comp n ((∑ a ∈ range (n + 1), u a) * ∑ b ∈ range (n + 1), v b) =
      G.comp n (∑ j ∈ range (n + 1), ∑ a ∈ range (j + 1), u a * v (j - a)) := by
  rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum, Finset.sum_range_diag_flip (n + 1) (fun a b ↦ u a * v b)]
  simp only [map_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha ↦ ?_
  have ha' : a < n + 1 := Finset.mem_range.mp ha
  symm
  refine Finset.sum_subset (Finset.range_subset_range.mpr (by omega)) fun b _ hb ↦ ?_
  exact huv a b n (by simp only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] at hb; omega)

/-! ### The exponential -/

/-- The exponential `∑_j x^j / j!`, meaningful when `x` has no constant term: in degree `n` it is
the degree-`n` component of `∑_{j ≤ n} x^j / j!`. -/
noncomputable def gexp (x : R) : R :=
  G.ofComps fun n ↦ G.comp n (∑ j ∈ range (n + 1), ((j.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • x ^ j)

theorem comp_gexp (x : R) (n : ℕ) :
    G.comp n (G.gexp x) = G.comp n (∑ j ∈ range (n + 1), ((j.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • x ^ j) :=
  G.comp_ofComps _ n

/-- For `x` without constant term the truncation may be taken at any order `N ≥ n`. -/
theorem comp_gexp_of_le {x : R} (hx : G.comp 0 x = 0) {n N : ℕ} (h : n ≤ N) :
    G.comp n (G.gexp x) = G.comp n (∑ j ∈ range (N + 1), ((j.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • x ^ j) := by
  rw [comp_gexp]
  exact G.comp_sum_range_of_le _ (fun j ↦ G.vanishBelow_smul _ (G.vanishBelow_pow hx j)) h

theorem gexp_zero : G.gexp 0 = 1 := by
  refine G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
  rw [comp_gexp, Finset.sum_range_succ']
  simp

include G in
/-- `(x + y)^j / j! = ∑_{a ≤ j} (x^a / a!) (y^{j-a} / (j-a)!)` for commuting `x`, `y`. -/
theorem smul_add_pow {x y : R} (hxy : Commute x y) (j : ℕ) :
    ((j.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • (x + y) ^ j = ∑ a ∈ range (j + 1),
      (((a.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • x ^ a) * (((j - a).factorial : ℚ)⁻¹ • y ^ (j - a)) := by
  rw [hxy.add_pow, Finset.smul_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha ↦ ?_
  have ha' : a ≤ j := Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Finset.mem_range.mp ha)
  rw [G.smul_mul, G.mul_smul, smul_smul, ← nsmul_eq_mul', ← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℚ, smul_smul,
    Nat.cast_choose ℚ ha']
  congr 1
  have h1 : (j.factorial : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.factorial_ne_zero j)
  have h2 : (a.factorial : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.factorial_ne_zero a)
  have h3 : ((j - a).factorial : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.factorial_ne_zero _)
  field_simp

/-- **The exponential of a sum of commuting elements without constant term is the product of the
exponentials.** -/
theorem gexp_add {x y : R} (hx : G.comp 0 x = 0) (hy : G.comp 0 y = 0) (hxy : Commute x y) :
    G.gexp (x + y) = G.gexp x * G.gexp y := by
  have huv : ∀ a b, G.VanishBelow (a + b)
      ((((a.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • x ^ a) * (((b.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • y ^ b)) := fun a b ↦ by
    rw [G.smul_mul, G.mul_smul]
    exact G.vanishBelow_smul _ (G.vanishBelow_smul _
      (G.vanishBelow_mul (G.vanishBelow_pow hx a) (G.vanishBelow_pow hy b)))
  refine G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
  rw [G.mul_congr n _ (∑ a ∈ range (n + 1), ((a.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • x ^ a) _
      (∑ b ∈ range (n + 1), ((b.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • y ^ b)
      (fun p hp ↦ G.comp_gexp_of_le hx hp) (fun p hp ↦ G.comp_gexp_of_le hy hp),
    G.comp_sum_mul_sum _ _ huv n, comp_gexp]
  exact congrArg _ (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ ↦ G.smul_add_pow hxy j)

theorem gexp_mul_gexp_neg {x : R} (hx : G.comp 0 x = 0) : G.gexp x * G.gexp (-x) = 1 := by
  rw [← G.gexp_add hx (by rw [map_neg, hx, neg_zero]) (Commute.neg_right (Commute.refl x)),
    add_neg_cancel, gexp_zero]

theorem gexp_neg_mul_gexp {x : R} (hx : G.comp 0 x = 0) : G.gexp (-x) * G.gexp x = 1 := by
  rw [← G.gexp_add (by rw [map_neg, hx, neg_zero]) hx (Commute.neg_left (Commute.refl x)),
    neg_add_cancel, gexp_zero]

theorem isUnit_gexp {x : R} (hx : G.comp 0 x = 0) : IsUnit (G.gexp x) :=
  ⟨⟨G.gexp x, G.gexp (-x), G.gexp_mul_gexp_neg hx, G.gexp_neg_mul_gexp hx⟩, rfl⟩

/-! ### Degreewise rescaling -/

/-- Multiply the degree-`n` component by `w n`. -/
noncomputable def weight (w : ℕ → ℚ) (a : R) : R := G.ofComps fun n ↦ w n • G.comp n a

theorem comp_weight (w : ℕ → ℚ) (a : R) (n : ℕ) : G.comp n (G.weight w a) = w n • G.comp n a :=
  G.comp_ofComps _ n

theorem weight_add (w : ℕ → ℚ) (a b : R) : G.weight w (a + b) = G.weight w a + G.weight w b :=
  G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ by simp only [comp_weight, map_add, smul_add]

theorem weight_zero (w : ℕ → ℚ) : G.weight w (0 : R) = 0 :=
  G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ by rw [comp_weight, map_zero, smul_zero]

theorem weight_neg (w : ℕ → ℚ) (a : R) : G.weight w (-a) = -G.weight w a :=
  G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ by rw [map_neg, comp_weight, comp_weight, map_neg, smul_neg]

theorem weight_one (a : R) : G.weight (fun _ ↦ 1) a = a :=
  G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ by rw [comp_weight, one_smul]

/-- The Cauchy product formula for rescaled factors. -/
theorem comp_weight_mul_weight (w w' : ℕ → ℚ) (a b : R) (n : ℕ) :
    G.comp n (G.weight w a * G.weight w' b) = ∑ p ∈ range (n + 1), (w p * w' (n - p)) •
      G.comp n (G.single p (G.comp p a) * G.single (n - p) (G.comp (n - p) b)) := by
  rw [comp_mul]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ ↦ ?_
  rw [comp_weight, comp_weight, single_smul, single_smul, G.smul_mul, G.mul_smul, smul_smul,
    map_smul]

/-- The Cauchy product formula for rescaled factors, indexed by the degree of the second one. -/
theorem comp_weight_mul_weight_rev (w w' : ℕ → ℚ) (a b : R) (n : ℕ) :
    G.comp n (G.weight w' b * G.weight w a) = ∑ p ∈ range (n + 1), (w' (n - p) * w p) •
      G.comp n (G.single (n - p) (G.comp (n - p) b) * G.single p (G.comp p a)) := by
  rw [comp_mul_rev]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ ↦ ?_
  rw [comp_weight, comp_weight, single_smul, single_smul, G.smul_mul, G.mul_smul, smul_smul,
    map_smul]

/-- A family of vectors killed by a square `ℚ`-matrix with nonzero determinant vanishes. -/
theorem eq_zero_of_sum_smul_eq_zero {k : ℕ} {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module ℚ N]
    (A : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℚ) (hA : A.det ≠ 0) (v : Fin k → N)
    (h : ∀ i, ∑ p, A i p • v p = 0) (q : Fin k) : v q = 0 := by
  have hBA : A⁻¹ * A = 1 := Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul A (isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hA)
  calc v q = ∑ p, (A⁻¹ * A) q p • v p := by
          rw [hBA]; simp [Matrix.one_apply]
    _ = ∑ i, A⁻¹ q i • ∑ p, A i p • v p := by
          simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, Finset.sum_smul, Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul]
          exact Finset.sum_comm
    _ = 0 := by simp [h]

/-- **Commutation from scalings.** If the rescalings `(2^{i n} c_n)_n` of `c` all commute with
`c'` (for every `i`), then every degreewise rescaling of `c` commutes with every degreewise
rescaling of `c'`: the homogeneous components of `c` and `c'` commute pairwise, by a Vandermonde
argument in each degree. -/
theorem commute_weight_of_commute_scaling {c c' : R}
    (h : ∀ i : ℕ, Commute (G.weight (fun n ↦ (2 : ℚ) ^ (i * n)) c) c') (w w' : ℕ → ℚ) :
    Commute (G.weight w c) (G.weight w' c') := by
  show G.weight w c * G.weight w' c' = G.weight w' c' * G.weight w c
  refine G.ext _ _ fun m ↦ ?_
  have key : ∀ i : ℕ, ∑ p ∈ range (m + 1), ((2 : ℚ) ^ (i * p)) •
      (G.comp m (G.single p (G.comp p c) * G.single (m - p) (G.comp (m - p) c')) -
        G.comp m (G.single (m - p) (G.comp (m - p) c') * G.single p (G.comp p c))) = 0 := by
    intro i
    have e := congrArg (G.comp m) (h i).eq
    rw [← G.weight_one c', G.comp_weight_mul_weight, G.comp_weight_mul_weight_rev] at e
    simp only [mul_one, one_mul] at e
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ ↦ smul_sub _ _ _, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, e, sub_self]
  have hXY : ∀ p ≤ m,
      G.comp m (G.single p (G.comp p c) * G.single (m - p) (G.comp (m - p) c')) =
        G.comp m (G.single (m - p) (G.comp (m - p) c') * G.single p (G.comp p c)) := by
    intro p hp
    have hinj : Function.Injective fun q : Fin (m + 1) ↦ (2 : ℚ) ^ (q : ℕ) :=
      (pow_right_injective₀ (by norm_num) (by norm_num)).comp Fin.val_injective
    have hdet : (Matrix.transpose
        (Matrix.vandermonde fun q : Fin (m + 1) ↦ (2 : ℚ) ^ (q : ℕ))).det ≠ 0 := by
      rw [Matrix.det_transpose]
      exact Matrix.det_vandermonde_ne_zero_iff.mpr hinj
    refine sub_eq_zero.mp (eq_zero_of_sum_smul_eq_zero _ hdet
      (fun q : Fin (m + 1) ↦
        G.comp m (G.single q (G.comp q c) * G.single (m - q) (G.comp (m - q) c')) -
          G.comp m (G.single (m - q) (G.comp (m - q) c') * G.single q (G.comp q c)))
      (fun i ↦ ?_) ⟨p, by omega⟩)
    have e := key i
    rw [← Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range] at e
    simp only [Matrix.transpose_apply, Matrix.vandermonde_apply, ← pow_mul]
    simpa only [mul_comm] using e
  rw [G.comp_weight_mul_weight, G.comp_weight_mul_weight_rev]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p hp ↦ ?_
  rw [hXY p (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Finset.mem_range.mp hp)), mul_comm (w p)]

/-! ### Power series evaluated at an element without constant term -/

/-- The value `∑_j F_j h^j` of a power series at `h`, meaningful when `h` has no constant term:
in degree `n` it is the degree-`n` component of `∑_{j ≤ n} F_j h^j`. -/
noncomputable def ev (h : R) (F : ℚ⟦X⟧) : R :=
  G.ofComps fun n ↦ G.comp n (∑ j ∈ range (n + 1), (coeff j F) • h ^ j)

theorem comp_ev (h : R) (F : ℚ⟦X⟧) (n : ℕ) :
    G.comp n (G.ev h F) = G.comp n (∑ j ∈ range (n + 1), (coeff j F) • h ^ j) :=
  G.comp_ofComps _ n

/-- For `h` without constant term the truncation may be taken at any order `N ≥ n`. -/
theorem comp_ev_of_le {h : R} (hh : G.comp 0 h = 0) (F : ℚ⟦X⟧) {n N : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ N) :
    G.comp n (G.ev h F) = G.comp n (∑ j ∈ range (N + 1), (coeff j F) • h ^ j) := by
  rw [comp_ev]
  exact G.comp_sum_range_of_le _ (fun j ↦ G.vanishBelow_smul _ (G.vanishBelow_pow hh j)) hn

/-- For `h` homogeneous of degree one, the degree-`n` component of `F(h)` is `F_n h^n`. -/
theorem comp_ev_of_isHom {h : R} (hh : G.IsHom 1 h) (F : ℚ⟦X⟧) (n : ℕ) :
    G.comp n (G.ev h F) = (coeff n F) • G.comp n (h ^ n) := by
  rw [comp_ev, map_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single n]
  · exact map_smul _ _ _
  · intro j _ hj
    rw [map_smul, G.isHom_pow hh j n (Ne.symm hj), smul_zero]
  · intro hn
    exact absurd (Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_self n)) hn

/-- The degree-`n` component of `F(h)` only depends on the coefficients of `F` of degree `≤ n`. -/
theorem comp_ev_congr (h : R) {F F' : ℚ⟦X⟧} {n : ℕ} (hF : ∀ i ≤ n, coeff i F = coeff i F') :
    G.comp n (G.ev h F) = G.comp n (G.ev h F') := by
  rw [comp_ev, comp_ev]
  exact congrArg _ (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi ↦ by
    rw [hF i (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Finset.mem_range.mp hi))])

theorem ev_add (h : R) (F F' : ℚ⟦X⟧) : G.ev h (F + F') = G.ev h F + G.ev h F' :=
  G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ by simp only [map_add, comp_ev, add_smul, Finset.sum_add_distrib]

theorem ev_smul (h : R) (q : ℚ) (F : ℚ⟦X⟧) : G.ev h (q • F) = q • G.ev h F :=
  G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ by
    rw [map_smul, comp_ev, comp_ev, ← map_smul, Finset.smul_sum]
    simp only [map_smul, smul_eq_mul, smul_smul]

theorem ev_zero (h : R) : G.ev h 0 = 0 :=
  G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ by simp only [comp_ev, map_zero, zero_smul, Finset.sum_const_zero]

theorem ev_neg (h : R) (F : ℚ⟦X⟧) : G.ev h (-F) = -G.ev h F := by
  rw [← neg_one_smul ℚ F, ev_smul, neg_one_smul]

theorem ev_sub (h : R) (F F' : ℚ⟦X⟧) : G.ev h (F - F') = G.ev h F - G.ev h F' := by
  rw [sub_eq_add_neg, ev_add, ev_neg, ← sub_eq_add_neg]

theorem ev_sum (h : R) {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (F : ι → ℚ⟦X⟧) :
    G.ev h (∑ i ∈ s, F i) = ∑ i ∈ s, G.ev h (F i) := by
  classical
  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty => simp only [Finset.sum_empty, ev_zero]
  | insert a s ha ih => rw [Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha, ev_add, ih]

theorem ev_one {h : R} (hh : G.comp 0 h = 0) : G.ev h 1 = 1 := by
  -- `hh` belongs to the shared signature; this proof does not need it.
  have _ := hh
  refine G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
  rw [comp_ev, Finset.sum_eq_single 0]
  · rw [coeff_one, ite_eq_left rfl, one_smul, pow_zero]
  · intro j _ hj
    rw [coeff_one, ite_eq_right hj, zero_smul]
  · intro h0
    exact absurd (Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.succ_pos n)) h0

theorem ev_X {h : R} (hh : G.comp 0 h = 0) : G.ev h X = h :=
  G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ by
    rw [comp_ev]
    rcases n with _ | n
    · rw [Finset.sum_range_one, coeff_X, ite_eq_right zero_ne_one, zero_smul, map_zero, hh]
    · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single 1]
      · rw [coeff_X, ite_eq_left rfl, one_smul, pow_one]
      · intro j _ hj
        rw [coeff_X, ite_eq_right hj, zero_smul]
      · intro h1
        exact absurd (Finset.mem_range.mpr (by omega)) h1

/-- **Evaluation at an element without constant term is multiplicative.** -/
theorem ev_mul {h : R} (hh : G.comp 0 h = 0) (F F' : ℚ⟦X⟧) :
    G.ev h (F * F') = G.ev h F * G.ev h F' := by
  have huv : ∀ a b, G.VanishBelow (a + b) ((coeff a F • h ^ a) * (coeff b F' • h ^ b)) :=
    fun a b ↦ by
      rw [G.smul_mul, G.mul_smul, ← pow_add]
      exact G.vanishBelow_smul _ (G.vanishBelow_smul _ (G.vanishBelow_pow hh _))
  refine G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
  rw [G.mul_congr n _ (∑ j ∈ range (n + 1), (coeff j F) • h ^ j) _
      (∑ j ∈ range (n + 1), (coeff j F') • h ^ j)
      (fun p hp ↦ G.comp_ev_of_le hh F hp) (fun p hp ↦ G.comp_ev_of_le hh F' hp),
    G.comp_sum_mul_sum _ _ huv n, comp_ev]
  refine congrArg _ (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ ↦ ?_)
  rw [coeff_mul, Finset.Nat.sum_antidiagonal_eq_sum_range_succ (fun a b ↦ coeff a F * coeff b F'),
    Finset.sum_smul]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha ↦ ?_
  have ha' : a ≤ j := Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Finset.mem_range.mp ha)
  rw [G.smul_mul, G.mul_smul, smul_smul, ← pow_add, Nat.add_sub_cancel' ha']

theorem ev_pow {h : R} (hh : G.comp 0 h = 0) (F : ℚ⟦X⟧) (n : ℕ) :
    G.ev h (F ^ n) = G.ev h F ^ n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rw [pow_zero, pow_zero, G.ev_one hh]
  | succ n ih => rw [pow_succ, pow_succ, G.ev_mul hh, ih]

theorem comp_zero_ev {h : R} (hh : G.comp 0 h = 0) {F : ℚ⟦X⟧} (hF : constantCoeff F = 0) :
    G.comp 0 (G.ev h F) = 0 := by
  -- `hh` belongs to the shared signature; this proof does not need it.
  have _ := hh
  rw [comp_ev, Finset.sum_range_one, coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff_apply, hF, zero_smul, map_zero]

/-- Powers of a power series without constant term have no terms of low degree. -/
theorem coeff_pow_of_lt {L : ℚ⟦X⟧} (hL : constantCoeff L = 0) {i j : ℕ} (h : i < j) :
    coeff i (L ^ j) = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := X_dvd_iff.mpr hL
  rw [hg, mul_pow, coeff_X_pow_mul', ite_eq_right (by omega)]

/-- **`exp (L(h)) = T(h)`** whenever `T = exp L` coefficient by coefficient. -/
theorem gexp_ev {h : R} (hh : G.comp 0 h = 0) {L T : ℚ⟦X⟧} (hL : constantCoeff L = 0)
    (hT : ∀ n, coeff n T = coeff n (∑ j ∈ range (n + 1), ((j.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • L ^ j)) :
    G.gexp (G.ev h L) = G.ev h T := by
  refine G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
  rw [G.comp_ev_congr h (F := T) (F' := ∑ j ∈ range (n + 1), ((j.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • L ^ j)
      fun i hi ↦ ?_, comp_gexp, ev_sum]
  · simp only [ev_smul, G.ev_pow hh]
  · rw [hT i]
    simp only [map_sum, map_smul]
    refine Finset.sum_subset (Finset.range_subset_range.mpr (by omega)) fun j _ hj ↦ ?_
    rw [coeff_pow_of_lt hL (by simp only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] at hj; omega), smul_zero]

/-! ### The Todd operation -/

/-- The weights `n! · ℓ_n`, where `log (x / (1 - e^{-x})) = ∑ ℓ_n x^n`. -/
noncomputable def toddWeight (n : ℕ) : ℚ := (n.factorial : ℚ) * coeff n logTodd

/-- The Todd operation on a "Chern character" `c = (c_n)_n`: the exponential of
`∑_n n! · ℓ_n · c_n`. For `c = ch(E) = ∑_i e^{x_i}` this is `∏_i x_i / (1 - e^{-x_i})`. -/
noncomputable def toddOf (c : R) : R := G.gexp (G.weight toddWeight c)

theorem comp_zero_weight_toddWeight (c : R) : G.comp 0 (G.weight toddWeight c) = 0 := by
  rw [comp_weight, toddWeight, coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff_apply, constantCoeff_logTodd,
    mul_zero, zero_smul]

theorem toddOf_zero : G.toddOf 0 = 1 := by
  rw [toddOf, weight_zero, gexp_zero]

/-- **The Todd operation turns sums into products**, for summands whose rescalings commute. -/
theorem toddOf_add {c c' : R} (h : Commute (G.weight toddWeight c) (G.weight toddWeight c')) :
    G.toddOf (c + c') = G.toddOf c * G.toddOf c' := by
  rw [toddOf, weight_add]
  exact G.gexp_add (G.comp_zero_weight_toddWeight c) (G.comp_zero_weight_toddWeight c') h

theorem toddOf_mul_toddOf_neg (c : R) : G.toddOf c * G.toddOf (-c) = 1 := by
  rw [toddOf, toddOf, weight_neg]
  exact G.gexp_mul_gexp_neg (G.comp_zero_weight_toddWeight c)

theorem toddOf_neg_mul_toddOf (c : R) : G.toddOf (-c) * G.toddOf c = 1 := by
  rw [toddOf, toddOf, weight_neg]
  exact G.gexp_neg_mul_gexp (G.comp_zero_weight_toddWeight c)

theorem isUnit_toddOf (c : R) : IsUnit (G.toddOf c) :=
  G.isUnit_gexp (G.comp_zero_weight_toddWeight c)

/-- **The Todd operation on `e^h`** for `h` homogeneous of degree one is the Todd series at `h`:
`td(e^h) = h / (1 - e^{-h})`. -/
theorem toddOf_ev_exp {h : R} (hh : G.IsHom 1 h) :
    G.toddOf (G.ev h (exp ℚ)) = G.ev h toddSeries := by
  have hh0 : G.comp 0 h = 0 := hh 0 zero_ne_one
  have hw : G.weight toddWeight (G.ev h (exp ℚ)) = G.ev h logTodd := by
    refine G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
    rw [comp_weight, G.comp_ev_of_isHom hh, G.comp_ev_of_isHom hh, smul_smul, coeff_exp]
    congr 1
    have hn : (n.factorial : ℚ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.factorial_ne_zero n)
    simp only [toddWeight, Algebra.algebraMap_self, RingHom.id_apply]
    field_simp
  rw [toddOf, hw]
  exact G.gexp_ev hh0 constantCoeff_logTodd coeff_toddSeries_eq_coeff_sum_logTodd_pow

/-- **The rank-one Koszul identity**: `td(e^h) · (1 - e^{-h}) = h`. -/
theorem ev_toddSeries_mul_one_sub_ev_expNeg {h : R} (hh : G.comp 0 h = 0) :
    G.ev h toddSeries * (1 - G.ev h expNeg) = h := by
  rw [← G.ev_one hh, ← ev_sub, ← G.ev_mul hh, toddSeries_mul_one_sub_expNeg, G.ev_X hh]

end GradedComplete

end GRR

import Mathlib
import GRR.GradedExp

/-!
# Graded maps between graded-complete rings

A ring map `φ : R →+* R'` between graded-complete `ℚ`-algebras is *graded* (`GRR.IsGradedHom`) if
it acts component by component through `ℚ`-linear maps. Such a map commutes with the exponential
`gexp`, with degreewise rescaling `weight`, with evaluation of power series `ev`, and therefore
with the Todd operation `toddOf`. Pullback of Chow cohomology classes is of this kind.
-/

open PowerSeries Finset

universe u v u' v'

namespace GRR

namespace GradedComplete

variable {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Module ℚ R] (G : GRR.GradedComplete.{u, v} R)
  {R' : Type u'} [Ring R'] [Module ℚ R'] (G' : GRR.GradedComplete.{u', v'} R')

/-- A ring map between graded-complete rings is graded if it acts component by component through
`ℚ`-linear maps. -/
structure IsGradedHom (φ : R →+* R') : Prop where
  exists_comp : ∀ n, ∃ ψ : G.M n →ₗ[ℚ] G'.M n, ∀ a, G'.comp n (φ a) = ψ (G.comp n a)

variable {G G'} {φ : R →+* R'}

theorem IsGradedHom.map_smul (hφ : IsGradedHom G G' φ) (q : ℚ) (a : R) :
    φ (q • a) = q • φ a := by
  refine G'.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := hφ.exists_comp n
  rw [hψ, _root_.map_smul, _root_.map_smul, _root_.map_smul, hψ]

theorem IsGradedHom.map_gexp (hφ : IsGradedHom G G' φ) (x : R) :
    φ (G.gexp x) = G'.gexp (φ x) := by
  refine G'.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := hφ.exists_comp n
  rw [hψ, comp_gexp, comp_gexp, ← hψ, map_sum]
  simp only [hφ.map_smul, map_pow]

theorem IsGradedHom.map_weight (hφ : IsGradedHom G G' φ) (w : ℕ → ℚ) (a : R) :
    φ (G.weight w a) = G'.weight w (φ a) := by
  refine G'.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := hφ.exists_comp n
  rw [hψ, comp_weight, comp_weight, hψ, _root_.map_smul]

theorem IsGradedHom.map_ev (hφ : IsGradedHom G G' φ) (h : R) (F : ℚ⟦X⟧) :
    φ (G.ev h F) = G'.ev (φ h) F := by
  refine G'.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := hφ.exists_comp n
  rw [hψ, comp_ev, comp_ev, ← hψ, map_sum]
  simp only [hφ.map_smul, map_pow]

/-- A graded ring map commutes with the Todd operation. -/
theorem IsGradedHom.map_toddOf (hφ : IsGradedHom G G' φ) (c : R) :
    φ (G.toddOf c) = G'.toddOf (φ c) := by
  rw [toddOf, toddOf, hφ.map_gexp, hφ.map_weight]

theorem IsGradedHom.isHom (hφ : IsGradedHom G G' φ) {n : ℕ} {a : R} (ha : G.IsHom n a) :
    G'.IsHom n (φ a) := fun p hp ↦ by
  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := hφ.exists_comp p
  rw [hψ, ha p hp, map_zero]

end GradedComplete

end GRR

import Mathlib
import StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.RationalIntersection.ChernCharacterMultiplicative
import StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.RationalIntersection.SecondAdamsChernCharacter
import StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.ChernClassDerived.TwistFormula
import GRR.GradedExp

/-!
# The Todd class in `∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ`

Let `(S, δ)` be a base situation of Chow homology and `X` locally of finite type over `S`. The ring
`Stacks.Chow.RationalTotalChowClass C sX = ∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ` is graded-complete
(`GRR.chowGraded`), so the Todd operation of `GRR.GradedComplete` applies to the Chern character
`ch : K₀(Vect X) → ∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ` of Stacks: `GRR.toddClass C sX a = td(a)` is the exponential of
`∑_p p! ℓ_p ch_p(a)`, where `log (x / (1 - e^{-x})) = ∑ ℓ_p x^p`.

Main results: `toddClass_add` (multiplicativity, hence on short exact sequences
`toddClass_classOf_of_shortExact`), `isUnit_toddClass`, and for an invertible module `L`,
`ch_classOf_invertible : ch(L) = e^{c₁(L)}` and
`toddClass_classOf_invertible : td(L) = c₁(L) / (1 - e^{-c₁(L)})`.
-/

open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory Stacks.Chow
open scoped TensorProduct

universe u

namespace GRR

namespace GradedComplete

variable {R : Type*} [Ring R] [Module ℚ R] (G : GRR.GradedComplete R)

include G in
/-- A combination `∑_j c_j x^j` of powers of `x` commutes with whatever `x` commutes with. -/
theorem commute_sum_smul_pow {x y : R} (h : Commute x y) (c : ℕ → ℚ) (N : ℕ) :
    Commute (∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, c j • x ^ j) y := by
  refine Commute.sum_left _ _ _ fun j _ ↦ ?_
  change c j • x ^ j * y = y * (c j • x ^ j)
  rw [G.smul_mul, G.mul_smul, (h.pow_left j).eq]

/-- **`exp x` commutes with whatever `x` commutes with**, for `x` without constant term: up to
degree `n` it agrees with the polynomial `∑_{j ≤ n} x^j / j!`. -/
theorem commute_gexp_left {x y : R} (hx : G.comp 0 x = 0) (h : Commute x y) :
    Commute (G.gexp x) y := by
  change G.gexp x * y = y * G.gexp x
  refine G.ext _ _ fun n ↦ ?_
  rw [G.mul_congr n (G.gexp x) (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), ((j.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹) • x ^ j) y y
      (fun p hp ↦ G.comp_gexp_of_le hx hp) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl),
    (G.commute_sum_smul_pow h (fun j ↦ ((j.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹)) (n + 1)).eq,
    G.mul_congr n y y _ (G.gexp x) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) (fun p hp ↦ (G.comp_gexp_of_le hx hp).symm)]

theorem commute_gexp_right {x y : R} (hx : G.comp 0 x = 0) (h : Commute y x) :
    Commute y (G.gexp x) :=
  (G.commute_gexp_left hx h.symm).symm

end GradedComplete

variable (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]

/-- A product of classes of degrees `i` and `j` in `ℚ ⊗ ∏_q A^q(X)` has no component of degree
other than `i + j`. -/
theorem rationalComponent_rationalSingle_mul_rationalSingle {i j p : ℕ} (hp : p ≠ i + j)
    (x : rationalChowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX i)
    (y : rationalChowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX j) :
    RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent p
      (RationalTotalChowClass.rationalSingle i x * RationalTotalChowClass.rationalSingle j y) =
        0 := by
  induction x using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | add x x' hx hx' => rw [map_add, add_mul, map_add, hx, hx', add_zero]
  | tmul r c =>
    induction y using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | add y y' hy hy' => rw [map_add, mul_add, map_add, hy, hy', add_zero]
    | tmul r' d =>
      rw [RationalTotalChowClass.rationalSingle_tmul, RationalTotalChowClass.rationalSingle_tmul,
        Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent_tmul,
        ((TotalChowClass.isHomogeneous_single i c).mul
          (TotalChowClass.isHomogeneous_single j d)) p hp, TensorProduct.tmul_zero]

/-- A family concentrated in degree `i` is lifted to `ℚ ⊗ ∏_q A^q(X)` by its degree-`i`
component, in every degree. -/
theorem rationalComponent_rationalSingle_of_isHom {i : ℕ} {a : RationalTotalChowClass C sX}
    (ha : ∀ p, p ≠ i → a p = 0) (k : ℕ) :
    RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent k (RationalTotalChowClass.rationalSingle i (a i)) =
      a k := by
  rcases eq_or_ne k i with rfl | hk
  · exact RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent_rationalSingle_self k (a k)
  · rw [RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent_rationalSingle_of_ne hk, ha k hk]

/-- **`∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ` is graded-complete**: its elements are the families of components
`a_p ∈ A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ`, multiplied by the Cauchy product. -/
noncomputable def chowGraded : GradedComplete.{u + 1, u + 1} (RationalTotalChowClass C sX) where
  M := fun n ↦ rationalChowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (n : ℤ)
  comp := fun n ↦
    { toFun := fun a ↦ a n
      map_add' := fun _ _ ↦ rfl
      map_smul' := fun _ _ ↦ rfl }
  ofComps := fun f ↦ f
  comp_ofComps := fun _ _ ↦ rfl
  ext := fun _ _ h ↦ RationalTotalChowClass.ext h
  smul_mul := fun q a b ↦ RationalTotalChowClass.ext fun m ↦ by
    rw [RationalTotalChowClass.smul_apply, RationalTotalChowClass.mul_apply,
      RationalTotalChowClass.mul_apply, map_smul, smul_mul_assoc, map_smul]
  mul_smul := fun q a b ↦ RationalTotalChowClass.ext fun m ↦ by
    rw [RationalTotalChowClass.smul_apply, RationalTotalChowClass.mul_apply,
      RationalTotalChowClass.mul_apply, map_smul, mul_smul_comm, map_smul]
  mul_congr := fun n a a' b b' ha hb ↦
    RationalTotalChowClass.mul_apply_eq
      (fun k hk ↦ (RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent_truncatedLift n a' hk).trans
        (ha k hk).symm)
      (fun k hk ↦ (RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent_truncatedLift n b' hk).trans
        (hb k hk).symm)
  mul_hom := fun i j a b ha hb p hp ↦ by
    change (a * b) p = 0
    rw [RationalTotalChowClass.mul_apply_eq
      (fun k _ ↦ rationalComponent_rationalSingle_of_isHom C sX (a := a) ha k)
      (fun k _ ↦ rationalComponent_rationalSingle_of_isHom C sX (a := b) hb k)]
    exact rationalComponent_rationalSingle_mul_rationalSingle C sX hp _ _
  comp_one := fun p hp ↦ by
    change (1 : RationalTotalChowClass C sX) p = 0
    rw [RationalTotalChowClass.one_apply, Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def,
      RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent_tmul, TotalChowClass.one_apply_of_ne hp,
      TensorProduct.tmul_zero]

@[simp]
theorem chowGraded_comp_apply (n : ℕ) (a : RationalTotalChowClass C sX) :
    (chowGraded C sX).comp n a = a n := rfl

/-- The degreewise rescaling, read on components. -/
theorem chowGraded_weight_apply (w : ℕ → ℚ) (c : RationalTotalChowClass C sX) (n : ℕ) :
    (chowGraded C sX).weight w c n = w n • c n :=
  (chowGraded C sX).comp_weight w c n

/-- The Chern character `ch : K₀(Vect X) → ∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ` of Stacks, as a ring map. -/
noncomputable abbrev ch : VectorBundleKZero X →+* RationalTotalChowClass C sX :=
  rationalTotalChernCharacterRingHom C sX

theorem ch_apply (a : VectorBundleKZero X) (n : ℕ) :
    ch C sX a n = chernCharacterVectorBundle C sX a n := rfl

/-- **The Todd class** `td(a) ∈ ∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ` of a class `a ∈ K₀(Vect X)`: the exponential of
`∑_p p! ℓ_p ch_p(a)`, where `log (x / (1 - e^{-x})) = ∑ ℓ_p x^p`. For `a = [E]` with Chern roots
`x_i` it is `∏_i x_i / (1 - e^{-x_i})`. -/
noncomputable def toddClass (a : VectorBundleKZero X) : RationalTotalChowClass C sX :=
  (chowGraded C sX).toddOf (ch C sX a)

/-- `ch((ψ²)^i a)` is `ch(a)` rescaled by `2^{i p}` in degree `p` (Stacks 0FEN, iterated). -/
theorem ch_secondAdams_iterate (i : ℕ) (a : VectorBundleKZero X) :
    ch C sX ((VectorBundleKZero.secondAdamsRingHom (VectorBundleKZero.squarePowersData X))^[i] a) =
      (chowGraded C sX).weight (fun n ↦ (2 : ℚ) ^ (i * n)) (ch C sX a) := by
  induction i with
  | zero =>
    refine RationalTotalChowClass.ext fun n ↦ ?_
    rw [chowGraded_weight_apply, Function.iterate_zero_apply, zero_mul, pow_zero, one_smul]
  | succ i ih =>
    refine RationalTotalChowClass.ext fun n ↦ ?_
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ch_apply, chernCharacterVectorBundle_secondAdams,
      ← ch_apply, ih, chowGraded_weight_apply, chowGraded_weight_apply, smul_smul, ← pow_add,
      add_mul, one_mul, add_comm]

/-- The degreewise rescalings of two Chern characters commute (the Chern character is a ring map
out of a commutative ring and `ch_p(ψ² a) = 2^p ch_p(a)`). -/
theorem commute_weight_ch (w w' : ℕ → ℚ) (a b : VectorBundleKZero X) :
    Commute ((chowGraded C sX).weight w (ch C sX a)) ((chowGraded C sX).weight w' (ch C sX b)) := by
  refine (chowGraded C sX).commute_weight_of_commute_scaling (fun i ↦ ?_) w w'
  rw [← ch_secondAdams_iterate]
  exact (Commute.all _ _).map (ch C sX)

theorem toddClass_zero : toddClass C sX 0 = 1 := by
  rw [toddClass, map_zero, GradedComplete.toddOf_zero]

/-- **The Todd class is multiplicative**: `td(a + b) = td(a) · td(b)`. -/
theorem toddClass_add (a b : VectorBundleKZero X) :
    toddClass C sX (a + b) = toddClass C sX a * toddClass C sX b := by
  simp only [toddClass, map_add]
  exact (chowGraded C sX).toddOf_add (commute_weight_ch C sX _ _ a b)

theorem toddClass_mul_toddClass_neg (a : VectorBundleKZero X) :
    toddClass C sX a * toddClass C sX (-a) = 1 := by
  simp only [toddClass, map_neg]
  exact (chowGraded C sX).toddOf_mul_toddOf_neg _

theorem toddClass_neg_mul_toddClass (a : VectorBundleKZero X) :
    toddClass C sX (-a) * toddClass C sX a = 1 := by
  simp only [toddClass, map_neg]
  exact (chowGraded C sX).toddOf_neg_mul_toddOf _

theorem isUnit_toddClass (a : VectorBundleKZero X) : IsUnit (toddClass C sX a) :=
  (chowGraded C sX).isUnit_toddOf _

theorem commute_toddClass_ch (a b : VectorBundleKZero X) :
    Commute (toddClass C sX a) (ch C sX b) := by
  have h := commute_weight_ch C sX GradedComplete.toddWeight (fun _ ↦ 1) a b
  rw [GradedComplete.weight_one] at h
  exact (chowGraded C sX).commute_gexp_left ((chowGraded C sX).comp_zero_weight_toddWeight _) h

theorem commute_toddClass_toddClass (a b : VectorBundleKZero X) :
    Commute (toddClass C sX a) (toddClass C sX b) := by
  have h0 := (chowGraded C sX).comp_zero_weight_toddWeight
  exact (chowGraded C sX).commute_gexp_left (h0 _)
    ((chowGraded C sX).commute_gexp_right (h0 _) (commute_weight_ch C sX _ _ a b))

/-- **Multiplicativity of the Todd class on short exact sequences** of finite locally free
modules: `td(E) = td(E') · td(E'')` for `0 → E' → E → E'' → 0`. -/
theorem toddClass_classOf_of_shortExact (S : ShortComplex X.Modules) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    [h₁ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} S.X₁]
    [h₃ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} S.X₃] :
    toddClass C sX (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X S.X₂) =
      toddClass C sX (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X S.X₁) *
        toddClass C sX (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X S.X₃) := by
  have h₂ := GenuineChern.isFiniteLocallyFree_of_shortExact S hS h₁ h₃
  have := hS.mono_f
  have := hS.epi_g
  rw [VectorBundleKZero.classOf_shortExact S.f S.g S.zero h₁ h₂ h₃ hS.exact, toddClass_add]

section Invertible

variable (L : X.Modules)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]

/-- The first Chern class `c₁(L)` of an invertible module, in `∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ` (in degree one). -/
noncomputable def firstChernQ : RationalTotalChowClass C sX :=
  RationalTotalChowClass.ofTotalChowClass (TotalChowClass.firstChernTotal C sX L)

theorem isHom_firstChernQ : (chowGraded C sX).IsHom 1 (firstChernQ C sX L) := fun p hp ↦
  show (1 : ℚ) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] TotalChowClass.firstChernTotal C sX L p = 0 by
    rw [TotalChowClass.firstChernTotal_apply_of_ne C sX L hp, TensorProduct.tmul_zero]

/-- **`ch(L) = e^{c₁(L)}`** for an invertible module `L`. -/
theorem ch_classOf_invertible :
    ch C sX (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X L) =
      (chowGraded C sX).ev (firstChernQ C sX L) (PowerSeries.exp ℚ) := by
  have h1 : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} L 1 :=
    isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one_of_isInvertible L
  have hF : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} L :=
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.isFiniteLocallyFree L 1
  refine RationalTotalChowClass.ext fun n ↦ ?_
  have hev : (chowGraded C sX).ev (firstChernQ C sX L) (PowerSeries.exp ℚ) n =
      PowerSeries.coeff n (PowerSeries.exp ℚ) • ((firstChernQ C sX L ^ n) n :
        rationalChowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX n) :=
    (chowGraded C sX).comp_ev_of_isHom (isHom_firstChernQ C sX L) (PowerSeries.exp ℚ) n
  rw [hev, ch_apply, chernCharacterVectorBundle_apply, powerSumKHom_classOf,
    powerSumOfFiniteLocallyFree_eq_powerSumTotal C sX L 1, powerSumTotal_of_rank_one,
    ← TotalChowClass.firstChernTotal_eq_homComponent_totalChern, firstChernQ,
    ← map_pow RationalTotalChowClass.ofTotalChowClass,
    RationalTotalChowClass.ofTotalChowClass_apply, PowerSeries.coeff_exp, TensorProduct.smul_tmul',
    Algebra.algebraMap_self_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_one, one_div]

/-- **`td(L) = c₁(L) / (1 - e^{-c₁(L)})`** for an invertible module `L`: the Todd class of a line
bundle is the Todd power series evaluated at its first Chern class. -/
theorem toddClass_classOf_invertible :
    toddClass C sX (VectorBundleKZero.classOf X L) =
      (chowGraded C sX).ev (firstChernQ C sX L) toddSeries := by
  rw [toddClass, ch_classOf_invertible,
    (chowGraded C sX).toddOf_ev_exp (isHom_firstChernQ C sX L)]

end Invertible

end GRR

import Mathlib
import StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.RationalIntersection.GysinChernCharacter
import StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.ChernClassDerived.TotalClassRestriction
import GRR.GradedHom
import GRR.ToddClass

/-!
# Pullback of rational Chow cohomology classes, and the projection formula

For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes locally of finite type over the base `(S, δ)`, restriction of
bivariant classes gives a graded ring map

  `f^* : ∏_p A^p(Y) ⊗ ℚ ⟶ ∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ`  (`GRR.pullbackAQ`).

It commutes with the Chern character and with the Todd class: `f^* ch(a) = ch(f^* a)`,
`f^* td(a) = td(f^* a)` for `a ∈ K₀(Vect Y)`. For proper `f` the cap action satisfies the
projection formula `f_* (f^* c ∩ γ) = c ∩ f_* γ` on `CH_* ⊗ ℚ`.
-/

open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory Stacks.Chow
open scoped TensorProduct

universe u

namespace GRR

variable (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
  (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY]

section Lifts

variable (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX)

/-- Restriction `ℚ ⊗ ∏_p A^p(Y) ⟶ ℚ ⊗ ∏_p A^p(X)`, the base change of the ring map
`TotalChowClass.res`. -/
noncomputable def resQ : ℚ ⊗[ℤ] TotalChowClass C sY →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ ⊗[ℤ] TotalChowClass C sX :=
  (TotalChowClass.res f hf).toAddMonoidHom.toIntLinearMap.baseChange ℚ

theorem resQ_tmul (r : ℚ) (c : TotalChowClass C sY) :
    resQ C sX sY f hf (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] c) = r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] TotalChowClass.res f hf c :=
  rfl

theorem resQ_one : resQ C sX sY f hf 1 = 1 := by
  rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def, resQ_tmul, map_one, ← Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]

theorem resQ_mul (x y : ℚ ⊗[ℤ] TotalChowClass C sY) :
    resQ C sX sY f hf (x * y) = resQ C sX sY f hf x * resQ C sX sY f hf y := by
  induction x using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | add x x' hx hx' => rw [add_mul, map_add, hx, hx', map_add, add_mul]
  | tmul r c =>
    induction y using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | add y y' hy hy' => rw [mul_add, map_add, hy, hy', map_add, mul_add]
    | tmul r' d =>
      rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, resQ_tmul, resQ_tmul, resQ_tmul, map_mul,
        Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul]

/-- Components commute with restriction. -/
theorem rationalComponent_resQ (p : ℕ) (x : ℚ ⊗[ℤ] TotalChowClass C sY) :
    RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent p (resQ C sX sY f hf x) =
      ((chowCohomologyRestrictionOfEq C sX sY hf (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) p).toIntLinearMap.baseChange ℚ)
        (RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent p x) := by
  induction x using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | add x x' hx hx' => rw [map_add, map_add, hx, hx', map_add, map_add]
  | tmul r c =>
    rw [resQ_tmul, RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent_tmul,
      RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent_tmul, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul,
      AddMonoidHom.coe_toIntLinearMap, TotalChowClass.res_apply_eq_chowCohomologyRestrictionOfEq]

/-- Componentwise restriction `∏_p A^p(Y) ⊗ ℚ ⟶ ∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ`, as a `ℚ`-linear map. -/
noncomputable def pullbackAQLinear :
    RationalTotalChowClass C sY →ₗ[ℚ] RationalTotalChowClass C sX where
  toFun c p := ((chowCohomologyRestrictionOfEq C sX sY hf (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
    (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) p).toIntLinearMap.baseChange ℚ) (c p)
  map_add' a b := RationalTotalChowClass.ext fun p ↦ map_add _ (a p) (b p)
  map_smul' r a := RationalTotalChowClass.ext fun p ↦ map_smul _ r (a p)

theorem pullbackAQLinear_apply (c : RationalTotalChowClass C sY) (p : ℕ) :
    pullbackAQLinear C sX sY f hf c p =
      ((chowCohomologyRestrictionOfEq C sX sY hf (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) p).toIntLinearMap.baseChange ℚ)
        (c p) :=
  rfl

/-- Restriction of a lift below degree `m` is a lift below degree `m` of the restriction. -/
theorem rationalComponent_resQ_truncatedLift (m : ℕ) (a : RationalTotalChowClass C sY) {k : ℕ}
    (hk : k ≤ m) :
    RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent k
        (resQ C sX sY f hf (RationalTotalChowClass.truncatedLift m a)) =
      pullbackAQLinear C sX sY f hf a k := by
  rw [rationalComponent_resQ, RationalTotalChowClass.rationalComponent_truncatedLift m a hk,
    pullbackAQLinear_apply]

theorem pullbackAQLinear_one : pullbackAQLinear C sX sY f hf 1 = 1 :=
  RationalTotalChowClass.ext fun p ↦ by
    rw [pullbackAQLinear_apply, RationalTotalChowClass.one_apply, RationalTotalChowClass.one_apply,
      ← rationalComponent_resQ, resQ_one]

theorem pullbackAQLinear_mul (a b : RationalTotalChowClass C sY) :
    pullbackAQLinear C sX sY f hf (a * b) =
      pullbackAQLinear C sX sY f hf a * pullbackAQLinear C sX sY f hf b :=
  RationalTotalChowClass.ext fun m ↦ by
    rw [pullbackAQLinear_apply, RationalTotalChowClass.mul_apply a b m, ← rationalComponent_resQ,
      resQ_mul, RationalTotalChowClass.mul_apply_eq
        (fun k hk ↦ rationalComponent_resQ_truncatedLift C sX sY f hf m a hk)
        (fun k hk ↦ rationalComponent_resQ_truncatedLift C sX sY f hf m b hk)]

end Lifts

/-- **Pullback of rational Chow cohomology classes** along `f : X ⟶ Y`, as a ring map
`∏_p A^p(Y) ⊗ ℚ ⟶ ∏_p A^p(X) ⊗ ℚ`: in each degree it is the restriction of bivariant classes of
Stacks, tensored with `ℚ`. -/
noncomputable def pullbackAQ (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) :
    RationalTotalChowClass C sY →+* RationalTotalChowClass C sX where
  toFun := pullbackAQLinear C sX sY f hf
  map_one' := pullbackAQLinear_one C sX sY f hf
  map_mul' := pullbackAQLinear_mul C sX sY f hf
  map_zero' := map_zero _
  map_add' := map_add _

variable (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hf : f ≫ sY = sX)

/-- The degree-`p` component of a pullback is the restriction of the degree-`p` component. -/
theorem pullbackAQ_apply (c : RationalTotalChowClass C sY) (p : ℕ) :
    pullbackAQ C sX sY f hf c p =
      ((chowCohomologyRestrictionOfEq C sX sY hf (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) p).toIntLinearMap.baseChange ℚ)
        (c p) :=
  rfl

/-- Pullback is a graded ring map. -/
theorem isGradedHom_pullbackAQ :
    GradedComplete.IsGradedHom (chowGraded C sY) (chowGraded C sX) (pullbackAQ C sX sY f hf) :=
  ⟨fun n ↦ ⟨(chowCohomologyRestrictionOfEq C sX sY hf (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
